picks.title: A gut-brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila.
picks.abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut-brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop-a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut-brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states.

picks.title: AI-based digital pathology defines spatial border ecosystems in triple-negative breast cancer.
picks.abstract: The invasive tumor border in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is currently poorly understood. We integrated digital pathology and spatial multi-omics to define border ecosystems in TNBC. AI-based digital pathology identified five border ecosystems, three associated with prognosis. Spatial multi-omics analyses further resolved the spatial niche, molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance of these ecosystems. Immune-infiltrated borders contain a triadic immune niche associated with favorable prognosis and immunotherapy sensitivity. Tumor-stroma borders harbor a MIF+ fibroblast exclusion niche that blocks immune infiltration and suppresses T cells function, predicting poor prognosis. Tumor-adipose borders, featured an FLT1+ endothelial niche, promote hypoxia, vascular leakage, and tumor dissemination. Targeting this niche inhibits tumor progression. Collectively, these findings establish a spatial resource that might enable border-directed therapeutic strategies in TNBC.

picks.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis.
picks.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

picks.title: Modular mRNA-encoded helper proteins enhance DNA delivery.
picks.abstract: DNA delivery is limited by inefficient nuclear translocation and restrictive intracellular environments. Here we present mRNA-enhanced DNA delivery (MEND), a system that codelivers mRNA-encoded helper proteins to actively prime cells for enhanced DNA processing. We demonstrate three classes of MEND proteins: DNA translocators, host modulators and immune dampeners. MEND's modular framework boosts transgene expression across various delivery vehicles and DNA formats in vitro and in vivo with LNP delivery.

picks.title: Izalontamab brengitecan versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous non-small-cell lung cancer after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PANKU-Lung01): a multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial in China.

sections.objective: Izalontamab brengitecan (iza-bren) is a first-in-class bispecific antibody-drug conjugate targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 (HER3) and has shown antitumour activity in EGFR-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We compared iza-bren with platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).
sections.methods: In this multicentre, randomised, open-label, phase 3 trial (PANKU-Lung01) conducted at 73 sites in China, eligible participants had EGFR-mutated locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC, disease progression after third-generation EGFR TKIs, and had received no previous chemotherapy for advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive iza-bren (2·5 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle) or pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for four to six cycles, with pemetrexed maintenance permitted in participants without progression. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). The primary analysis included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of study treatment (modified intention-to-treat population). We report the prespecified final progression-free survival and interim overall survival analyses. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06382116.
sections.results: Between May 22, 2024, and Sept 1, 2025, we screened 654 participants. After 222 (34%) were excluded, 432 (66%) participants were randomly assigned to iza-bren (n=217 [50%]) or chemotherapy (n=215 [50%]); 422 (98%) received study treatment (216 [51%] in the iza-bren group and 206 [49%] in the chemotherapy group) and comprised the modified intention-to-treat population. At the data cutoff (July 15, 2026; median follow-up for progression-free survival 14·6 months [95% CI 12·9-16·7] in the iza-bren group vs 15·2 months [11·2-18·2] in the chemotherapy group), median BICR-assessed progression-free survival was 11·1 months (9·2-12·7) with iza-bren versus 5·7 months (5·5-5·9) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0·40 [95% CI 0·31-0·51]; one-sided p<0·0001). Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 170 (79%) of 216 participants in the iza-bren group and 128 (62%) of 206 in the chemotherapy group (predominantly haematological); treatment-related adverse events led to permanent discontinuation of at least one study-treatment component in four (2%) participants in each group and treatment-related deaths occurred in one participant in each group. Treatment-related interstitial lung disease occurred in two (1%) participants in the iza-bren group and none in the chemotherapy group.
sections.conclusion: In participants with EGFR-mutated advanced non-squamous NSCLC after progression on third-generation EGFR TKIs, iza-bren significantly prolonged progression-free survival, although treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse were more frequent than with chemotherapy. To our knowledge, these findings provide the first phase 3 evidence for a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate and support iza-bren as a potential treatment option in this population.

picks.title: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials.

sections.objective: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis.
sections.methods: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting.
sections.results: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns.
sections.conclusion: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis.

picks.title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1-Negative Advanced NSCLC.

sections.objective: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis.
sections.results: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

picks.title: The blood-brain barrier imports diverse neuroprotective proteins through pathways impaired early in Alzheimer's disease models.
picks.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) has been defined primarily by what it excludes, yet the scale and function of physiological blood-to-brain protein transport remain largely unknown. Using bioorthogonal proteomics, we find that the healthy BBB samples 191 plasma proteins and permits 92 into the brain parenchyma. Enriched for carrier and metabolic functions, these proteins home to distinct brain cell types, such as apolipoprotein A1 (APOA1) to astrocytes and alpha-1 antitrypsin (SERPINA1) to microglia. This cell-type tropism relies on a BBB-parenchyma receptor hand-off: APOA1 crosses the BBB via SR-B1 and engages astrocytic ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1), a key Alzheimer's risk gene, driving cholesterol efflux that supports synapse integrity. Unlike LPS-induced nonspecific leakage, early-stage 5xFAD mice show selective BBB transport remodeling, with reduced APOA1 and increased SERPINA1 uptake. Hepatic APOA1 overexpression restores APOA1 in the 5xFAD brain, rescuing astrocytic, synaptic, and behavioral deficits. These findings recast the BBB as a selective interface that recruits neuroprotective circulatory proteins for brain health.

items.title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs.
items.abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

items.title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing.
items.abstract: Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude (M) <3] are commonly modeled as simple circular ruptures, leaving the fine-scale spatial attributes of rupture dynamics unresolved. We used near-source distributed acoustic sensing to image the millisecond-scale rupture of an M 2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California's Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the M 2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

items.title: The original researchers would like a wordResearch: A Manifesto Peter N. Miller Princeton University Press, 2026. 256 pp.
items.abstract: Humanists pioneered scholarly research, but scientists get all the credit, argues a historian.

items.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake.
items.abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude (Mw) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four Mw 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

items.title: Deception in motion.
items.abstract: Group motion may have evolved because it distorts what predators perceive.

items.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023-2024 record warming.
items.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023-2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean-atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

items.title: A tryptophan cation radical determines radical transfer kinetics and catalytic rate in a ribonucleotide reductase.
items.abstract: Ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) is the sole enzyme responsible for de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis for DNA replication and repair. In the Escherichia coli class Ia RNR, a radical must traverse 32 angstroms along a pathway composed of amino acids spanning β and α subunits to complete each turnover. By incorporating unnatural amino acids to alter reduction potentials of pathway tyrosine residues, we (i) perturb the rates of radical transfer and show that they match the rates of deoxynucleotide production and (ii) directly observe a tryptophan cation radical (W48+•) as a kinetically competent pathway intermediate. Together, these results establish that radical transfer through W48 in α2β2 is the rate-limiting process, which controls the enzymatic activity of E. coli RNR.

items.title: The absent-minded physicist who bested them allThe Man Who Broke Reality Philip Ball University of Chicago Press, 2026. 512 pp.
items.abstract: Despite his reputation for mumbling and bumbling, Niels Bohr's radical insights were unmatched.

items.title: Advancing undergraduates' skills for communicating science with the public.
items.abstract: Interdisciplinary communication and education research can help the next generation of science communicators address cultural conflicts.

items.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up.
items.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

items.title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels.
items.abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub-one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

items.title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity.
items.abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)-mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

items.title: Mitochondrial profiling links tumor genotype to metabolic and immune vulnerabilities in liver cancer.
items.abstract: Although oncogenic alterations influence tumor metabolism, how they impose distinct metabolic programs within a shared tissue remains poorly defined. We developed mitochondrial profiling platforms comparing metabolites and proteins in primary liver cancer (PLC) models. Analysis of six PLCs revealed that mitochondrial metabolism is dictated by oncogene identity. Kras-driven tumors required creatine metabolism to buffer energy, whereas c-MYC-driven tumors relied on oxidative phosphorylation. Among c-MYC-driven PLCs, Pten-deficient tumors accumulated mitochondrial phosphoethanolamine, a precursor of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE). Inhibition of PE synthesis selectively impaired Pten-deficient tumor growth and extended survival, partly through CD8+ T cell infiltration and sensitization to tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-mediated cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PE depletion increased the level of surface TNF receptors, promoting proinflammatory responses. These findings uncover genotype-specific metabolic liabilities and establish PE synthesis as a mechanism of immune evasion in PLC.

items.title: Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF inhibitor.
items.abstract: Targeting the RAS/MAPK pathway has long been constrained by dose-limiting toxicity in normal tissues at doses required for durable tumor control. Although Type 1.5 RAF inhibitors improved selectivity in BRAF(V600X)-monomer tumors, a comparable strategy for RAF dimer-driven cancers, including those with RAS mutations, has been lacking. We describe ELV-3111, a potent Type 1 RAF inhibitor that inhibits RAF dimers and exploits binding kinetics for tumor selectivity. ELV-3111 primes RAF in normal tissues, and its rapid dissociation during drug clearance generates drug-free RAF dimers that paradoxically activate MAPK signaling. RAS-mutant tumors are spared, where RAF is already primed. Combined with a MEK inhibitor, ELV-3111 restored normal tissue signaling while deepening tumor pathway inhibition, producing regressions across RAS- and BRAF-mutant experimental models. Thus, inhibitor dissociation kinetics provide a generalizable source of therapeutic index.

items.title: Mechanisms of nucleosome disruption shape epigenetic inheritance pathway choice.
items.abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

items.title: Giant-Cell Arteritis.
items.abstract: Giant-cell arteritis is a granulomatous vasculitis of large and medium-sized arteries that occurs almost exclusively in older adults. Suspected giant-cell arteritis warrants urgent diagnostic evaluation and, when ischemic risk is high, immediate treatment before diagnostic confirmation. Although glucocorticoids remain the cornerstone of therapy, treatment is frequently prolonged, associated with substantial toxic effects, and complicated by relapses. Advances in vascular imaging and insights into disease immunopathogenesis have expanded our understanding of disease heterogeneity and enabled the development of targeted therapies, particularly interleukin-6-receptor and Janus kinase inhibitors. Here, we review current concepts in the pathogenesis, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and management of giant-cell arteritis and highlight areas of uncertainty that warrant further investigation.

items.title: Blood-Pressure-Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum.

sections.objective: Treatment for lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of cardiovascular events among persons at high risk. Whether this benefit extends to those at lower risk remains unclear.
sections.methods: We performed a meta-analysis of individual participant data from randomized trials comparing antihypertensive treatment (intervention) with placebo, an active comparator, or usual care (comparator). The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major cardiovascular event (fatal or nonfatal stroke, fatal or nonfatal ischemic heart disease, or heart failure resulting in death or hospitalization; composite outcome). Safety was assessed in trials that compared antihypertensive treatment with placebo or usual care, according to three prespecified composite outcomes: cardiovascular or hemodynamic events (palpitations, bradycardia, or hypotension), adverse renal events, and neurovestibular or fall-associated events. Participants were grouped into deciles according to predicted 5-year risk of a major cardiovascular event (median, 12.3%; lowest decile, 27%).
sections.results: We included data from 51 trials and 357,440 participants - 169,042 in the intervention group and 188,398 in the comparator group. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, a major cardiovascular event occurred in 19,202 participants (11.4%) in the intervention group and in 24,398 (13.0%) in the comparator group. The overall estimated hazard ratio for a major cardiovascular event per 5-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure was 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 0.92), with no evidence of variation across deciles. The absolute reduction in the 5-year cumulative risk of a major cardiovascular event was greater in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (2.6 vs. 0.4 percentage points), and the number needed to treat to prevent one major cardiovascular event over 5 years was lower in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (38 vs. 255). The incidence of a cardiovascular or hemodynamic event was 12.0 per 1000 person-years in the intervention group and 6.5 per 1000 person-years in the comparator group; the incidence of an adverse renal event was 3.3 and 2.2 per 1000 person-years, respectively; and the incidence of a neurovestibular or fall-associated event was 19.1 and 16.6 per 1000 person-years. The relative increase in the risk of each safety-outcome event with antihypertensive treatment as compared with placebo or usual care did not appear to vary across deciles.
sections.conclusion: Blood-pressure lowering was associated with a decreased risk of major cardiovascular events across the risk spectrum, including a predicted 5-year risk below 4%. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; PROSPERO registry number, CRD42018099283.).

items.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3.
items.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

items.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor.
items.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal's assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing's most important challenges.

items.title: Nutritional interventions' impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings.
items.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

items.title: A fast radio burst at redshift 2, three billion years after the Big Bang.
items.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. We report radio observations of FRB 20240304B and near-infrared follow-up to identify its host galaxy. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

items.title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth.
items.abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas-informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

items.title: Stereodivergent telomerization of linear functionalized dienes with amines.
items.abstract: Despite the importance of divergent synthesis to obtain different isomers for medicinal and material chemistry, divergent stereocontrol over four distinct selectivity factors remains a fundamental challenge. The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We prepared diverse types of γ-amino esters from identical, readily available unsaturated esters and amines via synergistic palladium and acid catalysis, with each precisely obtained out of hundreds of potential telomers. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

items.title: Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in Intermediate-High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism.

sections.objective: Whether catheter-directed thrombolysis improves clinical outcomes in patients with intermediate-high-risk pulmonary embolism, as compared with anticoagulation alone, is uncertain.
sections.methods: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial, we randomly assigned patients with intermediate-high-risk acute pulmonary embolism (defined by hemodynamic stability, a simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index score of ≥1, and right ventricular dysfunction plus an elevated level of cardiac troponin or natriuretic peptide) in a 1:1 ratio to receive catheter-directed thrombolysis with alteplase plus anticoagulation therapy (thrombolysis group) or anticoagulation therapy alone (standard-care group). The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, recurrence of pulmonary embolism, or cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse within 7 days after randomization. Secondary outcomes included clinically relevant bleeding as defined by the Bleeding Academic Research Consortium, major bleeding as defined in the Global Use of Strategies to Open Occluded Coronary Arteries guidelines, and intracranial hemorrhage.
sections.results: A total of 558 patients underwent randomization; 280 were assigned to the thrombolysis group, and 278 to the standard-care group. The median age was 64 years, and 40.9% were female. A primary-outcome event occurred in 2 patients (0.7%) in the thrombolysis group and in 19 patients (6.8%) in the standard-care group (relative risk, 0.10; 95% confidence interval, 0.02 to 0.44; P<0.001); this difference was driven mainly by the lower incidence of cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse in the thrombolysis group. By day 7, clinically relevant bleeding had occurred in 13 patients (4.6%) in the thrombolysis group and in 14 patients (5.0%) in the standard-care group (P = 0.85); major bleeding in 4 (1.4%) and 6 (2.2%), respectively (P = 0.54); and intracranial hemorrhage in 2 (0.7%) and none. One patient in the thrombolysis group died within 30 days, and 4 patients in the standard-care group died within 7 days.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with intermediate-high-risk acute pulmonary embolism, catheter-directed thrombolysis with alteplase plus anticoagulation therapy led to a lower risk of death from any cause, recurrent pulmonary embolism, or cardiorespiratory decompensation or collapse within 7 days after randomization than anticoagulation therapy alone. (Funded by the Ministry of Health of the Czech Republic and others; PRAGUE-26 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05493163; EudraCT number, 2022-002218-18; European Union Clinical Trials number, 2024-516144-25-00.).

items.title: Eplontersen for Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is a progressive, life-threatening disease caused by deposition of misfolded transthyretin (TTR). Eplontersen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces the production of hepatic TTR. The effect of eplontersen on ATTR-CM is unclear.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, international, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with ATTR-CM to receive subcutaneous eplontersen (45 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 140 weeks, in addition to standard treatment. The primary end point was a cumulative composite of death from cardiovascular causes and recurrent cardiovascular clinical events up to week 140. The effect of death from noncardiovascular causes on the primary analysis was assessed with a cumulative composite of death from any cause and cardiovascular events up to week 140.
sections.results: A total of 1432 patients underwent randomization and received at least one dose of the assigned intervention (715 patients in the eplontersen group and 717 in the placebo group). The mean age of the patients was 76.4 years, and 90.6% were men. A total of 381 primary end-point events occurred in 210 patients (29.4%) receiving eplontersen, and 392 events occurred in 231 patients (32.2%) receiving placebo (rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 1.09; P = 0.28). Death from cardiovascular causes, as a component of the primary end point, occurred in 74 patients in the eplontersen group and in 70 in the placebo group; there were 307 cardiovascular clinical events in the eplontersen group and 322 in the placebo group. The rate ratio for the composite of death from any cause and cardiovascular events was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.71 to 1.04). Serious adverse events occurred in 413 patients (57.8%) in the eplontersen group and in 426 (59.4%) in the placebo group.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with ATTR-CM, eplontersen therapy did not lead to a lower risk of a composite of death from cardiovascular causes and recurrent cardiovascular events than placebo up to 140 weeks. (Funded by Ionis Pharmaceuticals and AstraZeneca; CARDIO-TTRansform ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04136171.).

items.title: The protease MALT1 uses K63-linked and linear ubiquitin chains to recruit and cleave substrates containing ubiquitin binding domains.
items.abstract: The protease mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue-1 (MALT1) regulates T-and B cell receptor (T/BCR)-induced lymphocyte activation and development. However, the mechanisms governing MALT1 substrate recognition and the extent to which its substrate specificity can be modulated pharmacologically remain incompletely understood. Using cells deficient in assembling K63-linked and/or linear ubiquitin chains on the MALT1 protease complex, together with approaches ablating ubiquitin-binding sites of specific MALT1 substrates, we demonstrate that ubiquitin chains associated with the MALT1 protease complex attract specific ubiquitin-binding substrates. Pharmacological inhibition of linear/K63-linked ubiquitin chain formation modulated the cleavage of individual MALT1 substrates in primary lymphocytes and cell lines according to their ubiquitin-binding properties. This led to altered lymphocyte cytokine responses dependent on changes in MALT1's substrate cleavage profile. Thus, we establish a paradigm for protease-substrate recognition in which ubiquitin chains associated with the protease complex facilitate substrate recruitment. This information has significant ramifications for immune regulation and cancer therapy.

items.title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome.
items.abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour-stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

items.title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes.
items.abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3-7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self-non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer-promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

items.title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems.
items.abstract: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR-Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex1,2. Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools3-6. Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST (PseCAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution8. However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation9. Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the PseCAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the PseCAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade-TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa PseCAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC-TnsB and TnsB-target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

items.title: A gut-brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila.
items.abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut-brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop-a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut-brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states.

items.title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals.
items.abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics1,2. Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively2, rare variation remains relatively unexplored1. Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from -17cm (ACAN) to +11 cm (FBN1) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes (TET1, DTL and IGF2BP2) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects-often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes-and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.

items.title: Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids.
items.abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V-1 s-1 and submillimetre drift lengths-far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection.

items.title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease.
items.abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb-seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

items.title: Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro.
items.abstract: Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1-7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

items.title: Middle-Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China.
items.abstract: Molecular and morphological evidence increasingly supports the view that most East Asian Middle to Late Pleistocene archaic Homo belong to Denisovans1, yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5-42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo, as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo.

items.title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST.
items.abstract: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs)1,2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus1, yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade-TniQ, TnsC and TnsA-TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems.

items.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains.
items.abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot-superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man's Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but lack topological protection3-5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man's Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6-8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man's Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

items.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage.
items.abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems-a centuries-old practice2,3-causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800-2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48-99) mW m-2-equivalent to 2.7 (1.8-3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing-originating from 0.4-0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52-110) mW m-2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (-9 (-15--2) mW m-2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

items.title: Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts.
items.abstract: Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide1-4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999-2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species' elevational ranges: upper portions of species' ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

items.title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation.
items.abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease.

items.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing.
items.abstract: Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1-7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10-12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of O ( 1 ) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

items.title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway.
items.abstract: Slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1-3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale.

items.title: An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals.
items.abstract: Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30-40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4-32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7-42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

items.title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP.
items.abstract: Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

items.title: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis.
items.abstract: Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol-1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

items.title: Prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and risk of neurodevelopmental disorders: Scandinavian multinational cohort study.

sections.objective: To assess whether prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children.
sections.methods: Population based cohort study. 3 643 376 children born in 2000-21 followed up for a median 9 years after birth in Sweden and 10 years in Norway and Denmark. Prenatal exposure, defined as ≥1 filled prescription for ADHD drug treatment anytime during pregnancy or in the second/third trimester (≥98 days after the last menstrual period). Analyses were also done for monotherapy with methylphenidate, amphetamines, and atomoxetine. Unexposed pregnancies had no filled prescriptions for ADHD drugs during pregnancy.
sections.results: 7595 (0.2%) children were prenatally exposed to any ADHD drug (5230 methylphenidate, 1510 amphetamines, 553 atomoxetine only). About one third (n=2389) were exposed in the second/third trimester. After control for confounders, neither any nor second/third trimester exposure to ADHD drugs overall or by drug type was associated with increased risk of any neurodevelopmental disorder (weighted hazard ratio 1.05, 95% confidence interval 0.98 to 1.12), behavioural and emotional disorders (1.04, 0.97 to 1.12), or disorders of psychological and intellectual development (1.06, 0.96 to 1.18). Some elevated hazard ratios for infrequent outcomes were observed but not consistently identified across analyses.
sections.conclusion: This multinational cohort study found no increased risk of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders associated with prenatal exposure to ADHD drugs. These findings strengthen existing evidence and can assist pregnant people and clinicians in weighing the benefits and risks of such treatment during pregnancy.
sections.other: Nationwide register data on births, dispensed drugs, and specialist healthcare diagnoses from Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. Neurodevelopmental disorders (any, subgroups, and individual disorders), identified on the basis of inpatient and outpatient diagnoses in specialist healthcare. Propensity score overlap weighted Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted (weighted) hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals. Data from Denmark were analysed separately, and results were pooled using random effects meta-analysis.

items.title: Advances in the management of myasthenia gravis.
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterised by fluctuating fatigable weakness of skeletal muscles. Advances have led to the identification of distinct antibody subtypes and expanding therapeutic options, transforming myasthenia gravis from a disease of significant morbidity and mortality to one that is increasingly manageable. This review presents a comprehensive overview of myasthenia gravis, including its epidemiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnostic strategies, and treatment modalities. Established therapies are discussed, including acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, corticosteroids, conventional oral immunosuppressants, intravenous immunoglobulin, plasma exchange, B cell depleting agents, complement inhibitors, neonatal fragment crystallisable receptor inhibitors, and thymectomy. A dedicated section highlights emerging treatments. Special considerations for pregnancy, myasthenic crisis, and individualised treatment approaches are emphasised. Physician-patient communication is highlighted as a critical factor in optimising adherence and outcomes. Effective integration of novel therapies into clinical practice depends on a clear understanding of their mechanisms, safety profiles, and applicability across diverse patient populations. As therapeutic complexity increases, improved clinical outcomes will require continued refinement of clinical tools, treatment algorithms, optimal communication strategies, and robust data to guide evidence based decision making.

items.title: Preconception antidepressant use in fathers and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring: Danish population based cohort study.

sections.objective: To investigate the associations between paternal antidepressant use during spermatogenesis and risk of metabolic disorders in offspring.
sections.methods: Nationwide population based cohort study. 1 365 887 liveborn singleton infants in Denmark from 2000 to 2023, followed from birth until 31 December 2023, death, emigration, or first occurrence of outcome, whichever came first.
sections.results: 23 572 (1.7%) offspring were born to fathers who used antidepressants during spermatogenesis. During a mean follow-up of 12.1 years (standard deviation 7.0 years), 18 353 (1.3%) offspring were diagnosed with a metabolic disorder, including 364 whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis and 17 989 whose fathers did not use antidepressants during this period (1.39 v 1.11 events per 1000 person years, respectively). Offspring whose fathers used antidepressants during spermatogenesis had a slightly higher risk of developing metabolic disorders (weighted hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04 to 1.38) compared with offspring who were unexposed. The associations varied by specific metabolic outcomes, with weighted hazard ratios ranging from 0.81 (95% CI 0.45 to 1.47) for hypercholesterolaemia to 1.64 (95% CI 1.21 to 2.22) for hypertension. However, when compared with offspring of fathers who took antidepressants during the pregnancy period only, no increased risk was found of any metabolic disorders (0.75, 95% CI 0.58 to 0.98) or of specific metabolic disorders.
sections.conclusion: The slightly increased risk of metabolic disorders in offspring of fathers using antidepressants during spermatogenesis was probably attributable to underlying paternal mental health disorders. These findings offer reassurance for men treated with antidepressants before pregnancy.
sections.other: Danish national registers.
