Despite the real-world setting and relatively poor-risk population, there were no new safety signals compared with those reported in previous of ipilimumab-nivolumab and cabozantinib-nivolumab in first-line mccRCC. These findings support use of first-line ipilimumab-nivolumab before a response-adapted treatment strategy.

items.title: Effect of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg on glycaemic outcomes and their association with weight loss: a substudy of the randomised, double-masked, parallel-group, phase 3a REDEFINE 2 trial.

sections.objective: CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg, a fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide, demonstrated substantial weight loss versus placebo in adults with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes in REDEFINE 2. We aimed to evaluate glycaemic outcomes in a subgroup of participants who underwent continuous glucose monitoring (CGM).
sections.methods: REDEFINE 2 was a global 68-week, double-masked, parallel-group phase 3a trial that included 1206 adults from 12 countries with a BMI of at least 27 kg/m2 and type 2 diabetes who were randomly assigned (3:1) to once-weekly subcutaneous CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg or placebo. Participants were assigned treatment using a centralised web-based system. Participants, investigators, site staff, and the sponsor were masked to group allocation throughout the trial. A subgroup of 199 participants from 35 US sites (including university hospitals, health-care centres, research centres, and other centres) were equipped with a CGM device (Dexcom G6 Pro) for double-masked measurements from week -3 to 0, week 20 to 24, and week 64 to 68. Prespecified secondary endpoints included change in time in range (TIR; 3·9-10·0 mmol/L) and change in time in tight range (TITR; 3·9-7·8 mmol/L) for CagriSema versus placebo. REDEFINE 2 is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05394519, and is completed.
sections.results: Between Feb 1 and Aug 11, 2023, 199 participants were enrolled in the CGM subgroup (149 in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and 50 in the placebo group) and had their CGM data analysed. The mean age of participants in the CGM subgroup was 60·4 years (SD 11·3), 106 (53%) of the 199 participants were female, 93 (47%) were male, and 160 (80%) were White. Compared with placebo, participants in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group had a significant increase from baseline to week 68 in mean percentage of TIR (45·9 percentage points [SE 1·2] vs 3·0 percentage points [5·7]; estimated treatment difference [ETD] 42·9 percentage points [95% CI 30·7-55·0]; p<0·0001) and mean percentage of TITR (50·4 percentage points [2·2] vs 2·8 percentage points [2·7]; ETD 47·7 percentage points [95% CI 40·7-54·7]; p<0·0001) using the trial product estimand. The overall observed mean change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68 was -16·7% (SD 7·9) for the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and -1·8% (4·5) for the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 144 (97%) of 149 participants in the CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg group and in 42 (84%) of 50 participants in the placebo group, and were predominantly mild or moderate in severity.
sections.conclusion: In this hypothesis-generating analysis, CGM-based assessments provided evidence of an effect of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg on glycaemic outcomes in people living with type 2 diabetes. These findings support the potential use of CagriSema 2·4 mg/2·4 mg for improving glucose control in people living with overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: The global hypertension care cascade in May Measurement Month 2023: a cross-sectional opportunistic blood pressure screening campaign.

sections.objective: Raised blood pressure is the leading contributor to global morbidity and mortality. May Measurement Month is an annual global blood pressure screening campaign aimed at raising hypertension awareness. In this study we present the results of the 2023 campaign.
sections.methods: In this multinational, cross-sectional blood pressure screening survey, volunteers aged 18 years and older were opportunistically recruited using convenience sampling. Recruitment took place between May 1 and July 31, 2023, at screening sites (eg, hospitals, community centres, etc) across 70 countries. Participants completed three sitting blood pressure measurements and a questionnaire on demographic, clinical, and lifestyle information all on the day of recruitment. Raised blood pressure was defined as systolic blood pressure of 140 mm Hg or more or diastolic blood pressure of 90 mm Hg or more or both (ie, from an average of the mean of the second and third of three readings). Hypertension was defined as raised blood pressure, taking blood pressure-lowering medication, or a combination of the two. The main outcome was to describe the hypertension care cascade at the global and regional level and by sex.
sections.results: Of 673 304 participants screened (mean age 47·5 years [SD 17·3]; 362 116 [54·2%] were female and 306 241 [45·5%] were male), 547 584 (81·3%) were from lower-income or middle-income countries and 95 920 (14·2%) had never previously had their blood pressure measured. Of 258 802 participants with hypertension (121 168 [39·6%] were male and 135 242 [37·3%] were female), 163 295 (63·1%) were aware, 156 218 (60·4%) were being treated, 89 530 (34·6%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 140/90 mm Hg, and 40 748 (15·7%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 130/80 mm Hg. Awareness, treatment, and control rates were all higher among females than males. Of 156 218 taking blood pressure-lowering medication, 89 530 (57·3%) had controlled blood pressure to lower than 140/90 mm Hg and 40 748 (26·1%) to lower than 130/80 mm Hg, with 67 062 (51·6%) using monotherapy. 169 272 participants had untreated or inadequately treated hypertension (25·1% of those surveyed; 65·4% of participants with hypertension). 128 448 (44·8%) of those with a BMI of 25 kg/m2 or higher, 35 482 (68·8%) with a history of diabetes, 5041 (68·8%) with kidney failure, and 7141 (76·2%) of those with heart failure had hypertension.
sections.conclusion: One-quarter of participants had untreated or inadequately treated hypertension, reflecting the high global burden and low rates of awareness. Opportunistic May Measurement Month screening provides a low-cost, scalable route to increase awareness and detection of raised blood pressure.

items.title: Incidence of Mycoplasma genitalium infection and prevalence of antimicrobial resistance markers in men who have sex with men receiving doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis in France: a secondary outcome analysis of the ANRS 174 DOXYVAC randomised trial.

sections.objective: Doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (DoxyPEP) reduces bacterial sexually transmitted infections among men who have sex with men (MSM), but its effect on Mycoplasma genitalium infection and potential to select for antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remain uncertain. We assessed M genitalium incidence in MSM and the effect of DoxyPEP on markers associated with M genitalium AMR in a secondary analysis of the ANRS 174 DOXYVAC trial.
sections.methods: In this open-label, 2 × 2 factorial randomised trial at ten hospital sites in Paris, MSM receiving HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis and with a bacterial sexually transmitted infection in the previous year were assigned (2:1) to receive doxycycline 200 mg orally within 72 h after condomless sex (up to three doses weekly) or no PEP, independently of meningococcal group B vaccination. Anal, urine, and throat samples underwent M genitalium PCR at baseline and every 3 months. Mutations in 23S rRNA, 16S rRNA, parC, and gyrA were assessed in positive samples (cycle threshold ≤30); mgpB sequencing was used for typing. Cox regression adjusted for vaccination estimated the first-infection hazard ratio; Fisher's exact tests compared resistance markers and sequence types. Analyses included participants with at least one follow-up visit. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04597424). Recruitment is complete.
sections.results: Between Jan 19, 2021, and Sept 19, 2022, 545 participants (median age 40 years [IQR 34-49]) were assigned to receive DoxyPEP (n=362) or no PEP (n=183). At baseline, 481 (88%) of 545 participants were recorded as White, 13 (2%) as Black, 13 (2%) as Asian, and 38 (7%) as other or unknown ethnicity. Overall, 138 (25%) of 545 participants had M genitalium infection. The incidence of a first M genitalium infection was 32·3 per 100 person-years (114 events) in the DoxyPEP group versus 44·9 (73 events) in the no-PEP group (adjusted hazard ratio 0·72 [95% CI 0·54-0·96]; p=0·027). During follow-up, macrolide resistance-associated mutations were detected in 26 (76%) of 34 samples in the DoxyPEP group versus 32 (94%) of 34 in the no-PEP group (p=0·083); fluoroquinolone resistance-associated mutations in 19 (54%) of 35 versus 17 (53%) of 32 (p>0·99); and 16S rRNA tetracycline-binding-site mutations in two (6%) of 32 versus six (22%) of 27 (p=0·13). Among 133 M genitalium-positive samples, 28 mgpB sequence types were identified, with no significant difference in distribution between groups (p=0·91). Dual-resistant ST159 was most frequent (43 [32%] of 133 samples).
sections.conclusion: DoxyPEP modestly reduced M genitalium incidence among MSM receiving HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis without a detected increase in resistance-associated mutations or selection of dual-resistant ST159, although limited testing constrains interpretation. These findings are consistent with guidance to restrict M genitalium testing and treatment to patients with symptomatic infections and highlight the need for AMR surveillance as DoxyPEP use expands.

items.title: Single-sequence, structure-free allosteric residue prediction with protein language models.
items.abstract: Large language models trained on protein sequences learn general coevolutionary relationships at scale, which contain useful structural and functional information. We show that attention maps, matrices of learned pairwise relationships between residues, include information about allostery. This enables prediction of allosteric relationships with no task-specific training, requiring a single input sequence and specified active-site residues, without structural information. Attention maps outperform established structure-based and sequence coevolution-based models across a benchmark of 109 allosteric proteins. In the beta-2 adrenergic receptor, a G-protein coupled receptor, attention maps correlate more strongly with experimental alanine-scanning measurements of allosteric effects on signaling than these comparators. Language model attention also guides efficient, low-throughput experimental discovery of putative allosteric residues in the protease DPP4 and residues coupled to the known allosteric pathway in ACE2. These results enable and demonstrate allosteric relationship prediction in a zero-shot, single-sequence, structure-free manner. We provide this method in the AlloGator web interface.

items.title: Microtubule Detyrosination Contributes to Altered Nuclear Mechanotransduction and Signaling in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
items.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is characterized by left ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction and is accompanied by extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, including increased desmin, tubulin, and detyrosinated tubulin levels, which we previously showed contribute to impaired relaxation. Because microtubules connect to the nucleus via the Linker of Nucleoskeleton and Cytoskeleton complex, we investigated whether cytoskeletal remodeling alters nuclear morphology, mechanics, and hypertrophy-associated signaling. Using electron microscopy and immunofluorescence in cardiac septal tissue from patients with obstructive HCM and nonfailing donors, and immunofluorescence and live-cell imaging in septal tissue from wild-type and homozygous HCM-associated Mybpc3 c.2373InsG mice, we found that nuclei were enlarged and highly invaginated, with restricted nuclear deformation during contraction, indicating altered mechanotransduction. These changes were associated with increased Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1) nuclear localization and increased expression of YAP1 target and hypertrophic genes. Inhibiting microtubule detyrosination reduced nuclear abnormalities, restored nuclear deformation, and tended to decrease YAP1 nuclear translocation, identifying nuclear mechanotransduction as a potential therapeutic target in HCM.

items.title: Associations of Physical Activity With Aortic Structure and Hemodynamics in the UK Biobank.

sections.objective: Intense physical training is associated with cardiac remodeling, but the relationship between habitual exercise and aortic phenotypes in the general population remains poorly characterized. This study evaluated associations between physical activity and aortic size and function in a large population-based cohort.
sections.methods: We analyzed 13,289 UK Biobank participants without hypertension who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance and wrist accelerometry. Ascending and descending aortic area, diameter, and distensibility were modeled against device-measured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), mean acceleration, and self-reported MVPA. Sex-stratified generalized linear models were adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, medications, laboratory values, vitals, and accelerometer wear. Stroke volume index and systolic blood pressure were evaluated as candidate mediators.
sections.results: Higher MVPA was associated with larger ascending and descending aortic dimensions in both sexes (P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, each additional 60 minutes per day corresponded to 0.37 mm (95% CI: 0.25-0.49) and 0.39 mm (95% CI: 0.25-0.53) larger ascending aortic diameter in women and men, respectively, and 0.28 mm larger descending aortic diameter in both women and men. Distensibility was preserved across all segments. Higher mean acceleration and self-reported MVPA were associated with greater aortic distensibility in men. Stroke volume index accounted for 42% to 60% of the MVPA-aortic area association. Systolic blood pressure was not a mediator.
sections.conclusion: Among adults without hypertension, MVPA was associated with larger aortic dimensions without impaired distensibility, partially mediated by greater stroke volume. These associations suggest physical activity-related aortic dilation may be distinct from vasculopathy-driven aortic enlargement. Longitudinal prospective studies incorporating exercise data are warranted to validate these findings.

items.title: Reduced microbial touch transmission by engineering the microtopography of medical glove surfaces.
items.abstract: Touch transmission of pathogens is a major contributor to the spread of infectious disease within hospitals as health care workers interact with patients and the environment. Reducing microbial transmission by touch contact can reduce rates of health care-associated infections. We modified commercial medical gloves with superhydrophobic (Cassie-Baxter) microtopographies to test rates of microbial attachment and transmission through touch contact with contaminated fomite surfaces. Molded post and groove topographies with critical dimensions between 2.5 and 15 micrometers were evaluated through compressive touch experiments with six clinically relevant microbial species (Candida albicans, Enterococcus faecium, Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Staphylococcus epidermidis). After compressive contact (1- to 9-newton force), results showed an average reduction of 1.65 log (97.8%) in cells transferred to post or straight-walled groove-modified gloves compared with unmodified gloves, for all species (P < 0.0001). For sequential touch transmission to multiple surfaces, there was a 1.8 to 2.0 log (98.4 to 99%) reduction in S. aureus and K. pneumoniae transferred to modified gloves compared with controls. Transfer efficiencies fell from 43.6 ± 12.2% to 1.79 ± 0.70% (P10) and 1.75 ± 0.48% (SW15) for S. aureus (P < 0.001), with comparable reductions for K. pneumoniae. Touch transmission from dry biofilms and hospital bedrail surfaces was similarly reduced. The mechanisms underlying this nonspecific microbial repellency were reduction in physical transfer of contaminated fluids and limited surface area for microbial attachment. These reductions in microbial attachment and transfer for topography-modified gloves may contribute to reducing pathogen transmission within hospitals.

items.title: Loperamide and survival in Ebola virus disease: an instrumental variable analysis of pooled individual patient data from the 2013-16 west African epidemic.

sections.objective: Mortality in Ebola virus disease is highest during the early phase of illness, in particular in low-resource settings where high temperatures and the risk of infection limit rehydration therapy. Scalable adjunctive therapies that reduce gastrointestinal fluid loss in the early phase of the disease could thus improve survival outcomes. WHO guidance has varied in its support for loperamide use for patients with Ebola virus disease and diarrhoea, and no previous analysis of individual patient data has evaluated the effect of loperamide on survival. We aimed to establish the effect of loperamide on the survival of patients with Ebola virus disease.
sections.methods: In this instrumental variable analysis, we analysed pooled observational individual patient data from the Infectious Disease Data Observatory (IDDO) Ebola platform, which included patients treated in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone from Jan 4, 2014, to April 1, 2016, during the 2013-16 Ebola virus disease epidemic in west Africa. We included patients with laboratory-confirmed Ebola virus disease and documented diarrhoea. We estimated the effect of recorded loperamide receipt on 30-day mortality using extended Cox models within a two-stage residual inclusion (2SRI) instrumental variable analysis, exploiting lagged site-level prescribing preference as the instrument. We conducted robustness and falsification tests using spline-based time-varying specifications and negative-control exposures.
sections.results: Of the 13 859 patients from 21 Ebola treatment units in the IDDO dataset, 5509 patients from 20 treatment units had laboratory-confirmed Ebola virus disease and documented diarrhoea; 2873 (52·2%) were female and 2636 (47·8%) were male. In the time-varying 2SRI model, loperamide was associated with baseline hazard ratio (HR) of 0·39 (95% CI 0·26-0·58) on day 0·5, corresponding to an HR of 0·34 (0·23-0·51) on day 1. This protective effect persisted throughout the 30-day follow-up and was robust to spline specifications and negative-control falsification analyses.
sections.conclusion: Instrumental variable analyses showed a protective early effect of loperamide use on mortality among patients with Ebola virus disease and diarrhoea. Robustness and falsification analyses provide triangulating evidence of the early effect estimate. Our results support reassessing loperamide for inclusion in WHO guidance on supportive care for patients with Ebola virus disease and considering its use and further evaluation where intravenous fluid therapy cannot be provided, including in some Ebola treatment units and during emergency care in communities and homes.

items.title: Sexual wellbeing in Britain: findings from the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4).

sections.objective: Sexual wellbeing is an individual state of feeling respected, safe, and comfortable with sex and sexuality, and having self-esteem, agency, and support in one's sexual life. It is related to, but distinct from, sexual function and sexual health. The epidemiology of sexual wellbeing in a general population is not well understood. We aimed to examine inequalities in low sexual wellbeing, and discover associations with sexual behaviour, sexual and reproductive health experiences, and general and mental health. We sought to understand which individual items within our validated 13-item measure of sexual wellbeing (the Natsal-SW) are most strongly associated with key sexual health behaviours and indicators.
sections.methods: We conducted the fourth National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4), which is a large nationally representative cross-sectional study of people aged 16-59 years who are resident in Britain (data used here collected between Sept 20, 2022, and Dec 3, 2023). 4160 participants reporting sexual experience ever completed the Natsal-SW; standardised score range 0-52, low selected as ≤33, and high as ≥48. Focusing attention on those with most need, we used age-adjusted logistic regressions to examine associations with low sexual wellbeing.
sections.results: The weighted prevalence of current low sexual wellbeing was similar in women (14·3% [95% CI 12·6-16·3]) and men (13·7% [11·7-15·9]), but high sexual wellbeing was slightly less prevalent in women than men (20·7% [95% CI 18·7- 22·8] vs 24·4% [21·8- 27·1]; p=0·024). Nine items on Natsal-SW differed by gender; notably women were more likely to report feeling upset with others about past sexual events, and men to report feeling ashamed about sexual thoughts. The odds of low sexual wellbeing were greater among young people (aged 16-24 years), individuals from sexual and gender minorities, individuals reporting lower income and, among women only, educational level. Low sexual wellbeing was associated with reporting first sex after age 25 years, symptoms of sexually-transmitted infections and less frequent sex in the past month, at least four partners, distressing sexual problems, and sexual violence in the past year, and at least one same-sex partner in the past 5 years. Low sexual wellbeing was associated with currently screening positive for depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-2-item) and anxiety (Generalised Anxiety Disorder-2-item) symptoms and low mental wellbeing, particularly among men. Associations between key sexual health and behaviour indicators, and low sexual wellbeing, remained after adjustment for mental health.
sections.conclusion: Low sexual wellbeing is unequally distributed, and patterns of association differ notably from sexual health. These data support future inclusion of sexual wellbeing in population health policy and intervention.

items.title: Prevalence and trends in sexual behaviour in Britain from 1990 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal).

sections.objective: Contemporary data on sexual behaviour are needed to inform and evaluate sexual and reproductive health strategies and services and understand societal shifts. In this assessment of the National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal), we aimed to provide up-to-date prevalence estimates and examine changes in key sexual behaviours in Britain reported between 1990 and 2024.
sections.methods: The Natsal study is repeat cross-sectional probability-sample surveys of the British population, undertaken approximately decennially since 1990. Natsal-4 (2022-24) used interviewer-administered and self-completion questionnaires, among two probability samples: an address-based sample and a probability panel. Data were weighted to broadly align with Britain's sociodemographic structure. In Natsal-4, prevalence of sexual experiences, partner numbers, frequency of sex, and online behaviours are presented by age and gender among participants aged 16-59 years, with changes in prevalence across Natsal surveys presented by age and gender among participants aged 16-44 years.
sections.results: Of 6719 Natsal-4 participants (aged 16-59 years), 89·4% (95% CI 88·3-90·4) reported ever having sex (median five lifetime partners for both women and men). In the past year, 77·0% (95% CI 75·6-78·4) reported having had sex, and 65·5% (63·9-67·0) reported one sexual partner. Reporting at least one new partner in the past year was highest among participants aged 16-24 years (21·7% [95% CI 17·3-26·8] in women, 30·1% [24·5-36·4] in men). Pornography use and sexting (sending or receiving sexual images) in the past year were more common among men (80·7% [95% CI 78·6-82·6] and 26·0% [23·9-28·3], respectively) than among women (36·6% [34·7-38·5] and 22·2% [20·5-23·9], respectively); both were higher among younger age groups. The proportion of 16-24-year-olds who reported never having had sex increased from 18·9% (95% CI 17·0-20·9) in Natsal-3 (2010-12) to 37·7% (36·2-43·1) in Natsal-4 (2022-24) among women; and 18·2% (16·2-20·4) to 28·4% (23·1-34·5) among men. Reporting of same-sex sex increased among 16-44-year-olds from 6·8% (95% CI 6·1-7·6) in 2010-12 to 14·0% (12·4-15·7) in 2022-24 among women, and from 4·0% (3·3-4·7) to 12·3% (10·4-14·5) among men. Among 16-44-year-olds, we found a decline in average frequency of sex from four times per month in Natsal-1 (1990) to twice per month in Natsal-4 (2022-24).
sections.conclusion: Sexual behaviour in Britain has shifted markedly since 1990, including a recent decline in sexual experience among young people and increased reporting of same-sex attraction and behaviour across all age groups. Sexual and reproductive health policies and services remain essential and must adapt to shifting needs and new areas of risk and vulnerability, including safe engagement in online sexual activity.

items.title: Sexually transmitted infections, behavioural risks, and uptake of sexual health services in Britain from 2010 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal).

sections.objective: Sexually transmitted infection (STI) diagnoses have increased in Britain since 2010, alongside major changes to sexual health policy, services, and disruptions owing to the COVID-19 pandemic. Meanwhile, sexual activity has decreased at population level, and more people report same-sex behaviours. To understand implications for HIV and STI control, we examined the general population prevalence of three STIs, sexual behaviours associated with STIs, and uptake of sexual health services, including HIV and chlamydia testing.
sections.methods: We conducted the fourth National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal-4) between Sept 20, 2022, and April 5, 2024. In this analysis, we used cross-sectional data from 5949 sexually experienced (who reported ever having sex) participants aged 16-59 years in Britain from the probability sample surveys. We estimated weighted prevalences for STIs using biosamples (vaginal swabs or urine samples; n=2721), self-reported STI-associated behaviours (including a composite of ≥4 partners, condomless sex with ≥2 partners in the past year, or overlapping partners in the past 5 years), and sexual health service uptake. Comparisons were made between groups defined by partners' sex and over time by comparing with Natsal-3 (2010-12).
sections.results: In Natsal-4, overall prevalence of Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and Trichomonas vaginalis was less than 1·0%. C trachomatis prevalence was highest in women aged 16-24 years (4·0%, 95% CI 1·3-11·7). STI-associated behaviours (composite) were most prevalent in young people (aged 16-24 years) with only opposite-sex partners (women 26·5%, 95% CI 20·2-33·9; men 29·4%, 22·5-37·6), women reporting sex with women and men (WSWM; 60·0%, 49·0-70·1), and men reporting sex with men (MSM; 57·1%, 48·6-65·3). Among those with only opposite-sex partners, past-year uptake was higher in women than men for sexual health service use (women 8·3%, 7·2-9·6; men 3·9%, 3·0-5·1), HIV testing (women 5·8%, 4·9-7·0; men 2·8%, 2·1-3·7), and chlamydia testing (women 8·4%, 7·1-10·1; men 4·7%, 3·4-6·4). Among participants reporting STI-associated behaviours, apart from MSM (47·3%, 36·1-58·8), the majority of people who reported STI-associated behaviours had not taken up services (eg, for sexual health services in participants with opposite-sex partners: women 73·8%, 67·8-79·1; men 84·9%, 79·4-89·4; WSWM 68·6%, 54.1-80.2). Between Natsal-3 and Natsal-4, HIV testing increased in MSM, sexual health service use decreased in young men with only opposite-sex partners, and chlamydia testing markedly declined (eg, in all women aged 16-24 years: Natsal-3 54·2%, 51·4-57·0; Natsal-4 17·8%, 12·7-24·5).
sections.conclusion: Many people remain at behavioural risk for STIs, particularly young people, WSWM, and MSM. Most people with STI-associated behaviours had not used sexual health services in the past year. Declining chlamydia testing and high prevalence in young women might cause reproductive harm. Universal sexual health services remain essential.

items.title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, vaccination, and cervical screening in Britain from 1999 to 2024: findings from the repeated cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal).

sections.objective: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and cervical screening have substantially reduced overall cervical cancer risk, but differences in uptake must be quantified to inform equitable access. This study aimed to provide population-level evidence of the impact of HPV vaccination on HPV types 16 and 18 (hereafter HPV-16/18) prevalence in England, Scotland, and Wales (hereafter Britain), and uptake of cervical cancer prevention interventions (ie, vaccination and screening), 15 years after the introduction of the vaccination programme in 2008.
sections.methods: We conducted the National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal), which are nationally representative, cross-sectional population surveys with individual-level data and HPV testing of biosamples. Data from Natsal-2 (1999-2001; before the vaccination programme was introduced, and included urine biosamples), Natsal-3 (2010-12; early in the vaccination programme, and included urine biosamples), and Natsal-4 (2022-24; after the vaccination programme was established, and included vaginal swab and urine biosamples) were analysed. Age-adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) for HPV-16/18 infection were estimated among women eligible for routine vaccination (born from Sept 1, 1995) compared with same-aged women before the vaccination programme was introduced. Combined Natsal-4 probability and non-probability data assessed factors associated with self-reported HPV vaccination and cervical screening.
sections.results: Among 10 418 Natsal-4 women (aged 16-59 years), 1059 women in the probability sample group (aged 18-44 years) provided usable biosamples (Natsal-2 n=1849; Natsal-3 n=2407). HPV-16/18 prevalence was 86% lower (aPR 0·14, 95% CI 0·02-0·84) among those aged 18-29 years in Natsal-4 (1·6%, 95% CI 0·3-8·2) than in Natsal-2 (8·7%, 95% CI 6·7-11·3). All HPV-16/18 infections reported in Natsal-4 occurred in unvaccinated women. Of 733 routine vaccination-eligible women, 23·0% (95% CI 19·4-27·0) reported being unvaccinated. Among 3530 women (aged 25-59 years) eligible for cervical screening, 5·3% (95% CI 4·4-6·3) reported never attending screening. Non-uptake of vaccination and screening was higher among minority ethnic groups, religious groups, and those born outside the UK. Prevalence of high-risk, non-vaccine-preventable HPV (HPV 35, 39, 51, 56, and 59) infections was 4·9% (95% CI 3·7-6·4) in the total population, without any statistically significant differences between these subgroups. Women with higher-risk sexual behaviours were more likely to both be vaccinated and attend for screening.
sections.conclusion: Britain's HPV vaccination programme has driven a dramatic decline in HPV-16/18 prevalence and WHO cervical cancer elimination targets might be achievable overall if this is sustained. However, women from minority ethnic groups, religious groups, and those not born in the UK are less likely to be vaccinated and screened while remaining at risk. It is crucial to improve the reach of prevention interventions to more equitably reduce cervical cancer morbidity and mortality.

items.title: A shared interbacterial membrane underlies mycobacterial cording.
items.abstract: Virulent mycobacteria grow into mechanically resilient serpentine cords, yet how individual cells coordinate growth, division, and adhesion to form cords remains unknown. Here, combining live-cell fluorescence microscopy with cryo-electron tomography, we show that snapping division generates a shared interbacterial membrane (IBM) between daughter cells, in which each bacterium contributes one leaflet continuous with the inner leaflet of the mycomembrane. During cord formation, the IBM extends laterally as the daughter cells align along a common axis, restricting the outer mycomembrane leaflet largely to the exterior. The increased IBM interleaflet spacing is consistent with the retention of trehalose mycolates in both leaflets. In Mycobacterium tuberculosis, an interleaflet density is associated with the secretion of phthiocerol dimycocerosate and ESX-1 substrates. Our results reveal a multi-bacterial membrane architecture that provides the structural basis for cording and for collective behaviors, including mechanical stability, molecular exchange, phage resistance, and the sequestration of surface-associated virulence factors within the cord interior.

items.title: Association between sleep health and ocular diseases: a population-based study.

sections.objective: The association between sleep health and ocular diseases among U.S. adults remains insufficiently understood.
sections.methods: Using publicly available data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2005-8, weighted restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, multivariable logistic regression, and subgroup analyses were performed to examine the associations of sleep health with the prevalence of ocular diseases, including glaucoma, cataract, age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy.
sections.results: A total of 5549 individuals were included, among whom 328 (5.91%) had glaucoma, 685 (12.34%) had cataract, 430 (7.75%) had AMD, and 1031 (18.60%) had diabetic retinopathy. A U-shaped relationship was observed between sleep duration and ocular diseases (glaucoma, cataracts, AMD, diabetic retinopathy) (all P for nonlinearity <0.05). It is evident that ocular disease risk decreases with increasing sleep duration, reaching the lowest risk around 7.0-8.0 h. Additionally, poor sleep patterns (abnormal sleep duration, trouble sleeping, sleep disorders) were risk factors for ocular disease.
sections.conclusion: In summary, the study observed a U-shaped association of sleep duration with the risk of glaucoma, cataract, AMD, and diabetic retinopathy. Both short and long sleep durations or poor sleep patterns increased the prevalence of ocular disease.

items.title: Choroidal volume and thickness associations with myopia and myopic maculopathy in the Aier-SERI High Myopia Adult Study.

sections.objective: To assess choroidal thickness and volume and their sectoral associations with axial length (AL), refractive error and myopic maculopathy in highly myopic adults.
sections.methods: Participants with high myopia (spherical equivalent [SE] ≤ - 5 dioptres [D]) underwent swept-source optical coherence tomography imaging. Volumetric choroidal segmentation was performed using deep learning and corrected for ocular magnification. Myopic maculopathy was assessed with META-PM grading. Choroidal thinning in dependence on AL or SE, and associations with myopic maculopathy, were evaluated across the Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) grid.
sections.results: 248 highly myopic participants with an age of 42.0 ± 6.7 (SD) years, SE of -7.7 ± 2.5 D, and AL of 26.6 ± 1.2 mm were included, with 111 (45%) having META-PM grading≥1 and 30 (12%) with myopic macular degeneration (MMD). Thinner choroids were associated with longer AL or more myopic SE, and with more severe myopic maculopathy. Odds ratios (OR) of any myopic maculopathy, including tessellation and MMD per 25 µm of global choroidal thinning were 2.29 (95% CI 1.81-2.88), 3.15 (95% CI 2.23-4.46) and 3.11 (95% CI 2.28-4.26) for the central, nasal and mean ETDRS subfields compared to eyes without maculopathy. For MMD, the OR was 2.92 (95% CI 1.78-4.81), 6.07 (95% CI 3.,13, 11.77) and 4.44 (95% CI 2.47-7.97), respectively.
sections.conclusion: Choroidal thicknesses and volumes were associated with AL or SE. Thinner choroidal measurements for the nasal and overall ETDRS show increased odds of myopic maculopathy compared to the central subfield. Comprehensive choroidal assessment may benefit evaluations of ocular health and risks of myopic degeneration.

items.title: Single-Stage Combined Lymphaticovenular Anastomosis, Vascularized Lymph Node Transfer, and Liposuction for Gynecologic Cancer-Related Lower Extremity Lymphedema.

sections.objective: Secondary lymphedema after gynecologic cancer treatment is a chronic, progressive condition characterized by lymphatic fluid stasis, fibrosis, and recurrent infections. Compared with single-modality procedures, the combination of physiological and debulking techniques is increasingly recognized as a promising therapeutic trend. Combining lymphaticovenular anastomosis, vascularized lymph node transfer, and liposuction in a single operation(3L integrated techniques) may address both fluid and solid components, but clinical evidence remains limited. This study evaluated the 2 years outcomes of this integrated approach.
sections.methods: This retrospective observational study included 44 patients with International Society of Lymphology stage II or III gynecologic cancer-related lower-extremity lymphedema. All patients underwent single-stage lymphaticovenular anastomosis, vascularized lymph node transfer, and liposuction. Affected-limb volume was assessed preoperatively and at 3 months and 2 years postoperatively. Cellulitis episodes and overall Lymphedema Quality of Life scores were assessed preoperatively and at 2 years. Lymphoscintigraphy, operative time, and perioperative complications were also evaluated.
sections.results: At 3 months, mean affected-limb volume reductions were 794.08 ± 346.85 mL in stage II and 1,115.90 ± 485.32 mL in stage III disease. At 2 years, the corresponding reductions were 1,378.49 ± 565.40 and 1,724.45 ± 566.34 mL. Median cellulitis episodes decreased from 1 to 0 in stage II and from 2 to 0 in stage III disease. Median overall quality-of-life scores increased from 5 to 7 and from 4 to 6, respectively. Postoperative radiotracer uptake at the lymph node transfer site was observed in 81.8% of patients, and 90.9% showed improved lymphatic drainage patterns. Median operative times were 5.75 hours for stage II and 7.45 hours for stage III disease. No major perioperative complications were recorded.
sections.conclusion: Single-stage integrated surgery was associated with sustained limb-volume reduction, fewer cellulitis episodes, and improved quality of life.

items.title: THE LITERATURE IS LARGER THAN THE EVIDENCE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW, COHORT-OVERLAP ANALYSIS, AND BIBLIOMETRIC APPRAISAL OF PHYSICIAN-MODIFIED ENDOGRAFTS.

sections.objective: Publication on physician-modified endografts (PMEGs) has grown rapidly. We examined whether this reflects an expanding evidence base or repeated publication from a limited number of clinical programs, and whether comparative studies support the comparisons they report.
sections.methods: We systematically reviewed PMEG publications in Scopus, Web of Science, and MEDLINE/PubMed through August 20, 2026, following PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, and BIBLIO, with a supplementary ClinicalTrials.gov search. Studies with ≥20 PMEG patients were rated across five exploratory evidence-maturity domains, assigned to inferred cohort-overlap families, and, when comparative, assessed with ROBINS-I for perioperative mortality. Analyses added during peer review are labeled post hoc; no comparative meta-analysis was performed. The review was retrospectively registered in OSF (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/A9YTB).
sections.results: Of 340 publications, 88.8% appeared from 2020 onward. Of 100 full texts assessed, 72 studies were included; 52 belonged to 12 multi-report families. Summed cohorts comprised 8,885 patient counts. Retaining one record per family gave 4,524 (50.9%); alternative family definitions gave 3,980 to 4,694 (44.8%-52.8%), and additionally excluding the two largest multicenter aggregates gave 2,706 (30.5%). These are documentary estimates, not verified counts of unique patients. No study rated high across all five maturity domains. All 16 comparative studies were at serious (n = 11) or critical (n = 5) risk of bias, chiefly from confounding by urgency, anatomy, or treatment era.
sections.conclusion: About half of the summed PMEG patient count in the published literature is independently attributable, and no comparative study achieves better than serious risk of bias because PMEG use is closely tied to urgency and device availability. Observational comparisons between PMEGs and company-manufactured devices should be read as comparisons of different clinical contexts rather than evidence of device equivalence. These findings do not question the clinical role of PMEGs. Standardized reporting of cohort overlap, indication, and surveillance would make future series independently interpretable.
sections.other: Clinicians, guideline writers, and regulators should read PMEG series as belonging to identifiable programs rather than as independent replications, and should not interpret observational comparisons of PMEGs with company-manufactured devices as simple device comparisons, because treatment allocation is frequently inseparable from urgency and device availability.

items.title: Clinicopathologic and Dermoscopic Features of Thick Cutaneous Melanomas (Breslow >1.0 mm) as Prognostic Indicators of Metastatic Progression: A Retrospective Study of 290 Cases.

sections.objective: Dermoscopy is routinely used for melanoma diagnosis, but its prognostic value remains poorly defined, particularly in patients with thick melanoma. To identify dermoscopic features independently associated with metastatic progression in primary cutaneous melanomas thicker than 1 mm.
sections.methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study including 290 consecutive patients with primary cutaneous melanoma (Breslow thickness >1 mm). Clinical, histopathologic, and dermoscopic variables were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Predictive performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis.
sections.results: Ninety-nine patients (34.1%) developed metastatic disease during follow-up. Independent predictors of progression included sentinel lymph node positivity, more than three dermoscopic colors, blue-white veil, and atypical vascular structures. Conversely, pigment network, globules, and streaks/pseudopods were independently associated with a lower likelihood of progression. The integrated clinicopathologic-dermoscopic model demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy (area under the curve, 0.93).
sections.conclusion: Dermoscopic features provide prognostic information beyond established clinicopathologic factors and may improve risk stratification in patients with thick melanoma.
sections.other: Single-center retrospective design without external validation.

items.title: Impact of Steroid-sparing Immunosuppressants on Lung Function and Mortality in Fibrotic Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Evidence supporting steroid-sparing immunosuppressants (SSIs) in fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (f-HP) remains limited.
sections.methods: Following Cochrane and PRISMA 2020 guidance (PROSPERO CRD420261413825), we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar through May 2026 for studies of mycophenolate, azathioprine, methotrexate, leflunomide, tacrolimus, or cyclophosphamide. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and appraised studies using ROBINS-I, JBI, or Newcastle-Ottawa tools. DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models pooled percent-predicted FVC and DLCO changes and hazard ratios for death or lung transplantation. GRADE assessed certainty.
sections.results: Seventeen studies (1,341 patients) were included. SSIs were associated with modest FVC stabilization (13 studies; +1.11% predicted, 95% CI 0.37-1.84; I2=0%) and DLCO stabilization (9 studies; +3.73% predicted, 95% CI 2.56-4.90; I2=24%). The estimand-consistent mortality pool of two adjusted overall-effect studies demonstrated no survival benefit and could not exclude harm (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.86-2.26; I2=0%). Certainty was low for lung function and very low for mortality. Descriptive benefit was concentrated in patients with identifiable antigens and less radiologic fibrosis.
sections.conclusion: Modest lung-function stabilization largely reflects uncontrolled within-group changes, not definitive disease modification. Controlled survival evidence remains insufficient; adequately powered randomized trials are needed.
sections.other: Do SSIs improve lung function or survival in adults with f-HP?

items.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and eye-related outcomes - A systematic review and meta-analysis. OphthoEvidence Report 1.

sections.methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials followed PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to August 2025. Eligible trials compared any GLP-1 RAs with placebo, standard care or active comparator for patients with any clinical indication. Pairs of reviewers conducted study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessments independently. We performed random-effects meta-analyses and rated certainty of evidence using GRADE.
sections.results: A total of 142 trials enrolling 172,050 participants met eligibility criteria. Moderate to high certainty evidence suggests GLP-1 RAs probably increase the risk of diabetic retinopathy (odds ratio (OR) 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.15 [1.03-1.28]), vitreous hemorrhage (OR 95% CI 1.64 [1.08-2.49]), need for retinal procedures (OR 95% CI 1.37 [1.07-1.75]), total retinal vascular disorders (OR 95% CI 1.54 [1.12-2.12]), including retinal vascular occlusion (2.33 [1.22-4.45]). High certainty evidence also showed GLP-1 RAs reduce glaucoma risk (0.58 [0.34-0.99]). Moderate certainty evidence suggests GLP-1 RAs likely have little to no effect on the risk of cataract (0.95 [0.85 - 1.06]) and retinal detachment (1.40 [0.87 - 2.27]). We are very uncertain about the effects of GLP-1 RAs on age-related macular degeneration (0.91 [0.15-5.45]) and ischemic optic neuropathy (2.19 [0.49-9.85]). Results were consistent in sensitivity analyses restricted to placebo- or standard-care-controlled trials, and follow-up duration did not modify the effects for any outcome.
sections.conclusion: Moderate- to high-certainty evidence suggests that GLP-1 RAs likely result in an increase in the risk of selected retinal events, but reduce the risk of glaucoma. Given the low absolute incidence of these events, clinicians can counsel patients that the ocular risks of GLP-1 RAs are small and likely outweighed by their cardiometabolic benefits, while advising early monitoring for retinal events in those with diabetes or pre-existing retinopathy.
sections.other: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials examining the association between glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) use across all clinical indications and ocular outcomes. GLP-1 RAs are widely used to manage diabetes, obesity, and other cardiometabolic conditions. However, their effects on diabetic retinopathy and other ocular outcomes remain uncertain.

items.title: Occupational Disparities in Cardiovascular Risk and Management in Contemporary China.

sections.objective: Although occupational disparities in cardiovascular health are increasingly recognized, a comprehensive understanding of cardiovascular health across contemporary occupational contexts-particularly in rapidly transitioning economies-remains limited. This study aimed to characterize geographic and occupational patterns of cardiovascular risk, risk-factor management, and potential prevention opportunities among employed adults in contemporary China.
sections.methods: In this nationwide cross-sectional study, we analyzed 1,421,390 employees aged 20 to 65 years who underwent health examinations at 167 centers across 24 provinces in China between 2021 and 2023. Eighteen occupations were defined based on participants' employer registration and industry affiliation, and were classified into primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors, with the tertiary sector further subclassified into modern, public, and life services. Age- and sex-standardized prevalence of coronary heart disease (CHD) and cardiometabolic risk factors was estimated, along with age- and sex-standardized rates of treatment and control for hypertension and diabetes, and treatment for hypercholesterolemia and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) control. Ten-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk was calculated using the Prediction for ASCVD Risk in China model. We then assessed changes in the proportion of individuals classified as having moderate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk under simulated scenarios that set elevated blood pressure and total cholesterol to target levels and current smoking to noncurrent smoking and compared these reductions across occupations.
sections.results: The mean age of participants was 33.8 years, and 53.4% were male. Overall, the age- and sex-standardized prevalence of CHD was 1.33% (95% CI: 1.29%-1.37%) and demonstrated a pronounced north-south gradient (P < 0.001), with the highest in the North and the lowest in the South. Cardiometabolic risk factors also exhibited a similar geographic distribution. Employees in modern service sectors exhibited the lowest age- and sex-standardized prevalence of CHD and cardiometabolic risk factors, particularly those in "information transmission, software, and information technology," whereas the highest burdens were concentrated in the secondary sector, especially in "production and supply of electricity, heat power, gas and water." The age- and sex-standardized rates of treatment and control were 29.5% and 20.8% for hypertension, 36.6% and 21.9% for diabetes, and 17.0% and 9.5% for hypercholesterolemia treatment and LDL-C control, respectively. Modern services in the tertiary sector had the lowest treatment rates for all 3 cardiometabolic conditions and the lowest control rates for hypertension and LDL-C. Among individuals aged ≥35 years without prior ASCVD, 23.3% were classified as having moderate-to-high 10-year ASCVD risk, with marked occupational variation, highest in "agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery" (30.4%) and lowest in "service to advanced manufacturing" (14.7%). Simulated control of elevated blood pressure, hypercholesterolemia, and current smoking revealed substantial occupational variation in potential ASCVD risk reduction.
sections.conclusion: Occupational context may provide a practical framework for identifying patterns of cardiovascular risk, management gaps, and prevention opportunities among China's working population. Despite lower observed disease burden, modern occupational sectors showed suboptimal risk-factor management, whereas simulated ASCVD risk reductions varied across occupations, highlighting distinct prevention needs and opportunities across occupational contexts.

items.title: Sotatercept Improves Right Heart Mechanics Despite Reduced Myocardial Contractility in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: A Prospective Exercise Hemodynamic Study.

sections.objective: The right ventricular (RV) response to pressure overload is a crucial determinant of outcomes in pulmonary arterial (PA) hypertension. Sotatercept improves clinical outcomes, but its effects on the right ventricle have been inconsistent. We evaluated the effects of sotatercept on load-independent measures of RV contractility, RV-PA coupling, and right heart deformation at rest and exertion in patients with PA hypertension.
sections.methods: In this prospective trial among participants with PA hypertension recruited between July 2024 and May 2025, we performed simultaneous echocardiography and invasive pressure measurements during rest and exercise to evaluate changes in RV contractility (end-systolic elastance [Ees]), afterload (PA elastance [Ea]), RV-PA coupling (ratio of arterial Ea to Ees), and right heart deformation, including RV and right atrial strain, before and after 24 weeks of sotatercept using mixed models.
sections.results: Among 30 participants (n=21; 70% female; mean age, 49.3 years [SD 13.5]), sotatercept decreased PA Ea. These changes were associated with reduced RV contractility, PA pulsatility index, and the maximal rate of RV pressure increase over time (dP/dtmax; P<0.001 for all). The decrease in Ees was associated with a decrease in PA Ea (r=+0.70 [95% CI, +0.44 to +0.85]; P<0.0001) with preserved RV-PA coupling (mean difference, +0.08 [95% CI, -0.11 to +0.26]; P=0.42). Although systolic indices measured at the base of the right ventricle (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion and systolic velocity of the lateral tricuspid annulus) decreased after sotatercept use, there was an increase in RV free wall-dependent systolic indices, including resting and exercise RV free wall strain (mean difference, +6.2% [95% CI, +4.5 to +7.8]; P<0.0001) and fractional area change (P=0.0001). Beyond the right ventricle, there was also improved right atrial filling and contractile performance across rest and exercise (P<0.0001 for all).
sections.conclusion: Sotatercept decreases RV contractility in proportion to reduced afterload, while preserving the RV-PA coupling relationship. Despite decreased RV contractility, global measures of right heart performance, such as RV free wall strain and RA strain, improve, alongside redistribution of RV deformation from annular motion to free wall shortening. These data suggest that sotatercept causes an energetically favorable reduction in resting RV contractility to match the lower afterload, which does not appear physiologically detrimental when considering the concurrent improvement in RV free wall contractile mechanics and exertional right heart reserve.

items.title: ALKBH5-Dependent m6A Demethylation Promotes Cardiac Aging Through SLC38A3 Reduction and Glutamine Metabolic Alteration.

sections.objective: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification has been linked to various types of physiological and pathological bioprocesses. However, the exact role of m6A mRNA methylation in cardiac aging is largely unknown. Here, we show that ALKBH5 (alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase AlkB homolog 5), an m6A demethylase, plays a critical role in regulating cardiac aging.
sections.methods: Physiologically aged and paraquat-induced mouse models of cardiac aging as well as senescent cardiomyocyte cell cultures were used to evaluate the expression and function of ALKBH5 in cardiac aging. The adeno-associated virus serotype 9 and small interfering RNAs were used to modulate ALKBH5 expression in vivo and in vitro, respectively. Cardiac aging and function were evaluated by histological analysis, immunostaining, and echocardiography. Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing and functional screening were performed to identify potential targets of ALKBH5 in regulating cardiac aging.
sections.results: ALKBH5 expression was increased in aged hearts and in senescent-like cardiomyocyte models, accompanied by reduced m6A levels. ALKBH5 knockdown attenuated senescence-associated phenotypes in cardiomyocytes and reduced aging-associated cardiac remodeling and dysfunction in physiological aging and paraquat-challenged mouse models when adeno-associated virus serotype 9-short hairpin RNA targeting ALKBH5 gene was delivered beginning in young adulthood, whereas ALKBH5 knockdown initiated in already aged hearts did not reverse established phenotypes. Mechanistically, ALKBH5-dependent m6A demethylation reduced the expression of SLC38A3 (solute carrier family 38-member 3), which suggested a YTHDC2 (YTH domain-containing protein 2)-dependent mechanism, thereby contributing to reduced glutamine accumulation, impaired mitochondrial homeostasis, and increased oxidative stress. SLC38A3 overexpression attenuated aging-associated cardiac phenotypes in vivo. In addition, glutamine supplementation reduced senescence-associated and cardiac aging-related phenotypes.
sections.conclusion: Our study demonstrates that ALKBH5-SLC38A3 axis is an important regulator of m6A-linked, glutamine-associated pathways in aging-related cardiac phenotypes. These findings support a role for ALKBH5 as a contributor to cardiac aging-associated remodeling and dysfunction and suggest this pathway as a candidate target for further mechanistic and translational investigation.

items.title: Asb2-KIF11 Axis Protects Against Heart Failure by Restoring Lysosomal Distribution and Mitochondrial Homeostasis.

sections.objective: Heart failure remains a leading cause of mortality globally, driven by persistent mitochondrial dysfunction and maladaptive cardiac hypertrophy. Although impaired autophagic flux contributes to cardiac deterioration, the precise molecular mechanisms are still unclear. The ubiquitin-proteasome system serves as a critical regulator linking protein ubiquitination to autophagic flux and mitochondrial homeostasis. Asb2 (ankyrin repeat-containing protein with suppressor of cytokine signaling box 2), a muscle-specific E3 ubiquitin ligase essential for embryonic cardiogenesis, is uncharacterized in adult cardiac homeostasis and disease pathogenesis.
sections.methods: Male mice with inducible cardiomyocyte-specific Asb2 knockout were generated to investigate Asb2's role in cardiac remodeling. Adeno-associated virus 9-mediated cardiomyocyte-specific Asb2 overexpression and KIF11 (kinesin family member 11) downregulation were used in transverse aortic constriction-induced hypertrophy and aging models. RNA sequencing, metabolite profiling, and mass spectrometry were used to assess the molecular mechanism by which Asb2 regulates cardiac metabolism and hypertrophy.
sections.results: Asb2β expression was significantly reduced in multiple forms of human cardiomyopathy and in hypertrophic murine hearts. Inducible Asb2 deletion in adult male mice led to the spontaneous development of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure, accompanied by progressive accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria and metabolic dysregulation. Mechanistically, Asb2 deficiency impaired ubiquitin-mediated degradation of KIF11, causing aberrant peripheral lysosomal redistribution and disrupting autophagosome-lysosome fusion, which resulted in impaired late-stage autophagic flux and metabolic disturbances. Notably, therapeutic restoration of Asb2 expression via adeno-associated virus 9-mediated delivery attenuated pressure overload-induced and age-related cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure. Moreover, both genetic and pharmacological inhibition of KIF11 effectively restored autophagic flux and mitochondrial homeostasis, thereby reversing pathological cardiac remodeling in Asb2-deficient hearts and transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction.
sections.conclusion: Asb2 is a novel regulator of mitochondrial quality control in cardiomyocytes via KIF11-mediated lysosomal redistribution. Targeting the Asb2-KIF11 axis may be a promising strategy for improving mitochondrial homeostasis and cardiomyocyte function in chronic heart failure.

items.title: Protocol-Based Implementation of Early Intensive Lipid Management After Acute Coronary Syndrome: The BRIDGE Trial.

sections.objective: Although guideline-recommended intensive lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) reduces recurrent cardiovascular events after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), timely implementation of intensive LLT and achievement of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) target remain suboptimal in routine clinical practice. The purpose of this study was to determine whether a protocol-based implementation strategy improves timely achievement of guideline-recommended LDL-C target after ACS.
sections.methods: We conducted a cluster-randomized trial involving patients with ACS. Ten centers were randomly assigned 1:1 to protocol-based or standard lipid management. In the protocol-based group, LLT was initiated or intensified during the index hospitalization according to a prespecified algorithm based on baseline LLT status and LDL-C levels using high-intensity statins, ezetimibe, and PCSK9 inhibitors. LDL-C was reassessed at 4 weeks, with treatment escalation when indicated. In the protocol-based group, an LDL-C level of approximately 55 mg/dL was used as the protocol-specified operational threshold for intensification, whereas LDL-C <70 mg/dL was the treatment goal in both groups. The primary and key secondary endpoints were achievement of LDL-C <70 mg/dL and <55 mg/dL at 6 months, respectively.
sections.results: Between November 2024 and July 2025, 330 patients were enrolled, and 329 patients comprised the study population after 1 patient withdrew consent. The primary efficacy analysis included 315 patients with complete 6-month LDL-C data. Baseline characteristics were balanced between groups. The mean age was 69 years, 18% were women, and the median LDL-C level was 110 mg/dL. At 6 months, LDL-C <70 mg/dL was achieved in 86.4% vs 73.7% (between-group difference, 12.6 percentage points [95% CI: 3.8-21.5 percentage points]; P = 0.005); the corresponding difference was 12.8 percentage points (95% CI: -2.0 to 27.6 percentage points; P = 0.08) in a hospital-level sensitivity analysis. Similar findings were observed for LDL-C <55 mg/dL (60.8% vs 34.5%; between-group difference, 26.3 percentage points [95% CI: 18.5-34.0 percentage points]; P < 0.001). At 6 months, use of high-intensity statins, ezetimibe, and PCSK9 inhibitors was higher in the protocol-based group.
sections.conclusion: A protocol-based implementation strategy for early intensive LLT significantly improved achievement of the guideline-recommended LDL-C target after ACS. These findings support a structured, algorithm-based care pathway to facilitate timely initiation and intensification of LLT and improve implementation of guideline-recommended lipid management in routine clinical practice. (Brief and Protocol-Based Intensive Lipid Management in Patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome; jRCT1020240029).

items.title: Cumulative Benefit With Evolocumab in Patients With No Prior Myocardial Infarction or Stroke in the VESALIUS-CV Study.

sections.objective: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibition with evolocumab reduced the risk of a first major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) in patients at high cardiovascular risk with no prior myocardial infarction (MI) or stroke in the VESALIUS-CV (Effect of Evolocumab in Patients at High Cardiovascular Risk Without Prior Myocardial Infarction or Stroke) trial. Recurrent MACE is common and important to patients, clinicians, and health care systems. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effect of evolocumab on total (first and subsequent) MACE.
sections.methods: The VESALIUS-CV trial randomized patients with qualifying atherosclerosis or high-risk diabetes, no prior MI or stroke, and a low-density lipoprotein cholesterol ≥90 mg/dL on optimized lipid-lowering therapy to evolocumab or placebo. The dual primary endpoints were a composite of coronary heart disease death, MI, ischemic stroke, or ischemia-driven arterial revascularization (4-point [4-P] MACE) and 3-point (3-P) MACE (not including ischemia-driven arterial revascularization). In this prespecified analysis, all dual primary endpoint events (first and subsequent) were analyzed using negative binomial regression models.
sections.results: Among 12,257 patients followed for a median of 4.6 years, there were 1,654 first 4-P MACE and 1,107 subsequent events (67% more) for 2,761 total events. There were 779 first 3-P MACE and 146 subsequent events (19% more) for 925 total events. Evolocumab reduced the rate of first 4-P MACE by 19% (HR: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.73-0.89; P < 0.0001), was associated with a reduction of subsequent events by 25% (incidence rate ratio [IRR]: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.61-0.91), and reduced total events by 20% (IRR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.71-0.90; P = 0.0002). Likewise for 3-P MACE, evolocumab reduced the rate of first events by 25% (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.65-0.86; P < 0.0001), was associated with a reduction of subsequent events by 37% (IRR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.42-0.94) and reduced total events by 27% (IRR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.63-0.86; P = 0.0001). Based on annualized incidence rate differences over the full follow-up period, evolocumab was projected to prevent 31 first and 24 subsequent 4-P MACE, for 55 total events per 1,000 patients over 5 years (95% CI: for the total-event difference: 36-74). The corresponding estimates for 3-P MACE were 20 first and 5 subsequent events, for 25 total events per 1,000 patients over 5 years (95% CI: for the total event difference: 15-37). Results were consistent across key subgroups, including by statin intensity and presence of qualifying atherosclerosis.
sections.conclusion: A substantial proportion of patients experiencing a cardiovascular event had more than 1 event. The addition of evolocumab reduced the total number of MACE, providing support for the role of intensive low-density lipoprotein cholesterol lowering to prevent first and subsequent MACE in patients at high cardiovascular risk and no prior MI or stroke. (Effect of Evolocumab in Patients at High Cardiovascular Risk Without Prior Myocardial Infarction or Stroke [VESALIUS-CV]; NCT03872401).

items.title: Low Ventricular Chamber Stiffness Identifies a High-Risk Eccentric Remodeling Phenotype in the Fontan Circulation: A FORCE Registry Analysis.

sections.objective: Rising end-diastolic pressure in patients with a Fontan circulation has led to the hypothesis that circulatory failure is driven by progressive ventricular stiffening. However, end-diastolic pressure is influenced by loading conditions and extracardiac constraint and may not accurately reflect chamber stiffness. We aimed to characterize ventricular chamber stiffness using the end-diastolic pressure-volume relationship and examine its clinical and prognostic significance in patients with a Fontan circulation.
sections.methods: In the FORCE registry (Fontan Outcomes Registry Using Clinical Examinations), chamber stiffness was quantified with the exponential coefficient β derived from single-beat end-diastolic pressure-volume relationship reconstruction using paired catheterization and cardiovascular magnetic resonance data. The β values were standardized as body surface area- and sex-based Z scores and related to clinical characteristics, ventricular remodeling, and a composite adverse outcome (death, transplantation listing, sustained atrial or ventricular arrhythmias, protein-losing enteropathy, or plastic bronchitis).
sections.results: Among 814 patients (median age, 14.7 years), median β was 0.034 mL-1 (0.025-0.046). Lower β Z score was associated with dominant right ventricle, eccentric remodeling with reduced ejection fraction, increased collateral flow and intracardiac recirculation, greater symptom burden, and higher arrhythmia prevalence, despite similar filling pressures. Over a median follow-up of 2.7 years (0.9-6.1 years), lower β Z score independently predicted adverse outcomes (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.30 per 1-SD decrease [95% CI 1.04-1.61]). A β Z score 103 mL/m2 showed similarly modest discrimination for adverse outcomes overall (area under the curve, 0.59), with greater discrimination in dominant right ventricles.
sections.conclusion: Contrary to prevailing assumptions, lower rather than higher chamber stiffness was associated with adverse Fontan outcomes, identifying a high-compliance phenotype characterized by ventricular dilation and eccentric remodeling. These findings suggest that, in the contemporary FORCE cohort, Fontan failure might be more closely associated with this remodeling phenotype than with progressive stiffening.

items.title: Effect of Aficamten vs Metoprolol on Cardiac Biomarkers in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.

sections.objective: Biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM) may change with therapy. The aim of this study was to examine biomarker responses to aficamten vs metoprolol monotherapy in patients with oHCM in the randomized MAPLE-HCM (Phase 3 Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aficamten Compared to Metoprolol Succinate in Adults With Symptomatic oHCM) trial and assess if changes parallel treatment effects.
sections.methods: Differences in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) from baseline to end of therapy were compared by treatment.
sections.results: Participants receiving aficamten (n = 88) or metoprolol (n = 87) were generally well matched for baseline characteristics. After 24 weeks, geometric mean NT-proBNP decreased by 73% with aficamten but increased by 42% with metoprolol (treatment effect -81% [-85% to -76%]; P < 0.001). Mean hs-cTnI decreased by 43% with aficamten and by 17% with metoprolol (treatment effect -28% [-41% to -13%]; P = 0.001); both biomarkers reverted to baseline after washout. Regardless of treatment, the correlation between changes in biomarkers was significant for NT-proBNP and peak oxygen uptake (-0.42; P < 0.001) and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS) (-0.26; P < 0.001) and between changes in hs-cTnI and KCCQ-CSS (-1.9; P = 0.013) but not peak oxygen uptake (-0.11; P = 0.22). When considering treatment, there were significant correlations between improvements in NT-proBNP and Valsalva left ventricular outflow tract gradient (LVOT-G) (r = +0.25; P = 0.02) and the ratio between early transmitral filling and early diastolic tissue Doppler velocity (r = +0.50; P = 0.001) with aficamten. Correlations between improvements in hs-cTnI and Valsalva LVOT-G (r = +0.17; P = 0.03) and maximal left ventricular wall thickness (r = +0.25; P = 0.001) were observed with aficamten.
sections.conclusion: Aficamten treatment resulted in lower NT-proBNP and hs-cTnI vs metoprolol. Reduction in NT-proBNP correlated with improved exercise capacity, LVOT-G, and health status. These results provide mechanistic insights regarding the benefit of aficamten over metoprolol in MAPLE-HCM. (Phase 3 Trial to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Aficamten Compared to Metoprolol Succinate in Adults With Symptomatic oHCM [MAPLE-HCM]; NCT05767346).

items.title: Highly selective visual circuits in mouse frontal cortex.
items.abstract: It is thought that elementary stimulus encoding happens primarily in the sensory cortex. We found that frontal cortex neurons in awake mice show highly selective visual spatial receptive fields, akin to the visual cortex. These neurons were most sensitive to binocular visual space, required retinotopically aligned V1 input and sent functional axonal feedback throughout the visual cortex, particularly binocular V1. This reveals a cortex-wide circuit suitable for selective feedback control of spatial vision.

items.title: Modular mRNA-encoded helper proteins enhance DNA delivery.
items.abstract: DNA delivery is limited by inefficient nuclear translocation and restrictive intracellular environments. Here we present mRNA-enhanced DNA delivery (MEND), a system that codelivers mRNA-encoded helper proteins to actively prime cells for enhanced DNA processing. We demonstrate three classes of MEND proteins: DNA translocators, host modulators and immune dampeners. MEND's modular framework boosts transgene expression across various delivery vehicles and DNA formats in vitro and in vivo with LNP delivery.

items.title: Highly accurate non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic and polygenic diseases from spent medium.
items.abstract: Traditional preimplantation genetic testing for in vitro fertilization (IVF) requires invasive trophectoderm biopsy, which may harm the embryo. Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) utilizing cell-free DNA from spent embryo culture medium (SCM) has been attempted, but trace DNA content, maternal cell contamination and high allele drop-out rates are barriers. Here we report an niPGT methodology achieving high diagnostic accuracy among reportable samples across diverse embryo and disease contexts. Reengineered linear whole-genome amplification (scm-LIANTI) with an extremely low error rate is followed by application of a Bayesian algorithm designed to determine which parental haplotypes are inherited at disease-causing sites. Among 191 SCM samples from 29 families affected by rare monogenic disorders, our method amplified all samples and enabled diagnosis of 220 out of 277 pathogenic alleles. All diagnoses (220/220) were concordant with invasive biopsy control. For select embryos, personalized genome-wide genotyping enabled exploratory polygenic risk assessment for type 2 diabetes. Our methodology requires no modification to IVF workflows and represents a key technological advance towards scalable, accurate and safe niPGT for both monogenic and polygenic diseases.

items.title: Artificial intelligence literacy among health-care professionals: a systematic review of reported competency needs.
items.abstract: Widespread calls for artificial intelligence (AI) literacy among health-care professionals have outpaced evidence on the AI information that should be taught and prioritised. We conducted a systematic review of studies published until Feb 12, 2026, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (protocol preregistered on Open Science Framework). 70 studies comprising 42 empirical and 28 perspective or commentary papers from 21 countries were included after screening 4095 records. Among empirical studies, conceptual understanding of the meaning of AI (AI fundamentals; 88·1%), application of ethical thinking to AI use in clinical practice (ethical reasoning; 71·4%), and knowledge of existing AI tools (tools and applications; 71·4%) were the most prevalent competency domains. Perspective papers showed a similar pattern, with comparatively less emphasis on tools and applications. In 20 studies that asked students and health-care professionals to rank competencies by importance, tools and applications and the ability to evaluate AI before adoption (pre-adoption evaluation) ranked the highest. These findings inform a candidate foundation for the development of clinical AI competency.

items.title: Association of a Biphasic Oxygen Protocol with Treatment in Retinopathy of Prematurity by Race.

sections.objective: In recent retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) studies, biphasic oxygen protocols have been associated with a decreased proportion of infants who develop severe ROP. As differences by race in both ROP severity and pulse oximetry have been described, this study considered whether a biphasic oxygen protocol might also have a differential impact by race.
sections.methods: Retrospective before and after cohort study. This study compared ROP treatment by race, before and after implementation of a biphasic oxygen protocol. To compare differences in the effect of the oxygen protocol by race, or an effect modification by race, an interaction term tested whether the association between time period and treatment differed by race. Black infants were compared to infants of other races. Analyses were adjusted for gestational age, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, and intraventricular hemorrhage.
sections.results: Overall, 48 of 903 infants (5.3%) received ROP treatment for Type 1 ROP. Among Black infants, the proportion treated decreased after the biphasic oxygen protocol implementation (5.8% vs 1.65%, p = 0.025). The proportion treated did not differ for infants of other races (p = 0.693). After adjustment for neonatal comorbidities, the effect of the change in oxygen protocol on Type 1 ROP was significantly more pronounced among Black infants compared to non-Black infants (aOR 0.027, 95% CI 0.002-0.351, p = 0.006).
sections.conclusion: This differential association should be interpreted cautiously and may reflect differences in oximetry performance, oxygen exposure, or other temporal factors. Future studies might consider prospective measurements of skin pigmentation to validate this data.
sections.other: Infants screened for ROP from 2016 to 2023, before and after biphasic oxygen protocol implementation in July 2021. ROP treatment (Type 1 ROP).

items.title: Strengthening public health research on urban green and blue space interventions: the GIFT framework for theory development.
items.abstract: Urban green and blue space (UGBS) interventions are increasingly promoted as strategies to improve population health and reduce health inequities. Yet the evidence needed to guide policy and practice remains difficult to interpret because evaluations often report mixed findings, with limited understanding of how and why health effects vary. This partly reflects a lack of explicit programme theory specifying how interventions are expected to generate health outcomes, and why effects might differ across population groups and contexts. Without a robust, evidence-informed understanding of how interventions produce effects, policy and practice might rely on insufficiently tested assumptions about expected health benefits from UGBS interventions. In this Viewpoint, we introduce the green and blue space intervention framework for theory development (GIFT), which supports the development of programme theory for UGBS intervention studies. GIFT was developed through a survey, workshop, and iterative feedback involving 25 international researchers. It provides guiding questions covering intervention components, pathways and mechanisms, population variation, contextual conditions, outcomes, and timescales. By providing a shared approach to articulating how UGBS interventions are expected to work, GIFT can support more theory-informed evaluations, improve interpretation of findings, strengthen judgements about transferability, and generate more actionable evidence for effective and equitable urban green and blue space interventions.

items.title: Pretreatment HIV-1 drug resistance among treatment-naive people living with HIV in Türkiye (TURHIV-DR): a nationwide, retrospective study.

sections.objective: Surveillance of pretreatment HIV-1 drug resistance has become increasingly important in the era of integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-based antiretroviral therapy, particularly in countries with increasing HIV-1 subtype diversity. We aimed to characterise pretreatment HIV-1 drug resistance, temporal trends, and subtype diversity among treatment-naive people living with HIV in Türkiye.
sections.methods: In this nationwide, retrospective, multicentre study, we included treatment-naive adults (aged 18 years and older) undergoing baseline HIV-1 genotypic resistance testing at the National HIV/AIDS Confirmation and Viral Hepatitis Reference Laboratory between Aug 1, 2016, and Dec 31, 2024.
