sections.objective: Current ESC/ERS guidelines suggest that initial monotherapy should be considered for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with cardiopulmonary comorbidities. However, data on the cardiopulmonary physiological responses to treatment in this subset of patients remain limited. Our aim was to evaluate the cardiopulmonary exercise and gas exchange response to treatment in patients with PAH and cardiopulmonary comorbidities.
sections.methods: Incident treatment-naïve patients with idiopathic, heritable, drug/toxins-induced, HIV, and connective tissue disease-associated PAH were analysed at first follow-up. Comorbid patients were defined based on the presence of ≥3 risk factors among obesity (body mass index ≥30 Kg/m2), systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, smoking history and transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide (TLCO) <45% predicted.
sections.results: A total of 178 patients were included: 52 with comorbidities and 126 without. Comorbid patients were older, predominantly male, and had a lower baseline exercise capacity, despite comparable hemodynamics. There were no differences in therapy, with approximately one third of patients receiving combination therapy in both groups at the time of reassessment. At follow-up, both groups demonstrated similar adjusted improvements from baseline in peak oxygen uptake, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency and 6-minute walk distance, all known prognostic markers in PAH. However, comorbid patients exhibited a significantly worse gas exchange response to treatment, with an adjusted widening of the peak A-a gradient of +1.23 kPa compared with -0.35 kPa in patients without comorbidities (p=0.003).
sections.conclusion: PAH patients with and without cardiopulmonary comorbidities achieve similar improvements in exercise capacity after treatment. However, the worse gas exchange response to exercise among comorbid patients warrants caution, careful monitoring and further research to confirm this finding.
sections.other: Do patients with PAH and a cardiopulmonary phenotype display a worse exercise capacity and gas exchange response to treatment?

items.title: Real-World Outcomes of Long-Acting Beta-Agonist Add-On Therapy to Inhaled Corticosteroids in Preschool Children with Asthma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.

sections.objective: The role of long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) add-on therapy to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in preschool children with asthma remains uncertain. Although ICS+LABA is an established step-up strategy, data in children younger than 6 years are limited.
sections.methods: and Methods: This retrospective comparative effectiveness study used the TriNetX research network, a multicenter electronic health record database. Children aged ≤6 years with asthma treated with ICS+LABA were compared with propensity-matched children treated with ICS alone (n≈12,100 per cohort). To account for treatment timing and the age-related effects on asthma severity and incidence, analyses were conducted using two index definitions: asthma diagnosis with LABA initiation within 12 months, and the time of LABA initiation itself. Outcomes included systemic corticosteroid exposure, bronchodilator use, ED visits/hospitalizations, pneumonia, fractures, and gastroenteritis.
sections.results: When indexed at asthma diagnosis, ICS+LABA was associated with higher hazards of systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.32-1.43), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.36-1.46), and pneumonia (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.28-1.52) compared to ICS alone. When reindexed to LABA initiation, these associations were attenuated, but not eliminated: systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.09-1.18), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.13-1.21), and pneumonia (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02-1.22). Direct comparison of the ICS+LABA cohort across index definitions showed lower rates of asthma-related outcomes after LABA initiation. Findings were similar in unmatched analyses, and in sensitivity analyses by younger age, later follow-up, Bayesian analysis and LABA type.
sections.conclusion: In young children selected for ICS+LABA escalation, excess morbidity was greatest compared to ICS alone before LABA initiation and attenuated after LABA initiation. These findings may provide real-world evidence for ICS+LABA effectiveness in a selected group of preschool children with uncontrolled asthma and the basis for future prospective studies.
sections.other: In children ≤6 years with asthma, how were morbidity outcomes associated with ICS+LABA therapy compared with ICS alone, before and after LABA initiation?

items.title: Transcarotid Artery Revascularization in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis Demonstrates Excellent Outcomes: A Decade Review of Three Stroke Centers.

sections.objective: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers.
sections.methods: Retrospective cohort study. We analyzed CEA and TCAR procedures for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis from January 2017 through February 2026 across three institutions. One-to-one nearest-neighbor propensity score matching was performed without replacement. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using the exact McNemar test. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Cox regression with robust variance estimates. Fine-Gray regression was used to treat death as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes.
sections.results: The final cohort included 889 procedures, 750 CEAs and 139 TCARs. Matching yielded 136 balanced pairs. No ipsilateral stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), myocardial infarction (MI), or death occurred within 30 days after TCAR, and no 30-day outcome differed significantly between matched groups. In adjusted analyses of the full cohort, TCAR was associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.31), stroke or death (aHR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.13-2.36), and the composite of TIA, stroke, MI, or death (aHR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.11-2.24). After matching, these associations did not reach statistical significance. Median follow-up in the matched cohort was 4.0 years. Long-term neurologic outcomes also did not differ significantly. Restenosis did not differ significantly (subdistribution HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 0.62-3.30; P = 0.399), and one reintervention occurred in each matched group.
sections.conclusion: Among selected asymptomatic patients, TCAR had low perioperative event rates. After matching, no significant differences from CEA were detected in long-term neurologic outcomes, mortality, composite outcomes, restenosis, or reintervention, while late MI remained higher after TCAR. These findings support TCAR as an attractive revascularization option when CEA is less suitable.

items.title: When Hip Pain Is Vascular: Internal Iliac Artery Aneurysmal Lesion in Behçet's Disease Treated with a Covered Stent.
items.abstract: Behçet's disease is a chronic relapsing systemic vasculitis in which arterial involvement is less common than venous disease but carries substantial rupture risk. Internal iliac artery involvement is rare and may be overlooked because symptoms are often nonspecific. We report a 34-year-old man with established Behçet's disease referred from orthopaedic surgery after 2 to 3 months of right hip and deep gluteal pain initially considered musculoskeletal. Plain hip x-ray was unremarkable. Pelvic imaging demonstrated a right pelvic arterial lesion, and computed tomography angiography (CTA) confirmed a 57 mm saccular aneurysmal lesion arising from the right internal iliac artery. Inflammatory markers were elevated, and perioperative immunosuppression was optimized with rheumatology input. Endovascular repair was performed via contralateral left common femoral access using a 6 × 60 mm self-expanding covered stent graft across the diseased internal iliac segment, without adjunctive coil embolization. Completion angiography showed complete sac exclusion with preserved distal internal iliac flow. Recovery was uneventful. One-month CTA confirmed persistent exclusion and stent-graft patency, and the patient remained clinically asymptomatic at 12 months. This case highlights an orthopaedic mimic and supports carefully selected flow-preserving endovascular repair under immunosuppressive cover, with lifelong imaging surveillance to detect late complications in this inflammatory disease setting.Clinical ImpactInternal iliac artery aneurysmal lesions are rare manifestations of vascular Behçet's disease and may present with hip, buttock or groin pain due to deep pelvic mass effect, leading to initial orthopaedic referral and potential diagnostic delay. This case emphasizes the need to consider a vascular cause in Behçet's disease patients with unexplained persistent pelvic or hip pain, especially when plain radiographs are normal. It also illustrates a flow-preserving endovascular strategy using a covered stent graft to exclude the lesion while maintaining internal iliac artery patency. Because Behçet's disease is an inflammatory vasculitis, technical success alone is insufficient; perioperative immunosuppression and lifelong clinical and imaging surveillance remain central to management.

items.title: One-Year Results From the EMBRACE Registry Evaluating the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis during BEVAR for Complex Abdominal and Thoracoabdominal Aneurysms.

sections.objective: The stability of bridging stents is critical to ensure the effectiveness and safety of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA). The goal of this multicenter registry was to assess the clinical performance and safety of the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis (VBX Stent Graft) as a bridging stent in BEVAR.
sections.methods: The EMBRACE registry is a multicenter study across 14 European centers with retrospective enrollment and prospective follow-up. Patients were divided into BEVAR and fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) arms. This analysis reports the BEVAR cohort, which included patients receiving the VBX Stent Graft as a bridging stent for at least 1 visceral vessel. The primary endpoint was patient-level primary patency at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included technical success, reintervention, and target vessel patency assessed annually for up to 5 years. Secondary safety outcomes included major adverse events and aneurysm-related mortality.
sections.results: A total of 165 patients (69.1% male, mean age 72.5 ± 9 years) were enrolled, receiving 454 VBX Stent Grafts (26.0% celiac trunk, 28.9% superior mesenteric artery (SMA), 21.8% left renal, and 23.3% right renal artery). VBX Stent Graft technical success was 99.6%. Thirty-day mortality was 7.9%, with major adverse events in 15.2% (1.8% respiratory failure, 7.3% renal function deterioration, 0.6% bowel ischemia, 4.2% paraplegia, and 1.8% major stroke). Freedom from aneurysm-related mortality was 92.1% at 30 days and 90.2% at 1 year. Freedom from patient-level VBX-related reintervention was 91.7%. Patient-level primary patency and secondary patency were 97.7% and 98.5%, respectively. Freedom from target vessel instability at the patient level was 90.4%.
sections.conclusion: Short-term findings from this multicenter registry confirm that the VBX Stent Graft is a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR, demonstrating high technical success, excellent 1-year patency, and low rates of target vessel instability. Ongoing follow-up will evaluate mid-term durability.Clinical ImpactBridging stent performance is fundamental to the success of branched endovascular repair, yet multicenter, real-world data remain limited. This analysis from the EMBRACE registry demonstrates high technical reliability, excellent 1-year target vessel patency, and low rates of VBX Stent Graft-related reintervention. Technical failures were uncommon and were primarily associated with inadequate distal landing zones, highlighting the importance of procedural planning. These findings provide clinicians with contemporary evidence supporting the VBX Stent Graft as a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR and may inform procedural decision-making to optimize target vessel durability.

items.title: The effects of size and sex mismatch on kidney functional adaption following living donor kidney transplantation.

sections.objective: The remarkable functional adaption of transplanted kidneys is poorly understood. Conflicting results for donor-recipient body size and sex mismatches, and concerns for hyperfiltration injury are unresolved.
sections.methods: This single center, longitudinal cohort study of 194 living kidney transplantations evaluated changes in isotopic 9 9mTc-DTPA measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR) from side-specific donor function at implantation through 12-months after transplantation against multiple anthropometric parameters, sex mismatch, and pathological hyperfiltration.
sections.results: Donor kidney mGFR was predicted by younger age, male sex, and heavier body weight using multivariable analysis; and strongly influenced 12-month mGFR. Post-transplant relative and absolute mGFR changes were determined by donor and recipient body sizes (weight, body surface area, and body mass index were statistically interchangeable) and donor and recipient sex using multivariable analysis. mGFR adaption was greatest in smaller female donor kidneys transplanted into large male recipients, but negligible or negative for male kidneys into female recipients. The mGFR ratio significantly correlated with mismatch in donor-recipient body surface area (r=0.285) and body mass index (r=0.248). Absolute mGFR significantly increased with recipient lean body mass (r=0.425) but not total fat content using body composition analysis. Diabetes, fasting blood glucose, hemoglobin A1c, androgenic hormones, and hypertension were unrelated. Evidence of significant maladaptive glomerular hyperfiltration assessed by albuminuria, glomerular pathology, percentage glomerulosclerosis, glomerulomegaly, transcription factor WT1 podocyte immunostaining, chronic interstitial fibrosis, and ultrastructural podocyte effacement at 12-months was absent. Death-censored graft survivals for five-, 10-, and 20-years after transplantation were excellent at 96.9%, 94.3%, and 80.8%, respectively.
sections.conclusion: mGFR following transplantation depends on input donor quality with adaption driven primarily by larger recipient body size mismatch and male sex. Functional adaption appears as a benign physiological response appropriately calibrated to individual recipient metabolic need without evidence of pathological hyperfiltration injury.

items.title: Complex Endovascular Repair for Genetically-Triggered Aortic Disease in Italy (CENTRAL Multicentric Registry).

sections.objective: The role of fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) in patients with genetically triggered aortic disease and connective tissue disorders (CTDs) remains controversial due to concerns regarding long-term durability and disease progression. This multicenter study aimed to evaluate early and mid-term outcomes of F/BEVAR in patients with CTD treated for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).
sections.methods: This retrospective multicenter study included all consecutive CTD patients with genetically triggered aortic disease undergoing F/BEVAR for TAAA between 2013 and 2024 at 12 Italian centers. Primary endpoints were technical and clinical success, early and mid-term survival, and major adverse events (MAEs). Secondary endpoints included target vessel instability and the need for reintervention. Survival and freedom from adverse events were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.
sections.results: A total of 45 CTD patients (62.2% male; mean age, 56.4 ± 11.7 years) were treated with F/BEVAR. Marfan syndrome was present in 80% of patients, and 68.9% were treated for post-dissection TAAA. Most patients presented with type II TAAA (91.1%), and 88.9% had undergone at least 1 prior aortic operation. Technical and clinical success were achieved in 86.6% and 82.2% of cases, respectively. Early mortality and MAEs occurred in 4.4% of patients. During a mean clinical follow-up of 35.0 ± 33.9 months, estimated overall survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 90.0%, 86.7%, and 79.2%, respectively, with no aorta-related deaths. At a mean imaging follow-up of 33.8 ± 32.2 months, target vessel patency was 98.8%. Target vessel instability occurred in 40% of patients, and 42.2% required 1 or more secondary interventions. Reintervention-free survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 75.6%, 72.4%, and 59.0%, respectively. No baseline, anatomic, or procedural variable independently predicted late adverse outcomes.
sections.conclusion: In this cohort of CTD patients, predominantly treated in complex redo settings, F/BEVAR demonstrated acceptable early and mid-term outcomes. Late adverse events and reinterventions were frequent but consistent with the natural history of CTD-related aortic disease and were not driven by identifiable baseline factors. These findings support the role of F/BEVAR as a valuable approach within a comprehensive, lifelong management strategy for CTD patients rather than as a definitive alternative to open surgery (OS).Clinical ImpactPatients with genetically triggered aortic disease often require multiple interventions throughout their lifetime because of the progressive nature of the underlying aortopathy. In this context, fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) should not be considered an alternative to open surgery, but rather a complementary approach within the long-term management of these patients. This multicenter study provides one of the largest dedicated experiences with F/BEVAR in this challenging population, showing that acceptable early and mid-term outcomes can be achieved even in complex redo and post-dissection settings. These findings support the integration of endovascular techniques into individualized, lifelong aortic treatment strategies at experienced centers, acknowledging the need for continued surveillance and secondary interventions.

items.title: Proliferative Glomerulonephritis with "Monoclonal" Immunoglobulin Deposits: Time for Revising the Name and a New Classification.
items.abstract: Proliferative glomerulonephritis with "monoclonal" immunoglobulin deposits (PGNMID) is a glomerular-limited disease characterized by glomerulonephritis with non-organized monotypic immunoglobulin deposits. Most cases are derived from IgG3, while the remainder are derived from IgG1, IgG2, IgA, IgM, or immunoglobulin light chain (LC) only. Despite the known low rates of detection of monoclonal gammopathy (MG) and B-cell clonal proliferative disorders in PGNMID (especially PGNMID-IgG3), it has traditionally been considered a monoclonal gammopathy of renal significance (MGRS) lesion. However, the association with MG has been recently challenged by demonstration that clone detection rate is rare in PGNMID-IgG3 despite ultrasensitive sequencing techniques and that the glomerular deposits in clone-negative cases, while monotypic, are in fact polyclonal. In contrast, most cases of PGNMID-LC and elderly PGNMID-IgG1 are associated with MG. Based on recent advances, we propose changing the official name of the disease from "proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits" to "proliferative glomerulonephritis with monotypic immunoglobulin deposits", and classifying the disease into MGRS PGNMID and non-MGRS PGNMID. Kidney biopsy reporting of PGNMID should include the immunoglobulin class (and subclass for PGNMID-IgG) given the notable differences in hematologic characteristics among these immunofluorescence morphologic variants. The new terminology and classification of PGNMID should improve communication between pathologists, nephrologists, and hematologists and help stratify patients for precision therapy.
keywords: proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits

items.title: Itch in Autoimmune Connective Tissue Diseases: Characteristics, Pathogenesis, and Current and Emerging Therapies.
items.abstract: Itch is a dominant, under-appreciated symptom across many autoimmune connective tissue diseases (AICTDs). Despite its prevalence and impact on quality of life, the evidence base for managing itch is fragmented and opaque. Unlike in other inflammatory dermatoses like atopic dermatitis, itch is rarely considered an endpoint in clinical trials and is inconsistently assessed; if it is, it is often measured indirectly via patient-reported disease activity scores. Here, we synthesize the current evidence underlying the pathophysiology and management of itch across dermatomyositis (DM), Sjögren's disease (SjD), lupus erythematosus (LE), and systemic sclerosis (SSc). In each case, we quantify the burden of itch; assess whether its etiology is inflammatory, neurogenic, or mixed; and assess the strength of evidence supporting possible therapies. Dermatomyositis is marked by profound itch and correlates with IL-31, IL-6, and type I interferons (T1IFN). Sjögren's disease leads to small fiber neuropathy (SFN) and pauci-inflammatory itch. Itch in CLE is shaped by both T1IFN and SFN. SSc involves both type 2 inflammation and prominent SFN. With itch surfacing as such a prominent symptom for patients with AICTDs, we call for a more active and dedicated approach to relieving it, guided by clinical trials that measure it explicitly.

items.title: Switching From Dupilumab to Upadacitinib in Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis: 52-Week Safety and Efficacy Results From an Open-Label Extension of the Phase 3 Heads Up Study.

sections.objective: Despite multiple available systemic therapies for atopic dermatitis (AD), many patients experience inadequate disease control. Safety and efficacy data after switching treatments are needed. To evaluate upadacitinib safety and efficacy in a 52-week open-label extension (OLE) study, continuously or after switching from dupilumab.
sections.methods: Patients with moderate-to-severe AD who completed 24 weeks of dupilumab 300 mg or upadacitinib 30 mg in the phase 3b Heads Up study were enrolled in an OLE (NCT04195698) and received 52 weeks of upadacitinib 30 mg. We report results through OLE week 52.
sections.results: Upadacitinib safety profiles were similar among patients who received continuous upadacitinib treatment and patients who switched from dupilumab to upadacitinib, consistent with previous AD studies. Clinical responses for skin clearance and itch relief were sustained during the OLE with continuous upadacitinib. For patients who switched from dupilumab to upadacitinib, clinical response at the end of the OLE was generally comparable to patients who received continuous upadacitinib.
sections.conclusion: Upadacitinib may offer a safe, effective therapeutic option for managing moderate-to-severe AD. Skin and itch outcomes at the end of the OLE were generally comparable between patients who switched from dupilumab to upadacitinib and those who received continuous upadacitinib.
sections.other: Open-label study.

items.title: Association of allergic conjunctivitis severity with meibomian gland abnormalities in children: a cross-sectional study.

sections.objective: To evaluate associations of allergic conjunctivitis (AC) severity with meibomian gland structure and function and tear film stability in children.
sections.methods: Single-center, cross-sectional study. The primary analysis included 144 children: 32 healthy controls and 112 patients with active AC classified as mild (n = 42), moderate (n = 39), or severe (n = 31). Supplementary analyses included 141 adults. Participants underwent standardized ocular surface examinations and noncontact meibography. AC severity was classified according to ocular surface signs. Multivariable linear regression evaluated severity-related associations after adjustment for age, sex, and disease duration.
sections.results: Median total MGL was 9.00%, 20.50%, 31.00%, and 36.00% in the control, mild, moderate, and severe groups, respectively. Corresponding median FBUT values were 9.50, 4.00, 3.00, and 2.00 seconds (both overall P < .001). Meibum expressibility and gland morphology scores differed across groups (both P < .001), whereas meibum quality grade did not (P = .447). After adjustment, each one-category increase in AC severity was associated with 7.54 percentage points higher total MGL (95% CI, 3.17-11.92). Each increase was also associated with 0.72 seconds shorter FBUT (β = -0.72; 95% CI, -0.95 to -0.50; both P < .001). Similar associations were observed in adults.
sections.conclusion: Greater AC severity was associated with greater MGL and reduced tear film stability in children. Meibum quality grade, however, did not differ significantly across groups. These findings support including meibomian gland and tear film assessments in the clinical evaluation of pediatric AC. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between AC severity and gland abnormalities.
sections.other: Total meibomian gland loss (MGL), fluorescein breakup time (FBUT), gland morphology scores, and meibum quality and expressibility scores.

items.title: Anticoagulants compared with aspirin in patients with embolic strokes of undetermined source: an individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised trials.

sections.objective: Direct-acting oral anticoagulation did not reduce recurrent stroke compared with aspirin in randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS), and subgroup benefits suggested by analyses of individual RCTs were inconsistent across trials. We aimed to evaluate the effect of anticoagulation on the risks of recurrent stroke and major bleeding in patients with ESUS, overall and in prespecified subgroups using individual participant data from RCTs.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE and Scopus for RCTs published between April 1, 2014, and March 1, 2025, without language restriction, comparing anticoagulants with aspirin in patients with ESUS. Non-randomised studies and studies not enrolling patients with ESUS were excluded. We requested individual participant data from the principal investigators of all eligible trials. The primary outcomes were recurrent stroke and major bleeding. For each outcome of interest, we estimated the treatment effect for the overall trial population separately within each trial and the resulting overall treatment estimates were subsequently pooled across trials. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (version 2.0) for the primary efficacy outcome of stroke recurrence. Hazard ratios (HRs) with corresponding 95% CIs were estimated following adjustment for prespecified covariates and pooled by use of the random-effects model. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025644724).
sections.results: Our systematic database search identified 1170 records. Of these studies, four were eligible for inclusion in the analysis, including a total of 13 970 participants. Mean age of participants was 66 years (SD 10·6); 5486 (39·3%) participants were female and 8484 (60·7%) were male. Across all trials, 6989 patients were assigned to receive a direct-acting oral anticoagulant and 6981 were assigned to receive aspirin. The hazard for recurrent stroke was similar between participants allocated to anticoagulant or aspirin (399 of 6989 patients [4·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 417 of 6981 [4·8 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 0·94, 95% CI 0·78-1·14), without evidence of heterogeneity across studies (I2=5%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·37). The hazard for major bleeding was also similar between the two groups (149 of 6989 patients [1·6 events per 100 patient-years] in the anticoagulant group vs 106 of 6981 [1·1 events per 100 patient-years] in the aspirin group; adjusted HR 1·19, 95% CI 0·52-2·73), but heterogeneity was present across studies (I2=79%, p for Cochran's Q test=0·0023).
sections.conclusion: Anticoagulation did not reduce the risk of recurrent stroke after ESUS when compared with aspirin, and the risk of major bleeding did not differ significantly between the two treatments. A possible benefit from anticoagulation in patients with ESUS and left atrial enlargement, as shown in a hypothesis-generating subgroup analysis, should be investigated in future trials.

items.title: Human iPS cell-derived thymus-seeding T cell progenitors support in vivo polyclonal naive-like T cell development.
items.abstract: Strategies to provide less-differentiated naive T cell clones in patients with cancer and immunodeficiencies are expected to improve the efficacy of immunotherapies. Adoptive transfer of T cell progenitors with thymus-seeding progenitors (TSPs) differentiated from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS cells) represents a potential approach to provide histocompatible naive T cell clones. In contrast to mature T cells, the generation of TSPs from human iPS cells remained a challenge. Here, we identified a chemically defined condition to generate VE-cadherin+CD34hiCD7med TSP-like cells (iTSPs) from human iPS cell-derived hemogenic endothelial cells (HECs). The differentiated cells engrafted into the thymus of immunodeficient mice and yielded CCR7+CD45RA+CD62L+TCF7+ naive T cells expressing a diverse T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire. iTSPs expressing a CD19-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) differentiated into CAR T cells in recipients and mediated antitumor activity against CD19+ leukemia. Together, these findings establish a platform for generating human iTSPs and provide developmental insight into naive-like T cell generation in vivo.

items.title: Organ-preserving multimodal therapy for patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma in China (DISTINCT-I): a single-arm, phase 2 trial.

sections.objective: Radical nephroureterectomy is the standard treatment for patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma, but causes irreversible nephron loss and can limit subsequent systemic therapy. We aimed to assess a response-adapted kidney-preserving strategy integrating induction disitamab vedotin plus tislelizumab, selective kidney-sparing surgery, and longitudinal circulating tumour DNA and urinary tumour DNA monitoring in patients with localised high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
sections.methods: DISTINCT-I was a single-arm, phase 2 trial conducted at two tertiary referral centres in China. Adults aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed, localised, high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma (cT1-T3, N0-N1, M0), and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2 received 2·0 mg/kg intravenous disitamab vedotin plus intravenous 200 mg tislelizumab once every 3 weeks for two to four cycles, followed by response-adapted kidney-sparing surgery when feasible. The primary endpoint was the 1-year kidney-intact event-free survival rate, assessed in the intention-to-treat population. Kidney-intact event-free survival was defined as the time from enrolment to the earliest occurrence of high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma recurrence, death from any cause, or conversion to radical nephroureterectomy. Safety was assessed in all patients who received at least one dose of study treatment and according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events and Clavien-Dindo classification. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05912816), and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Sept 6, 2023, and Nov 15, 2024, 36 patients were assessed for eligibility; ten did not meet the eligibility criteria and six declined to participate. Of the 20 patients enrolled, 17 (85%) were male and three (15%) were female; all patients were Chinese. At data cutoff (Dec 31, 2025), median follow-up was 17·0 months (IQR 14·0-23·0). The 1-year kidney-intact event-free survival rate was 70% (95% CI 46-88; 14 participants). Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in two (10%) patients (fatigue in one and increased γ-glutamyl transferase in another). No grade 4-5 treatment-related adverse events, serious treatment-related adverse events, or treatment-related deaths occurred.
sections.conclusion: This structured, multimodal, response-adapted strategy was associated with kidney preservation in selected patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma. These findings support further prospective comparative evaluation of organ-preserving strategies in patients with high-risk upper tract urothelial carcinoma.
sections.other: For the Chinese (Mandarin) translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

items.title: Prostate and pelvic nodal stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) versus prostate-only SBRT for high-risk, localised prostate cancer (PACE-NODES): early adverse event results from an international, open-label, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: Radiotherapy to the prostate and pelvic lymph nodes compared with prostate-only radiotherapy has shown benefits for high-risk prostate cancer in some studies, but evidence remains unclear. In low-risk or intermediate-risk disease, prostate-only stereotactic body radiotherapy (P-SBRT) is safe and effective. PACE-NODES aims to demonstrate safety and efficacy of prostate and pelvic nodal SBRT (PPN-SBRT) for high-risk disease.
sections.methods: PACE-NODES is a phase 3, open-label, randomised trial conducted at 47 hospitals in the UK, Ireland, and New Zealand. The trial recruited men aged 18 years or older, with a WHO performance status of 0-2, and with high-risk (Gleason score 8-10, stage T3a-T4, or prostate-specific antigen >20 ng/mL), localised prostate adenocarcinoma, planned for at least 12 months of hormone therapy. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1), using minimisation with a random element, to P-SBRT (36·25 Gy prostate) or PPN-SBRT (36·25 Gy prostate, 25 Gy pelvic nodes) in five fractions, on alternate days. Neither participants nor researchers were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint is time to biochemical or clinical failure (not yet mature). This preplanned safety analysis is on secondary endpoints, with a focus on Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade 2 or worse gastrointestinal and genitourinary adverse events within 12 weeks of treatment, analysed by treatment received. Patient-reported outcomes include Expanded Prostate Index Composite Short Form (EPIC-26), International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), and EQ-5D-5L. This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05613023) and is ongoing.
sections.results: Between Sept 9, 2022, and July 31, 2025, 1166 participants were recruited and randomly assigned (583 per group). The median age was 72·7 years (IQR 67·7-76·5). 18 patients did not receive radiotherapy; a further 60 (17 assigned to P-SBRT, 43 assigned to PPN-SBRT) did not receive allocated radiotherapy, mostly where planning constraints were not met. This analysis includes 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 511 patients receiving PPN-SBRT who had completed acute follow-up. Median follow-up was 13·8 months (IQR 7·8-21·0). 118 (21·3%) of 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 143 (28·0%) of 511 receiving PPN-SBRT had grade 2 or worse gastrointestinal events within 12 weeks (difference 6·7 percentage points [95% CI 1·6-11·9]; p=0·011; odds ratio [OR] 1·44 [95% CI 1·09-1·91]). This included grade 3 events in eight (1·4%) patients treated with P-SBRT and 11 (2·2%) treated with PPN-SBRT, and a grade 4 event in one (0·2%) patient treated with P-SBRT. 223 (40·2%) of 555 patients receiving P-SBRT and 183 (35·8%) of 511 receiving PPN-SBRT had grade 2 or worse genitourinary events (difference -4·4 percentage points [-10·2 to 1·5]; p=0·14; OR 0·83 [0·65-1·06]). This included grade 3 events in seven (1·3%) patients treated with P-SBRT and two (0·4%) treated with PPN-SBRT (no grade 4 events). Genitourinary and gastrointestinal adverse events peaked at 2 weeks and were low and similar between groups at 12 weeks. There were no treatment-related deaths. More patients receiving PPN-SBRT had important decreases in bowel function on 4-week EPIC-26 (208 [54·9%] of 379 receiving P-SBRT, 239 [65·5%] of 365 receiving PPN-SBRT). The proportion of patients reporting moderate or severe urinary symptoms on IPSS at 4 weeks was similar in those receiving P-SBRT (312 [72·4%] of 431) and those receiving PPN-SBRT (284 [71·9%] of 395), as were 4-week decreases in overall health score on EQ-5D-5L (-3·2 [99% CI -4·8 to -1·6] for P-SBRT and -2·5 [-4·1 to -0·9] for PPN-SBRT).
sections.conclusion: P-SBRT and PPN-SBRT for patients with high-risk prostate cancer were deliverable in an international multicentre trial. PPN-SBRT increased gastrointestinal but not genitourinary adverse events. Side-effects diminished rapidly, with no difference by 12 weeks. Follow-up continues for late adverse events and cancer control, which are essential for confirming a role for PPN-SBRT in this setting.

items.title: Antimicrobial prescribing and guideline adherence in febrile inpatients in the Masanga Fever Study (MaFeStu) in Sierra Leone: a substudy within a prospective observational study.

sections.objective: Antimicrobial resistance is increasing in sub-Saharan Africa, yet detailed data on prescribing practices remain scarce. We aimed to characterise antimicrobial compounds prescribed at admission, assess their concordance with treatment guidelines, and examine antimicrobial compounds prescribed during hospitalisation.
sections.methods: We conducted a substudy of the Masanga Fever Study (MaFeStu), a prospective observational study of febrile inpatients at Masanga Teaching Hospital in rural Sierra Leone from Sept 26, 2023, to Sept 26, 2024. Patients aged 5 months or older who were assessed within 3 h of admission and had documented fever (tympanic temperature >37·5°C) or reported fever within the previous 72 h were eligible. Patients were excluded if study procedures would delay urgent care, and those without available medication records were excluded post hoc. Clinical data and diagnoses were recorded prospectively, and antimicrobial prescriptions were extracted from patient files after discharge. The primary outcome was concordance of antimicrobial compounds initiated at admission with the hospital protocol and WHO guidance, assessed using predefined decision rules. Prescribed compounds were also classified by WHO Access, Watch, and Reserve category and indication. Secondary analyses summarised antimicrobial compounds prescribed during hospitalisation, including oral step-down and culture-directed therapy.
sections.results: 689 febrile inpatients included in the analysis, the median age was 14 years (IQR 1·8-34·0), 358 (52%) were female, and race and ethnicity data were not collected. At admission, 487 (71%; 95% CI 67-74) patients received one or more antimicrobial compounds. Of 882 antimicrobial compounds prescribed, 573 (65%; 95% CI 62-68) were WHO Access antibiotics, and 309 (35%; 95% CI 32-38) were WHO Watch antibiotics. Ceftriaxone was the most frequently prescribed compound (268 [30%] of 882). Lower respiratory tract infections, sepsis, and skin and soft tissue infections accounted for the largest share of compounds prescribed, overall and within the Watch category. Overall, 650 (74%; 95% CI 71-77) of 882 prescribed compounds were concordant with the hospital protocol, compared with 491 (56%; 95% CI 52-59) under WHO guidance. Discordant prescribing under both guidelines was concentrated in common indications, particularly sepsis and lower respiratory tract infection. During hospitalisation, 58 (4·9%; 95% CI 3·8-6·3) of 1183 antimicrobial compounds prescribed represented oral step-down therapy, and 73 (6·2%; 95% CI 4·9-7·7) were culture-directed.
sections.conclusion: Most prescribed compounds were WHO Access antibiotics and were largely concordant with hospital guidance and, to a lesser extent, with WHO guidance. Prescribing patterns suggest that strengthening diagnostics, refining treatment guidelines, and improving guideline familiarity could enhance guideline-concordant prescribing and antimicrobial stewardship in similar settings with constrained diagnostic and stewardship resources.

items.title: Genome writing reveals SVA retrotransposon consequences in X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism.
items.abstract: Human retrotransposon insertions are often associated with diseases. Regarding neurodegenerative X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism (XDP), a human-specific SINE-VNTR-Alu (SVA) subfamily F retrotransposon was inserted in intron 32 of the TAF1 gene. Here, we genomically rewrote a portion of the mouse Taf1 allele with the corresponding 78-kb XDP patient-derived TAF1 allele. In mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs), the presence of the intronic SVA-rather than the hybrid gene structure-reduces hyTAF1 (hybrid TAF1 mRNA) levels. This leads to transcriptional downregulation of genes with TATA boxes enriched in their promoters and triggers apoptosis. Chromatin and transcriptome profiling revealed that intronic SVAs are actively transcribed, forming barriers that likely impede transcription elongation. In mice, neuronal-lineage TAF1 humanization resulted in lethality in male progeny within 2 months. XDP male mice developed severe atrophy centered on the striatum-the same brain region affected in XDP patients. Lastly, CRISPRa-mediated activation of hyTAF1 restored mESC viability, suggesting that boosting TAF1 transcription could be a therapeutic approach.

items.title: Myelin pathology is a key feature of X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism.
items.abstract: X-linked dystonia-parkinsonism (XDP) is an adult-onset movement disorder predominantly affecting males of Filipino descent. It is caused by the insertion of a SINE-variable number of tandem repeat (VNTR)-Alu subfamily F (SVA_F) retrotransposon in the TATA-box binding protein-associated factor 1 (TAF1) gene. A barrier to XDP research has been the lack of animal models. Here, we introduce a conditional humanized XDP mouse model harboring a hybrid mouse-human Taf1/TAF1 gene (hyTAF1) containing the pathogenic SVA_F. We activated hyTAF1 in Nestin+ cells and found the resulting XDP male mice recapitulate features of human XDP, including severe motor impairment and striatal atrophy. Transcriptomic, histological, and electron microscopy analyses revealed a reduction in oligodendrocyte-lineage cells and myelin disruption. Consistent with this, postmortem brain tissue from XDP patients revealed similar myelin pathology, including loss of myelin in the medial prefrontal cortex. These results identify oligodendrocyte dysfunction and myelin loss as major contributors to XDP, providing new mechanistic insight into this disorder.

items.title: Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination.
items.abstract: New catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca-F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F- capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F- shuttling. Late Ca-F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F- by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

items.title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection: implications for women's health, clinical care, and future research.
items.abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognised cause of acute coronary syndromes, characterised by spontaneous separation of the layers of the coronary arterial wall. It predominantly affects younger women, and recent registry and imaging studies indicate that SCAD is more common than previously appreciated, challenging its historical classification as a rare condition. Clinically, SCAD is associated with a substantial early risk of adverse events, particularly in the first weeks after the index dissection. Given the high frequency of spontaneous healing, conservative management is preferred for most patients, whereas revascularisation is generally reserved for ongoing ischaemia or haemodynamic compromise. However, evidence to guide both pharmacological and interventional management remains scarce. This Review summarises current evidence on SCAD epidemiology, underlying mechanisms including genetic susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, management principles, implications for reproductive and women's health, and research priorities to improve outcomes for affected patients.

items.title: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.

sections.objective: The R21/Matrix-M (R21) malaria vaccine candidate, recommended by WHO for use in young children, could be extended to the whole population. Seasonal mass vaccination (SMV) before peak malaria transmission could be a promising tool to accelerate progress towards malaria elimination. We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of SMV with R21 in two malaria-endemic settings in west Africa.
sections.methods: This open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in The Gambia, a setting with low-to-moderate seasonal transmission, and Burkina Faso, a setting with intense seasonal transmission. 54 medium-sized villages (30 in The Gambia and 24 in Burkina Faso) were randomly assigned (1:1) by use of computer-restricted randomisation to receive either SMV with R21 (intervention group) or no SMV (control group). All study villages received national standard malaria control interventions. In the intervention group, residents who were aged 5 months and older, willing to comply with trial procedures, and could provide written informed consent (from parents or guardians for children aged <18 years plus assent for children aged 12-17 years) were eligible for vaccination. The intervention was delivered as three monthly doses of 5 μg (participants aged <15 years) or 10 μg (participants aged ≥15 years) R21 plus 50 μg of Matrix-M. The primary outcome was malaria prevalence at peak transmission, defined as the proportion of participants with Plasmodium falciparum infection assessed by quantitative PCR. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06578572) and the Pan-African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR202404544467702), and is ongoing.
sections.results: The intervention was delivered between May 30, and Aug 21, 2024. A cross-sectional survey to estimate the primary endpoint was conducted between Nov 18 and Dec 6, 2024. The population available for vaccination varied across the three rounds. In The Gambia, among 4311 total residents in intervention villages, 2565 (59·5%) received three vaccine doses; in Burkina Faso, among 6235 total residents in intervention villages, 4072 (65·3%) received three vaccine doses. SMV with R21 reduced the odds of malaria infection by 70% (adjusted odds ratio 0·30 [95% CI 0·20-0·44]; p<0·0001) in The Gambia and by 25% (0·75 [95% CI 0·58-0·98]; p=0·036) in Burkina Faso. In The Gambia, prevalence decreased across all age groups, whereas in Burkina Faso the largest effect was observed in children younger than 5 years. The vaccine was safe and well tolerated. 651 adverse events were reported in 581 (13·5%) vaccine recipients in The Gambia, and 795 adverse events were reported in 705 (11·3%) vaccine recipients in Burkina Faso. Among 69 serious adverse events reported overall, only one was considered related to vaccination (febrile convulsions in a female participant aged 8 years after the second dose in The Gambia).
sections.conclusion: SMV with R21 reduced malaria prevalence in both settings. It could become an additional strategy for malaria control in endemic areas of seasonal transmission. In low-to-moderate transmission settings, the vaccine could accelerate progress towards elimination; in high-transmission areas it could further reduce the malaria burden.

items.title: Reproductive health in women in Britain from 2010 to 2024: findings from repeated, cross-sectional National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal).

sections.objective: Major policy and funding shifts threaten access to essential reproductive services and reproductive autonomy in Britain (England, Scotland, and Wales) amid growing attention towards hormone hesitancy and declining birth rates. We report on prevalence, changes, and sociodemographic differences in reproductive health indicators among women of reproductive age in Britain from 2010 to 2024.
sections.methods: Britain's National Surveys of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles (Natsal) are cross-sectional, nationally representative surveys (Natsal-3 Sept 6, 2010, to Aug 31, 2012; Natsal-4 Sept 20, 2022, to April 5, 2024). Using 3198 Natsal-4 probability sample participants (assigned female at birth, aged 16-54 years, and reported vaginal sex ever), we estimated weighted prevalences of key health indicators of reproductive autonomy: reporting no effective contraception use, hormonal contraception use, abortion, unplanned or ambivalent pregnancy, infertility, help-seeking for infertility, and fertility intentions, and compared these with Natsal-3. Age-adjusted regression assessed changes between Natsal-3 and Natsal-4 by sociodemographic subgroups. Using Natsal-4 combined probability and non-probability samples (N=7053), we examined associations with age, education, area-level deprivation, ethnicity, and country of birth.
sections.results: In Natsal-4, 18·5% (95% CI 16·6-20·7) of women at risk of unintended pregnancy reported not using any effective contraception, and 41·9% (33·8-50·6) of past-year pregnancies were scored as unplanned or ambivalent. The prevalence of ever having had an abortion increased from Natsal-3 to Natsal-4 (from 16·0% to 20·7%, age-adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1·35, 95% CI 1·18-1·55), whereas overall prevalences of other indicators were stable. Subgroup analyses showed declining overall hormonal contraception use in those younger than 35 years (eg, from 64·6% to 50·3% for those aged 16-24 years, OR 0·55, 95% CI 0·39-0·79). The proportion of those aged 16-44 years reporting definitely not wanting children more than doubled from Natsal-3 to Natsal-4 (from 7·7% to 16·6%; adjusted OR 1·66, 95% CI 1·28-2·16), driven by women younger than 35 years. In Natsal-4, women with below degree-level education, living in more deprived areas, or of Black, African, Caribbean, or Black British ethnicity were more likely to report no effective contraception use and ever having had an abortion. Women living outside the most affluent areas or reporting below degree-level education were less likely to seek help for infertility.
sections.conclusion: The increase in women not intending to have children has major demographic implications and, alongside the persistent unmet need for effective contraception, underscores the importance of high-quality, easily accessible contraceptive services. The paucity of improvement in women's reproductive health in Britain and its entrenched inequalities demand person-centred, culturally competent policies and integrated services that uphold reproductive autonomy.

items.title: CD19 CAR T cell therapy alters disease-associated immune signatures in multiple sclerosis.
items.abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory central nervous system (CNS) disease. Although current immunotherapies control relapses, they have limited impact on progression, which might reflect incomplete access to or modulation of compartmentalized CNS inflammation. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells can infiltrate tissues, but their ability to access and eliminate immune cells residing in the CNS remains elusive. We report the treatment of five individuals with progressive or relapsing-remitting MS with autologous CD19 CAR T cells to assess safety-relevant aspects, CNS bioavailability, and compartment-specific effects. The intervention induces remodeling of the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) B cell pool, with a sustained reduction in CSF humoral biomarkers. Notably, CSF-infiltrating CAR T cells selectively upregulate phosphodiesterase 7B, while reconstituted peripheral B cells show altered cytokine and homing profiles. These findings indicate compartment-specific immunomodulation beyond peripheral B cell depletion and support controlled trials to test safety, durability, and efficacy.

items.title: RNA folding drives species-dependent host mRNA partitioning in Ebola virus condensates.
items.abstract: RNA viruses form membraneless condensates in host cells to drive replication, but whether these compartments regulate host RNAs remains unclear. Using multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH)-based subcellular transcriptomics, we quantified cellular mRNA recruitment into Ebola virus condensates under basal and interferon (IFN)-stimulated states. We find that, in the basal state, cellular RNAs with minimally folded coding regions are selectively recruited. Under IFN stimulation, however, IFN-stimulated genes (ISGs) with structured 3' UTRs concentrate in viral condensates. We find that both RNA structural features are conserved in the viral genome and support its retention in condensates. In parallel, for cellular mRNAs, we find that partitioning into condensates prolongs RNA half-life and amplifies, rather than dampens, ISG expression. Fruit bats, which do not experience severe disease from RNA viruses, instead have ISGs with reduced 3' UTR folding and may evade condensate sequestration, thus enabling balanced antiviral responses. This selective stabilization links condensate function to RNA regulation as a molecular determinant of virus-host co-evolution and disease pathogenesis.

items.title: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission.
items.abstract: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-transmitting mosquito, has invaded Africa and rapidly adapts to the high temperatures in urban settings. However, the molecular basis of its thermal adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identified a variant of a 5-kb deletion in the circadian clock gene timeless (tim-5kb) that rose to high frequency after 3 years of rearing at high laboratory temperatures. The tim+/-5kb heterozygous males maintain stable expression of the period gene at high temperatures, conferring a competitive mating advantage through the increased expression of the adipokinetic hormone gene AKH1 to promote energy mobilization and flight activity, together with the upregulation of fatty acyl-CoA reductase genes FAR3 and FAR5 to enhance the production of heptacosane pheromone. Moreover, heterozygous females exhibit increased susceptibility to Plasmodium infection, increasing malaria transmission potential. These findings reveal a circadian-based genetic mechanism that may underlie thermal adaptation in An. stephensi and hold important implications for malaria control in Africa.

items.title: Genomic surveillance reveals age-structured SARS-CoV-2 transmission across settings.
items.abstract: Understanding respiratory virus transmission requires integrating pathogen genomic data with detailed epidemiological context. We analyzed >85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genomes linked to epidemiological data collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Collected in 666 settings, including schools, colleges, and skilled nursing facilities, this dataset enabled direct comparison of within-setting transmission to community-wide risk. Elevated transmission was concentrated in specific age-defined subpopulations-older adolescents in schools, undergraduates in colleges, and residents in nursing facilities-with little additional risk among other groups, notably including staff. Young adults, particularly in colleges, played a disproportionate role in spread, and new viral lineages consistently expanded first within this group. Viral spread followed reproducible urban-to-rural gradients, and vaccination was associated with reduced onward transmission. We further estimated sequencing thresholds required for timely detection of emerging variants. Together, these findings reveal consistent demographic and spatial structure in SARS-CoV-2 transmission that can inform viral respiratory pathogen genomic surveillance.

items.title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality.
items.abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N-player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

items.title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis.
items.abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

items.title: Assessing Multiple Treatment Regimens for Tuberculosis.

sections.objective: Ganfeborole and BTZ-043 are new drugs that may improve tuberculosis treatment.
sections.methods: In this phase 2, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned participants with rifampin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis to receive the standard four-drug combination (isoniazid-rifampin-pyrazinamide-ethambutol; HRZE) for 24 weeks; bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin for 16 weeks; or one of 10 new four-drug combinations for 16 weeks. The new regimens contained ganfeborole, BTZ-043, or both, with combinations of bedaquiline, delamanid, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide, pretomanid, and linezolid. The primary end point was the log10(time to positivity) slope (rate of change from baseline to week 12 in the time to Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a positive sputum culture). The treatment effect was assessed as the Bayesian posterior probability of superiority of each new regimen to HRZE with respect to the primary end point (results were used to select regimens for further evaluation, rather than for characterization of efficacy).
sections.results: A total of 401 participants underwent randomization; 371 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 400 in the safety population. We identified two promising regimens for further evaluation: ganfeborole-bedaquiline-pretomanid-moxifloxacin (BPMG) and BTZ-043-bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin (BDMT). The log10(time to positivity) slope was 0.129 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.112 to 0.146) with BPMG and 0.142 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.126 to 0.160) with BDMT, as compared with 0.118 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.105 to 0.131) with HRZE, for a relative difference of 9.1% (95% Bayesian credible interval, -8.6 to 29.0) and 20.5% (95% Bayesian credible interval, 2.7 to 41.1), respectively, and a posterior probability of superiority of 0.83 and 0.99. The incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was 38% in the BPMG group (none of the participants discontinued), 28% in the BDMT group (one discontinued because of a drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms), and 24% in the HRZE group (none discontinued). Bedaquiline-moxifloxacin-pyrazinamide-BTZ-043 was discontinued because of hepatotoxic effects.
sections.conclusion: In this trial, two four-drug regimens, one with ganfeborole and one with BTZ-043, showed evidence of potential efficacy and a safety profile that did not preclude progression to further evaluation. (Funded by Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking and others; PARADIGM4TB ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06114628.).

items.title: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome.
items.abstract: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Although the definition of the syndrome has evolved over the past several decades, the core elements (acute onset, hypoxemia, and bilateral radiographic opacities) remain consistent. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. New research suggests that precision medicine approaches to ARDS management that focus on discrete biologic, radiographic, or physiological subphenotypes may improve outcomes, and prospective trials of these approaches are ongoing.

items.title: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 for HER2-Positive Advanced Breast Cancer.

sections.objective: The combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. The efficacy and safety of anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801) in this context are unknown.
sections.methods: In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point.
sections.results: A total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; P<0.001). The percentage of patients with an objective response was 87.6% in the anbenitamab group and 73.4% in the THP group. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 204 of 444 patients (45.9%) in the anbenitamab group and in 151 of 439 patients (34.4%) in the THP group. Neutropenia was the most common adverse event of grade 3 or higher in both groups (13.1% in the anbenitamab group and 8.4% in the THP group). Adverse events leading to death occurred in 2 patients in each group.
sections.conclusion: Anbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. (Funded by Shanghai JMT-Bio Technology and others; HEALER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05838066.).

items.title: Trial of Endovascular Therapy for Mild Stroke with Large-Vessel Occlusion.

sections.objective: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain.
sections.methods: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days.
sections.results: A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group).
sections.conclusion: In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. (Funded by Fujian Medical University Union Hospital and others; MILD-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06179017.).

items.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke.

sections.objective: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain.
sections.methods: We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety.
sections.results: A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).

items.title: Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in STEMI.

sections.objective: The safety of omitting up-front treatment with aspirin during primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains unclear.
sections.methods: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in Japan involving patients with STEMI who were undergoing primary PCI. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio before PCI to receive low-dose prasugrel monotherapy or dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with aspirin and low-dose prasugrel for 12 months. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction at 12 months, which was assessed for noninferiority with a prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.50 for the 95% confidence interval of the hazard ratio. The major secondary outcome was major bleeding (defined as a bleeding event of Bleeding Academic Research Consortium [BARC] type 3 [nonfatal major bleeding] or 5 [fatal bleeding]) at 12 months, which was assessed for superiority if noninferiority was established for the primary outcome.
sections.results: A total of 2216 patients were included in the full analysis population; 1109 were assigned to receive monotherapy and 1107 to receive DAPT. At 12 months, death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction had occurred in 124 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 11.0%) in the monotherapy group and in 94 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 8.5%) in the DAPT group (hazard ratio, 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.02 to 1.75; P = 0.40 for noninferiority). Major bleeding had occurred in 61 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 5.6%) in the monotherapy group and in 92 patients (Kaplan-Meier estimate, 8.4%) in the DAPT group (hazard ratio, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.91). The percentages of patients with definite or probable stent thrombosis and serious adverse events appeared to be similar in the two groups.
sections.conclusion: Among patients with STEMI who were undergoing primary PCI, low-dose prasugrel monotherapy initiated before PCI was not noninferior to DAPT for 12 months with respect to a composite of death from any cause, stroke, or myocardial infarction at 12 months. (Funded by Boston Scientific Japan; PREMIUM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05709626.).

items.title: Lipid-Lowering Strategies in the Era of Early Atherosclerosis Detection: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
items.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) begins early in life, driven in large part by cumulative exposure to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and other atherogenic lipoproteins. Contemporary evidence from epidemiologic cohorts, genetic studies, imaging studies, and lipid-lowering trials supports a paradigm of earlier identification and more sustained treatment of individuals at increased ASCVD risk. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews the rationale for early adoption of lipid-lowering strategies, with emphasis on lifetime lipid burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and the role of subclinical atherosclerosis assessment. Available clinical trial data suggest that greater absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and longer treatment duration can reduce ASCVD events, even though direct evidence remains limited in younger populations at low short-term risk. Atherosclerosis detected by imaging may identify individuals whose ASCVD risk is underestimated by traditional calculators, but optimal strategies for screening, treatment thresholds, safety, adherence, cost-effectiveness, and value require further study. Clinicians should integrate estimated short- and long-term risk, lipid burden, risk enhancers, imaging findings when appropriate, and patient preferences to guide individualized, shared decision making to reduce lifetime ASCVD risk.

items.title: Outcomes of Endovascular Repair for Stanford Type B Aortic Dissection with Concurrent Retrograde Intramural Hematoma Involving the Aortic Arch and/or Ascending Aorta (Zone 0-2) in a Chinese Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

sections.objective: To evaluate the outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD) with concurrent retrograde intramural hematoma (RTIMH) involving the aortic arch, with or without further extension into the ascending aorta.
sections.methods: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included. Co-primary outcomes were technical success and post-TEVAR retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD), defined as the new development of a communicating dissection flap within the previously non-flow intramural hematoma. Secondary outcomes included early mortality, stroke, type I endoleak, reintervention, survival, aortic rupture, and aortic remodelling. Proportions were pooled using single-arm random-effects meta-analysis following logit transformation; remaining findings were synthesised narratively.
sections.results: Seven retrospective cohort studies comprising 342 patients, all from mainland Chinese institutions, were included. The pooled technical success rate was 99% (95% CI 97-99%; I2 = 0.0%). The pooled post-TEVAR RTAD rate was 3% (95% CI 1-8%; I2 = 7.6%), with all events preceded by proximal stent-graft-induced new entry. Secondary outcomes included pooled 30-day mortality of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), aortic rupture of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), reintervention of 7% (95% CI 5-11%; I2 = 0.0%), late all-cause mortality of 4% (95% CI 3-6%; I2 = 0.0%), and type I endoleak of 4% (95% CI 2-7%; I2 = 0.0%). All studies reporting pre- and post-procedural imaging demonstrated reductions in ascending aortic diameter and hematoma thickness, with complete ascending IMH resolution in 52.5-100% of patients.
sections.conclusion: TEVAR is technically feasible with low perioperative mortality and consistent aortic remodelling in selected patients with TBAD-associated RTIMH. Post-TEVAR RTAD and type I endoleak represent the principal procedure-specific risks. Contemporary evidence remains limited to small retrospective cohorts from a single geographic region.

items.title: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment: A contemporary review of repair techniques, common complications, advances in imaging and access to care.
items.abstract: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) is a vision-threatening ophthalmic emergency with a rising global incidence driven by aging populations and the worldwide myopia epidemic. Despite modern surgical techniques achieving anatomic reattachment in over 90% of cases, as many as 40% of successfully reattached eyes fail to recover functional vision, underscoring a persistent and clinically important gap between anatomic and visual outcomes. We synthesize contemporary evidence across a wide clinical spectrum of RRD. We examine the pathophysiologic cascade initiated by posterior vitreous detachment, the classification and clinical significance of types of retinal breaks, and the epidemiologic burden of established risk factors including high myopia, pseudophakia, and hereditary vitreoretinal disorders. The historical evolution of repair techniques is reviewed. Evidence based rationale for personalized surgical selection in phakic, pseudophakic, and giant retinal tear-associated detachments is then discussed. The most common complications of surgical repair are addressed, with particular emphasis on proliferative vitreoretinopathy as the dominant cause of surgical failure and the most pressing unmet therapeutic need. We further examine how neighborhood-level social determinants of health independently shape presentation severity and visual recovery, underscoring that equitable access to timely care can be as fundamental to influencing outcomes as surgical technique itself. Finally, emerging pharmacologic strategies, intraoperative optical coherence tomography, robotic surgical assistance, and imaging prognostic tools, with and without the use of artificial intelligence are evaluated as future directions. Advancing outcomes in RRD will require the integration of surgical refinement, emerging pharmacology, imaging-based prognostication, and an unwavering commitment to equitable access across all patient populations.

items.title: Network Meta-Analysis of Complement Inhibitors for Geographic Atrophy in Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
items.abstract: Pegcetacoplan (PEG) and avacincaptad pegol (ACP) are approved complement inhibitors for geographic atrophy (GA) secondary to age-related macular degeneration, yet direct comparative evidence is lacking. We conducted a PROSPERO-registered frequentist network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of complement inhibitors for GA.
