MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 5, 2025. Twenty-two reports of 13 trials (5,126 patients) were included. Compared with sham, moderate-certainty evidence showed that PEG 15 mg monthly and every other month reduced untransformed GA lesion growth. ACP estimates were imprecise when reconstructed from arm-level data, but both ACP doses reduced GA growth when the trials' model-based treatment differences were used, consistent with the pivotal trials. No ACP and PEG regimens differed in GA growth, and no complement inhibitor improved low-luminance visual acuity. At final follow-up, PEG regimens and ACP 4 mg increased neovascular age-related macular degeneration compared with sham, and its incidence was lower with ACP 2 mg than with PEG 15 mg monthly in indirect comparison (low certainty), with no other ACP and PEG difference. These comparisons are limited by differences in trial populations, endpoints, and follow-up. Head-to-head trials with functional endpoints are needed.

items.title: Secondary analysis of the FIELD randomized trial evaluated the performance of GFR slope in a non-glomerular model of estimated GFR decline.

sections.objective: Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) decline is a recent surrogate kidney endpoint for trials. Estimated GFR (eGFR) decline has been modelled using GFR slope, correlating total and chronic GFR slopes with composite kidney endpoints. Several included interventions caused an initial eGFR decline mediated by glomerular hemodynamics. We tested the association of GFR slopes with clinical endpoints for fenofibrate, an agent with an acute, non-glomerular eGFR decline (i.e. no effect on inulin clearance).
sections.methods: The FIELD trial randomized adults to fenofibrate or placebo. Total slope was calculated using a repeated measures 2-slope linear mixed model for the entire intervention period. A three-year sensitivity analysis was performed. Chronic slope was calculated from month four. The composite kidney endpoint was doubling of serum creatinine or 40% decline/eGFR under 15 ml/min/1.73 m2/kidney death/kidney replacement therapy. The total slope from baseline to eight-week washout eGFR was an exploratory subgroup analysis.
sections.results: 9795 participants were followed for five years. Post-washout eGFR was ascertained in 660 sub-study participants. Fenofibrate produced an acute eGFR decline of -9.05 ml/min/1.73 m2. Fenofibrate improved chronic slope (significant between-group difference 0.61 ml/min/1.73 m2/ annum [95% CI 0.50 to 0.71]) but worsened total slope (significant between group difference -1.54, 95% CI -1.65 to -1.44). Fenofibrate significantly increased the clinical endpoint (hazard ratio 1.48, 95% CI 1.16 to 1.89). Washout analyses demonstrated treatment benefit on total slope, contrary to on-study analyses in the overall cohort.
sections.conclusion: Conventional composite endpoints include surrogate components that may not always accord with measured kidney function, though widely accepted in trials. Total slope and the conventional composite yielded concordant treatment effects under an acute eGFR change both larger and mechanistically distinct from those in previous validation work, supporting the conclusion that total slope will produce similar results to conventional endpoints.

items.title: Dietary sodium restriction enhances the renoprotective efficacy of endothelin-A receptor antagonism in proteinuric chronic kidney disease.

sections.objective: Endothelin-A receptor antagonists (ERAs) are emerging as an important treatment for proteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD). As with renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) inhibition, dietary sodium intake may influence their therapeutic efficacy, but this has not been investigated. Here, we examined whether dietary sodium restriction enhances the systemic and kidney effects of acute selective endothelin-A (ETA) receptor antagonism in proteinuric CKD.
sections.methods: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 12 adults (mean age 46 years) with non-diabetic proteinuric CKD (mean eGFR 55 mL/min/1.73 m2; median proteinuria 1.8 g/day) receiving maximally tolerated RAAS inhibition completed two 14-day dietary interventions (habitual dietary sodium intake [13.3 g salt/day] and dietary sodium restriction [6.3 g salt/day, approximating guideline-recommended levels]) in random order. During each dietary period, participants underwent two study visits and received intravenous infusion of either placebo or the selective ET A receptor antagonist, BQ123. Systemic hemodynamics, arterial stiffness, kidney hemodynamics and proteinuria were assessed following each intervention.
sections.results: BQ123 produced comparable reductions in systolic blood pressure (about 12-14 mmHg), systemic vascular resistance and arterial stiffness under both dietary conditions and increased kidney blood flow (about 320-335 mL/min) irrespective of dietary sodium intake. In contrast, significant reductions in glomerular filtration rate (peak placebo-adjusted reduction: about 5 mL/min/1.73 m2), effective filtration fraction (peak reduction about 1.5%), and proteinuria (about 300 μg/min) were observed only during dietary sodium restriction and not during habitual sodium intake.
sections.conclusion: Dietary sodium restriction enhances the short-term kidney efficacy of selective endothelin-A receptor antagonism in proteinuric CKD while preserving its beneficial systemic hemodynamic effects. As ERAs become established therapies for proteinuric kidney disease, these findings suggest that adherence to dietary sodium restriction may maximize their kidney-protective benefits. Whether the acute changes demonstrated here translate into long-term kidney protection requires prospective evaluation.

items.title: Checkpoint Inhibition during primary hepatitis E virus infection alters memory development of virus-specific T-cells in humans.

sections.objective: HEV infection is an underappreciated differential diagnosis in patients presenting with acute hepatitis during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. As T-cells are the key targets of ICIs, particularly through blockade of inhibitory immune checkpoints such as PD-1, this intervention is likely to influence the dynamics and differentiation fate of de novo primed virus-specific T-cells during primary HEV infection. We therefore aimed to examine how PD-1 blockade during primary HEV-infection influences expansion, contraction, and memory formation of virus-specific CD8+ T-cells.
sections.methods: HEV-specific CD8 and CD4+ T-cells were analyzed by applying a reverse phenotyping approach combined with single-cell transcriptomics and TCR sequencing, as well as multiparameter flow cytometry with MHC class I tetramers. We characterized HEV-specific T-cell responses in patients receiving ICI and in untreated patients during acute-viremic infection and after viral clearance.
sections.results: Under ICI, de novo primed HEV-specific CD8+ T-cells showed enhanced clonal expansion, cytotoxicity, and terminal differentiation. Rather than transitioning into classical memory subsets, these cells retained a cytotoxic transcriptional program and acquired features of long-lived effector-like T-cells (LLEC). While HEV-specific T-cells remained detectable over > 2 years, their functional recall responsiveness declined in ICI-treated patients.
sections.conclusion: Collectively, our findings demonstrate that PD-1 blockade during the formation of a primary immune response reshapes the fate of the antiviral CD8+ T-cell pool, favoring terminally differentiated effector states over conventional memory formation, with potential implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies.
sections.other: Our study represents the first demonstration in a human model that PD-1 blockade during primary antigen exposure reshapes antiviral CD8+ T-cell effector formation and memory differentiation. By identifying PD-1 signaling during a primary immune response as a regulator of antiviral CD8+ T-cell fate, our findings establish a conceptual framework for understanding how immune checkpoint blockade influences the development of primary antiviral T-cell responses, with implications for viral infections, vaccination, and immunotherapeutic strategies.

items.title: Smoke, Not Smoking, as a Possible Risk Factor Triggering Conversion in Leber's Hereditary Optic Neuropathy: A Retrospective Case Series.

sections.objective: To describe the association of wildfire smoke exposure with conversion of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) mutation carriers to symptomatic LHON.
sections.methods: In this retrospective observational case series, we performed an exploratory analysis of our institutional LHON registry for patients under observation during 2017-2018. We described four LHON mutation carriers who developed bilateral vision loss within 4-8 weeks of documented wildfire smoke exposure during the 2017 Wine Country and 2018 Camp (Paradise) fires in Northern California. We performed an exploratory analysis of our institutional LHON registry for patients under observation during 2017-2018.
sections.results: All four carriers resided in regions where the Air Quality Index exceeded 150 for multiple consecutive days. Two individuals had remained asymptomatic carriers for more than four decades prior to conversion. In the registry cohort of 40 carriers, 15 converted during 2017-2018. Conversion occurred in 7 of 9 carriers (78%) residing in the Northern California wildfire-affected region, compared with 8 of 31 (26%) residing elsewhere (odds ratio 10.1; Fisher's exact p=0.02). In a time-window analysis restricted to the 8 weeks following the November 2018 Paradise fire, 3 of 5 Northern California carriers at risk (60%) converted compared with 0 of 23 carriers residing outside the region (odds ratio 65.8; Fisher's exact p=0.006).
sections.conclusion: We observed temporal clustering of LHON conversion following wildfire smoke exposure and regional enrichment of conversion during 2017-2018. Although causality cannot be established in this retrospective analysis, acute particulate exposure may represent a mitochondrial stressor that lowers the threshold for conversion in susceptible individuals.
sections.other: Four genetically confirmed LHON mutation carriers who developed bilateral vision loss after the 2017 Wine Country, or 2018 Camp Fire (Paradise) wildfire and 40 genetically confirmed carriers were examined and followed up from 2017-2018 to 2026. Time from regional wildfire smoke exposure to symptomatic conversion and conversion frequency among registry carriers.

items.title: Historical Redlining and Present-Day Vision Disability in Atlanta, Georgia: The Mediating Role of Neighborhood Deprivation.

sections.objective: To investigate whether present-day vision disability (VD) prevalence reflects historical redlining in Atlanta, Georgia, quantify mediation by neighborhood deprivation, and assess generalizability across redlined United States (U.S.) cities.
sections.methods: Ecologic, cross-sectional, retrospective analysis. Census tract-level VD prevalence (2015-2019 American Community Survey) was linked to Home Owners' Loan Corporation (HOLC) grade, Social Deprivation Index (SDI), and distance to nearest eye care office. Unadjusted associations used Spearman correlations and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Besag-York-Mollié 2 (BYM2) spatial models estimated risk ratios (RR) per 1-SD adjusting for age and sex; causal mediation analysis quantified the indirect effect of HOLC grade on VD through SDI. Analyses were repeated across 108 cities and pooled via random-effects meta-analysis. Statistical significance was defined as p<0.05 for correlation and group comparison tests, and 95% confidence intervals for BYM2 model and mediation analysis estimates.
sections.results: In Atlanta, HOLC score was not associated with VD risk (fully adjusted RR=0.89, 95% CI: 0.72-1.09). The indirect effect through SDI was significant (ACME=1.15 percentage points per one-grade increase, 95% CI: 0.76-1.56, p<0.001), and the direct effect was not (ADE=0.11 percentage points, 95% CI: -0.60-0.66, p=0.88); the proportion mediated through SDI was 91%. Lack of vehicle access was most strongly associated with VD risk (RR=1.73, 95% CI: 1.39-2.12). Eye care office distance did not differ by HOLC grade (p=0.56). Nationally, the HOLC-VD association (pooled RR=1.21, 95% CI: 1.18-1.24) attenuated after SDI adjustment (pooled RR=1.03, 95% CI: 1.01-1.05); 78% was mediated through SDI (pooled ACME=0.37 percentage points, 95% CI: 0.33-0.41). The indirect effect varied substantially between cities (I²=65.3%).
sections.conclusion: In Atlanta and across redlined U.S. cities, the association between redlining and VD prevalence was largely explained by neighborhood deprivation. Lack of transportation access was most strongly associated with VD, and eye care offices in Atlanta were not farther from more redlined neighborhoods, suggesting access and affordability may underlie these inequities. Reducing place-based VD inequities may require investing in social determinants, such as transportation, beyond clinical services.
sections.other: 93 Atlanta census tracts and 12,432 tracts across 108 redlined U.S. cities. VD prevalence by HOLC grade, SDI, racial composition, and eye care distance.

items.title: Sarcoidosis for the Dermatologist : Part 2: Treatment and Monitoring.
items.abstract: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem inflammatory disease that may require treatment for multiorgan disease, or organ specific involvement, including sometimes for primary cutaneous disease or cutaneous involvement that fails to respond to treatment for multiorgan disease. Skin treatments range from local therapy to systemic anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and immunosuppressive agents, depending on the extent and severity of involvement. Management is individualized and aims to control disease activity, prevent irreversible organ damage, reduce treatment-related toxicity, and improve quality of life. Because the clinical course is variable, careful follow-up is essential, with attention to treatment response, relapse, and the development of extracutaneous involvement. Ongoing monitoring should be guided by symptoms, organ involvement, and the therapies being used.

items.title: Reflectance Confocal Microscopy Improves Clinicopathologic Correlation in Facial Lentigo Maligna: A Prospective Real-Life Study.

sections.objective: Pigmented facial lesions pose a diagnostic challenge, and lentigo maligna (LM) must not be overlooked as a differential diagnosis. Despite integrated evaluation with clinical examination and dermoscopy, diagnostic uncertainty may persist. Reflectance confocal microscopy (RCM) has emerged as a complementary diagnostic tool. To assess the diagnostic performance of RCM in clinically suspected cases of facial LM.
sections.methods: We conducted a prospective single-center study between February 2021 and September 2025, including 248 flat pigmented facial lesions clinically suspected of LM. RCM was performed, and lesions suggestive of LM were biopsied. Results were compared with the gold standard, defined as the diagnosis obtained after integrated clinical-dermoscopic-RCM-histopathological evaluation.
sections.results: RCM achieved 100% sensitivity and 94.2% specificity for LM diagnosis, and 75% (n = 187) of lesions did not undergo biopsy following RCM evaluation. Perifollicular dendritic cells on RCM were present in 100% of biopsy-proven LM. Among all LM, 20% had an initially negative biopsy despite RCM findings suggestive of LM, prompting additional histopathological evaluation that ultimately confirmed LM in all cases.
sections.conclusion: RCM strengthens the correlation between clinical, dermoscopic, and histopathologic findings in LM.
sections.other: Single-center real-world study, limited to facial lesions, potential underestimation of false negatives and operator-dependent interpretation.

items.title: Endovenous Microwave Versus Radiofrequency Ablation for Isolated Small Saphenous Vein Reflux: A Randomised Controlled Trial.

sections.objective: No randomised trial has directly compared endovenous microwave ablation (EMA) with radiofrequency ablation (RFA) for isolated small saphenous vein (SSV) reflux. This trial aimed to determine whether EMA is non-inferior to RFA for 12-month SSV trunk occlusion and to characterise the sural nerve injury profile of each modality.
sections.methods: Patients with duplex-confirmed symptomatic isolated SSV reflux were randomised 1:1 to EMA or RFA at a single vascular centre. The primary efficacy endpoint was duplex-confirmed SSV trunk occlusion at 12 months, assessed in the per-protocol (PP) population with a pre-specified 10% non-inferiority margin. The key secondary safety endpoint was clinically confirmed sural nerve injury at 12 months. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) - Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS), Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire (AVVQ), and Chronic Venous Insufficiency Questionnaire (CIVIQ-14) - were assessed longitudinally using a mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM).
sections.results: Baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups. At 12 months, the PP occlusion rate was 98.4% in both groups (EMA 60/61; RFA 62/63; risk difference -0.05%, 95% CI -4.6% to 4.5%), confirming non-inferiority (P < .001). The intention-to-treat sensitivity analysis (EMA 92.3%, RFA 95.4%) also satisfied the 10% margin. Clinically confirmed sural nerve injury occurred in 3.3% (2/61) of EMA patients and 1.6% (1/63) of RFA patients (P = .614); all sensory symptoms resolved within six months. EMA was associated with a nominally shorter operative time (30.2 ± 9.0 vs 33.1 ± 7.9 min; P = .054) and a nominally lower one-month VCSS score (P = .030); neither difference persisted beyond three months. MMRM analysis showed significant within-group improvement across all three PROM instruments over 12 months (all P < .001), with no significant between-group difference at any timepoint.
sections.conclusion: With adequate perivenous tumescent anaesthesia and a proximal-selective dual-cycle ablation strategy, EMA achieves 12-month SSV occlusion non-inferior to RFA. Sural nerve injury rates are low and reversible with both modalities. EMA offers a marginal operative time advantage and may confer early symptomatic benefit, though these differences are not sustained at 12 months. Both techniques appear to be appropriate first-line options for symptomatic isolated SSV reflux.

items.title: Low-Concentration Atropine Eye Drops in Children With Myopia and Intermittent Exotropia: The AMIXT2 Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: The optimal atropine concentration for myopia control in children with coexisting intermittent exotropia (IXT) remains uncertain. To compare the efficacy and safety of 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine eye drops in children with myopia and IXT.
sections.methods: This single-center, double-masked, 3-arm randomized clinical trial was conducted from September 2023 to March 2026. Children aged 6 to 12 years with basic-type IXT and myopia (cycloplegic spherical equivalent [SE], -0.50 to -6.00 diopters [D]) were enrolled. Data analysis was conducted from March 2026 to July 2026. Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to 0.01%, 0.02%, or 0.04% atropine eye drops nightly in both eyes.
sections.results: Among 264 randomized children (mean [SD] age, 8.4 [1.5] years; 130 female [49.2%]), 224 (84.8%) completed the 12-month assessment. Mean (SD) SE changes were -0.43 (0.50) D, -0.35 (0.51) D, and -0.18 (0.60) D with 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine, respectively (overall P = .001). Compared with 0.01% and 0.02% atropine, 0.04% atropine was associated with less SE progression (vs 0.01%: difference, 0.24 D; 95% CI, 0.11-0.37 D; P < .001; vs 0.02%: difference, 0.16 D; 95% CI, 0.04-0.29 D; P = .02). Mean (SD) AL changes were 0.31 (0.25) mm, 0.25 (0.23) mm, and 0.15 (0.29) mm, respectively (overall P < .001); corresponding differences for 0.04% vs 0.01% and 0.02% were -0.16 mm (95% CI, -0.22 to -0.10 mm; P < .001) and -0.10 mm (95% CI, -0.16 to -0.04 mm; P < .001). Mean (SD) near exodeviation decreased by 3.46 (5.76) prism diopters (PD), 4.84 (8.05) PD, and 6.13 (7.11) PD, respectively (overall P = .04); the reduction was greater with 0.04% vs 0.01% atropine (difference, -2.68 PD; 95% CI, -4.78 to -0.57 PD; P = .008). Study drug-related photophobia occurred in 8 (9.1%), 9 (10.2%), and 19 participants (21.6%) in the 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine groups, respectively; no participant discontinued treatment because of photophobia.
sections.conclusion: In the AMIXT2 randomized clinical trial among children with myopia and IXT, 0.04% atropine eye drops were associated with less myopia progression and axial elongation over 12 months than 0.01% or 0.02% atropine eye drops. Higher concentrations were associated with greater reductions in near magnitude of exodeviation, which warrant further investigation.
sections.other: The primary outcome was 12-month change in cycloplegic SE. Secondary outcomes included changes in axial length (AL), exotropia conditions, binocular vision, and ocular safety parameters.

items.title: Grafting vs Intraoperative Mitomycin C for Preventing Pterygium Recurrence: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

sections.objective: Postoperative recurrence remains a major challenge after primary pterygium surgery, and whether grafting approaches are more effective than intraoperative mitomycin C (MMC) in reducing recurrence remains uncertain. To determine whether grafting with conjunctival autograft (CAG) or amniotic membrane transplant (AMT) is superior to MMC in preventing 1-year recurrence after primary pterygium excision.
sections.methods: This multicenter, open-label randomized clinical trial with masked outcome assessment with 12-month follow-up was conducted at 5 tertiary hospitals in China. Enrollment and follow-up occurred between January 2016 and December 2020, and data were analyzed from September 2025 through January 2026. Patients aged 18 to 80 years with primary pterygium were enrolled and randomly assigned 1:1:1 to AMT (n = 249), MMC (n = 248), or CAG (n = 253). Standardized pterygium excision with conjunctival excision extending radially 4 mm from the limbus, combined with AMT, MMC, or CAG.
sections.results: Of 750 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 57.2 [10.5] years; 487 women [64.9%]), 681 (90.8%) completed follow-up. Recurrence in the intention-to-treat analysis was 57 participants of 249 with AMT (22.9%), 34 of 248 with MMC (13.7%), and 13 of 253 with CAG (5.0%). Risk differences were 9.2 percentage points for AMT vs MMC (98.33% CI, 0.6-17.9; P = .01), 17.9 for AMT vs CAG (98.33% CI, 10.5-25.4; P < .001), and 8.7 for MMC vs CAG (98.33% CI, 2.2-15.2; P = .001). Risk ratios were 1.69 (98.33% CI, 0.99-2.91; P = .02), 4.62 (98.33% CI, 2.14-9.97; P < .001), and 2.73 (98.33% CI, 1.20-6.20; P = .004), respectively. Complete-case analyses yielded similar results. Adverse events occurred in 18 of 249 AMT participants (7.2%), 28 of 248 MMC participants (11.3%), and 16 of 253 CAG participants (6.3%), with no intervention-related serious adverse events.
sections.conclusion: In this randomized clinical trial, among patients undergoing primary pterygium excision, recurrence was lowest with CAG, intermediate with MMC, and highest with AMT. The moderate magnitude of the between-procedure differences makes recurrence prevention an important-but not exclusive-determinant of surgical choice and may inform individualized surgical management.
sections.other: The primary outcome was 12-month postoperative recurrence. Secondary outcomes included best-corrected visual acuity, epithelial healing time, and conjunctival congestion scores.

items.title: Three-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Therapy Using Covered Stent-Grafts Versus Interwoven Nitinol Stents in Severely Calcified Femoropopliteal Artery Disease From a Retrospective Multicenter Registry.

sections.objective: This study aimed to compare the long-term safety and efficacy of Viabahn covered stent-grafts (CSG) and Supera peripheral stents (SPS) in calcified femoropopliteal artery lesions.
sections.methods: We retrospectively analyzed 341 cases who had Rutherford class 2 to 6 peripheral artery disease and underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) with either CSG (n = 137) or SPS (n = 204) for femoropopliteal lesions with bilateral calcification assessed by fluoroscopic image based on Peripheral Arterial Calcium Scoring System classification, between April 2017 and February 2021 at 7 cardiovascular centers in our country.
sections.results: Following propensity score (PS) matching, the final study population comprised 142 matched patients with no remarkable intergroup difference in baseline characteristics. The 3-year primary patency was 70.9% in the CSG group and 56.2% in the SPS group, respectively, and was not statistically different (P = .083). Moreover, no significant difference was noted in freedom from target lesion revascularization (72.8% vs 63.5%, P = .16), limb salvage rate (100.0% vs 96.2%, P = .32), and overall survival rate (67.6% vs 66.6%, P = .61). Stratification analysis revealed that advanced age and current smoking had a significant interaction on the association of CSG versus SPS implantation with restenosis (interaction P < .05).
sections.conclusion: In patients with severely calcified femoropopliteal lesions, the 3-year primary patency was not significantly different between EVT using CSG and SPS following PS matching.Clinical ImpactSevere calcification in femoropopliteal disease remains a challenge for EVT. Covered stent-graft and SPS are reliable devices for calcified femoropopliteal lesions. We compared the 3-year outcomes in patients undergoing EVT using either CSG or SPS. Following the propensity matching, the 3-year primary patency was not different at 70.0% and 56.2% (P = .083) in the CSG (n = 71) and SPS (n = 71) groups, respectively. Moreover, no significant difference was noted in freedom from target lesion revascularization and limb salvage rate.

items.title: Endovascular Recanalization of Chronically Occluded Femoropopliteal Bypass Grafts: Feasibility and Early Clinical Outcomes.

sections.objective: Chronic occlusion of femoropopliteal bypass grafts remains a complex clinical challenge, particularly in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) who have limited surgical options and high operative risk. Although redo bypass surgery has traditionally been considered the standard treatment, it is associated with increased morbidity. Advances in endovascular techniques have expanded revascularization strategies; however, data on graft-directed endovascular recanalization remain limited.
sections.methods: This retrospective single-center study included 32 consecutive patients who underwent endovascular recanalization for chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts between January 2018 and December 2024. A stepwise graft-directed technique was applied, consisting of intraluminal guidewire crossing, sequential balloon predilatation, and stent implantation along the graft body and anastomotic segments when necessary. Technical success, procedural safety, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) were evaluated.
sections.results: The mean age of the patients was 69.8 ± 9.6 years, and 68.8% were male. Technical success was achieved in 30 patients (93.8%). Median ABI improved significantly from 0.34 (interquartile range [IQR]: 0.22-0.48) before intervention to 0.71 (IQR: 0.58-0.84) after revascularization. Stent implantation was performed in all patients, with a median of 3 stents per case. Periprocedural complications occurred in 2 patients (6.3%) and were managed conservatively or by endovascular means. No procedure-related mortality or major limb loss was observed during hospitalization.
sections.conclusion: Stepwise endovascular recanalization of chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts is feasible and safe, providing favorable early technical and clinical outcomes. This graft-targeted approach may expand the endovascular treatment spectrum for PAD patients who are poor candidates for surgical reintervention and should be regarded as a procedural optimization strategy rather than a replacement for redo bypass surgery.Clinical ImpactGraft-directed endovascular recanalization of chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts demonstrated high technical success (93.8%), improved limb perfusion, and low periprocedural complication rates. This minimally invasive approach may represent a feasible revascularization option for selected high-risk patients with limited surgical alternatives. Further studies are warranted to establish its long-term durability.

items.title: Hybrid Repair of a True Left Subclavian Artery Aneurysm After Coronary Bypass: A Tailored Strategy to Avoid Pitfalls.
items.abstract: True subclavian artery aneurysms are rare and clinically and technically challenging, particularly when located proximal to a patent left internal mammary artery (LIMA) coronary bypass, where preservation of myocardial perfusion is mandatory. We report the case of a 75-year-old man with an incidentally detected left subclavian artery aneurysm located just proximal to a patent LIMA-left anterior descending artery bypass. Previous sternotomy and left thoracotomy precluded conventional open repair, while the absence of adequate proximal and distal landing zones ruled out a conventional endovascular approach. A single-stage hybrid strategy was therefore adopted, consisting of a carotid-subclavian bypass via a supraclavicular approach, distal aneurysm exclusion using a vascular plug, and final proximal exclusion with a thoracic endograft. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 3. At 6-month follow-up, computed tomography angiography demonstrated complete aneurysm exclusion, patency of the carotid-subclavian bypass and the LIMA graft, and preserved vertebral artery flow. This case highlights how a carefully planned hybrid repair can represent a safe and effective option for complex proximal subclavian artery aneurysms in patients with prior coronary bypass surgery.Clinical ImpactIn patients with a patent LIMA-LAD bypass, repairing a proximal left subclavian artery aneurysm comes down to one priority: myocardial perfusion must never be interrupted. This case offers a practical framework for avoiding the main pitfalls. Revascularization must come before exclusion, and every step should be planned to preserve coronary flow, from clamping to plug placement to endograft coverage. Following this sequence allows a complex repair to be performed safely with off-the-shelf devices.

items.title: Angiopoietin-2 in retinal vascular fibrosis: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications for diabetic retinopathy.
items.abstract: Retinal vascular fibrosis is a pathological hallmark of advanced diabetic retinopathy (DR), marking the transition from reversible vascular dysfunction to irreversible structural damage. Emerging evidence has established angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) as a crucial initiating factor in retinal vascular fibrosis. In the diabetic retina Ang-2 expression is persistently upregulated by hyperglycemia, hypoxia, and inflammation. Through dysregulating Ang-2/Tie signaling, Ang-2 disrupts endothelial junctional proteins, promotes vascular leakage and inflammation, and induces pericyte loss, collectively leading to endothelial destabilization and microvascular abnormalities. A key mechanism underlying this fibrotic shift is endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), which drives extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation and vascular fibrosis. Ang-2 drives EndMT primarily by inducing transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) expression. Concurrently, within a chronic inflammatory microenvironment, M2-polarized macrophages secrete numerous pro-fibrotic mediators. In addition, upregulation of tissue inhibitors of metalloproteinases suppresses ECM degradation. From a therapeutic perspective, the Ang-2/Tie2 signaling has emerged as a pivotal regulatory node in vascular homeostasis and inflammatory modulation. Dual Ang-2/vascular endothelial growth factor inhibition with agents like faricimab has proven effective not only in reducing vascular leakage and neovascularization but also in curbing inflammation and halting fibrosis progression. Emerging Ang-2-targeted strategies, including long-acting fusion proteins, gene therapies, and nanoparticle-based delivery systems, aim to achieve sustained vascular stabilization and durable disease modification. We synthesize current insights into the pathogenic role of Ang-2 in DR, with a focus on its contribution to retinal vascular fibrosis and highlight recent advances in Ang-2-directed therapies. Collectively, these insights provide novel perspectives for the development of anti-retinal vascular fibrosis therapies.

items.title: Preferential Conduction Along the Epicardial Ventricular Septum During Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Basal LV Summit: A Pitfall for Anatomical Ablation.

sections.objective: An anatomical ablation of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) originating from the left ventricular summit (LVS) is delivered from endocardial sites across the myocardium adjacent to the site of the VA origin with the guidance of transvenous epicardial mapping. Therefore, electrophysiological information obtained by transvenous epicardial mapping should be carefully interpreted. This study investigated ventricular activation patterns within the great cardiac vein (GCV) during idiopathic LVS VAs.
sections.methods: We studied 38 consecutive patients who underwent a successful endocardial ablation of idiopathic LVS VAs at the left ostial process, left coronary sinus, and commissure between the left and right coronary cusps.
sections.results: Twenty-nine patients exhibited a radial activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded around the junction between the GCV and anterior interventricular vein (AIVV). The remaining 9 patients exhibited a septal activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded within the AIVV, with the activation sequence being from the AIVV to GCV. The septal group mainly exhibited left bundle branch block pattern, whereas the radial group exhibited right bundle branch block pattern (P < 0.0001). The distance between the earliest ventricular activation site within the GCV or AIVV and the successful ablation site was significantly larger for LVS VAs with a septal activation pattern than those with a radial activation pattern.
sections.conclusion: During idiopathic basal LVS VAs, activation from those VA origins often preferentially conducted along the ventricular septum. It should be kept in mind that this unusual activation pattern may mislead the mapping and catheter ablation of LVS VAs.

items.title: Mortality and prognostic factors in invasive aspergillosis: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis.

sections.objective: Invasive aspergillosis remains a life-threatening infection, but robust real-world mortality estimates are scarce. We aimed to generate contemporary overall and subgroup-specific mortality estimates for invasive aspergillosis using individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis.
sections.methods: In this systematic review and IPD meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science for articles published between Jan 1, 2015, and Dec 31, 2024, that reported mortality of at least ten patients with invasive aspergillosis diagnosed using established criteria, with clearly defined and analysed follow-up periods. Corresponding authors were contacted to obtain IPD on demographics, underlying conditions, site of invasive aspergillosis, diagnostic certainty, and mortality. The primary outcome was overall all-cause mortality at 4, 6, 12, and 24 weeks, 1 year, and 2 years after invasive aspergillosis diagnosis. Secondary outcomes were intensive care unit (ICU) mortality and in-hospital mortality. One-stage IPD meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled mortality. This study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025621772).
sections.results: 16 020 articles were identified, of which 9686 articles were screened after removal of duplicates. Of the articles screened, 209 studies including 15 357 patients were eligible. IPD were obtained from 46 studies, comprising 3880 patients. Across IPD cohorts, patients were predominantly middle-aged and had pulmonary involvement, and probable invasive aspergillosis was the most common diagnostic certainty; classic immunocompromised host factors were common in the mortality-after-invasive aspergillosis-diagnosis cohort, whereas COVID-19 predominated in the ICU mortality cohort. Estimated overall mortality was 26·7% (95% CI 21·0-38·2) at 4 weeks, 32·0% (26·9-42·6) at 6 weeks, 41·7% (34·9-55·1) at 12 weeks, 48·5% (41·4-61·4) at 24 weeks, 53·8% (46·8-64·0) at 1 year, and 57·2% (49·7-68·3) at 2 years. ICU mortality was 57·1% (47·5-66·5) and in-hospital mortality was 46·7% (39·4-54·1). By underlying condition, estimated 4-week mortality was highest among patients with ICU admission (42·9%, 30·4-53·2). By site, estimated 4-week mortality was 27·2% (21·3-40·0) for pulmonary, 21·1% (15·1-28·9) for sinus, and 40·4% (35·0-54·5) for brain invasive aspergillosis. The overall pooled estimates yielded I2 values of 93·2% (92·0-94·3) for 4-week mortality, 89·5% (87·6-91·2) for in-hospital mortality, and 92·3% (90·8-93·5) for ICU mortality.
sections.conclusion: Mortality among patients with invasive aspergillosis remains high despite modern diagnostic and therapeutic advances. Greater vigilance, earlier diagnosis, and timely antifungal treatment are needed, particularly for patients with newly recognised host factors, including ICU admission and COVID-19.

items.title: Multimodal multitask deep learning for predicting tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence in gastric cancer: a multicentre development, validation, and testing study.

sections.objective: Peritoneal recurrence remains a common and fatal complication following curative gastric cancer surgery. Tertiary lymphoid structures are crucial indicators of immune response in cancer, and their maturation is associated with better prognosis and therapy outcomes. Evaluation of these structures could improve patient stratification for treatment of cancer but is hindered by the invasive and biased nature of histological methods. This study aimed to explore a non-invasive radiological method of assessment in patients with gastric cancer, using a novel multitask hybrid model to predict the presence and maturation status of tertiary lymphoid structures and peritoneal recurrence-free survival.
sections.methods: We developed CTransNet, a multitask hybrid model combining a convolutional neural network (ResNet50) and a Transformer model to predict tertiary lymphoid structure maturation and peritoneal recurrence-free survival in patients with gastric cancer. The study used retrospective data from eight Chinese cohorts of patients treated for gastric cancer at Nanfang Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, Yunnan Cancer Hospital, and Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine (one training cohort, two internal validation cohorts, three external validation cohorts, and two independent cohorts of patients treated with anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 inhibitors for at least two cycles). Patients were classified into three categories based on the presence and maturation of tertiary lymphoid structures (identified using haematoxylin-eosin and immunohistochemistry staining): TLS0 (absent tertiary lymphoid structures), TLS1 (primary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures without germinal centres), and TLS2 (secondary follicle-like tertiary lymphoid structures with germinal centres [ie, more mature structures]). Peritoneal recurrence was assessed using imaging (ultrasonography, CT, or PET-CT), clinical signs, or reoperation. We evaluated the accuracy of the multitask hybrid model in classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status using receiver operating characteristic analysis. Patients were stratified into risk groups using the median predicted score from the training cohort (high vs low), which was then applied to the validation cohorts. Survival outcomes (peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival) were analysed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox proportional hazards models. We also analysed the relationships between predicted scores and responses to chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
sections.results: Patients in the Chinese cohorts were recruited between Jan 1, 2005, and Feb 28, 2022. In the training cohort, for classifying patient-level tertiary lymphoid structure status, values for area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0·910 (95% CI 0·882-0·938) for TLS0, 0·925 (0·899-0·951) for TLS1, and 0·953 (0·933-0·974) for TLS2. For predicting peritoneal recurrence-free survival, the model achieved a concordance index of 0·654 (95% CI 0·620-0·688) in the training cohort. Across all cohorts, patients with low model scores had substantially higher 5-year peritoneal recurrence rates than those with high scores (eg, 66·69%, 95% CI 60·11-73·27 vs 26·28%, 20·05-32·51; p<0·0001 in the training cohort). Multivariate analysis confirmed risk stratification based on the multitask hybrid model score as an independent predictor of peritoneal recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival. Analysis of patients with stage II or stage III disease in the training cohort and internal and external validation cohorts showed that in those with low predicted scores versus high predicted scores, adjuvant chemotherapy was associated with improved disease-free survival and overall survival in patients with low scores but not those with high scores. In the immunotherapy cohorts, objective response rates were higher for patients with high predicted scores than for those with low predicted scores (54·5% vs 5·6%; p<0·0001 in immunotherapy cohort 1 and 53·1% vs 9·7%; p=0·0010 in immunotherapy cohort 2).
sections.conclusion: By accurately predicting tertiary lymphoid structure status, peritoneal recurrence, and survival, the multitask hybrid model shows strong potential as a non-invasive tool for personalised gastric cancer care. The model's potential to identify patients who might benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy and are more likely to respond to immunotherapy could help clinicians to optimise treatment strategies.

items.title: Closing the evidence gap: a life course and neurodiversity-informed participatory scoping review of healthy ageing randomised controlled trials in adults with developmental disabilities.
items.abstract: Adults aged 18 years and older with developmental disabilities experience disproportionate adverse health outcomes across the life course and shortened life expectancy. We conducted a participatory scoping review of randomised controlled trials of healthy ageing interventions for adults with developmental disabilities, informed by the WHO life course framework and neurodiversity principles. We searched Ovid MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection on June 25, 2024, and April 10, 2025, and charted study characteristics and framework alignment. We included 79 trials with 8221 participants. Although 77 (97%) of 79 studies addressed at least one functional ability, only 25 (32%) targeted life course transitions, 28 (35%) targeted multiple ecosystem levels, 22 (28%) used participatory approaches, and 20 (25%) used strengths-based approaches. Life course and neurodiversity principles were incompletely integrated into intervention research, indicating opportunities to address developmental transitions, multiple ecosystem levels, social and community participation, and strengths across the life course.

items.title: Host-microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues.
items.abstract: As a primary port of pathogen entry, the intestinal mucosa has developed a sophisticated set of defences to ward off infections. Investigating the human-specific intestinal barrier responses to pathogens is limited by the lack of models integrating the necessary architectural complexity with an autologous immune compartment1. Here we developed engineered barrier models of the human small intestine and colon combining a multilineage epithelium, mucus layer, accessible microbial compartment and autologous tissue-resident immune cells. These tissues recapitulate morphological and functional properties that are region specific and compare with those of the native organ. We use the model to characterize the human epithelial response to Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium at the single-cell level, uncovering the distinct gene regulatory networks that underpin luminal versus intracellular pathogen presence. Invaded epithelial cells initiate an IL-18 signalling axis that triggers cytotoxic T cell activation, resulting in epithelial shedding and barrier disruption. Overall, this work allows for the modular integration of epithelial, microbial and immune compartments, providing a versatile system for studying human intestinal physiology and pathologies.

items.title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands.
items.abstract: Islands account for a disproportionate share of global biodiversity1, yet insects, including invaluable pollinators such as bees2, remain underrepresented in island biogeography research3. Here we present a global checklist of island bees, recording 4,147 species across 305 islands. Although islands comprise only about 6% of the Earth's land area, they support around 20% of known global bee diversity, and 42% of insular species are endemic, making up around 8% of all known bee species. Island bee species richness peaks at mid-latitudes (at least in the Northern Hemisphere), mirroring continental trends4. Native richness increases with island area and declines with isolation, consistent with patterns in other taxa5. The strength of island species-area relationships varies among biomes and is steepest in Mediterranean-type systems, which also support disproportionately high bee richness relative to flowering plant diversity. The number of endemic species is highest on large tropical islands, reflecting extensive in situ diversification. Major centres of bee endemism include Madagascar, Malesia (the Greater Sundas and New Guinea) and the Hawaiian islands, where a single large radiation of Hylaeus (Nesoprosopis) dominates6. Among islands that are capable of supporting endemic species, endemism scales strongly with total richness. These findings highlight the need to integrate island bee diversity into global conservation planning and position bees as a model for understanding insect evolution and conservation on islands.

items.title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts.
items.abstract: Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and can profoundly influence individual fitness and population dynamics1,2. Although the ecological and social conditions that favour cannibalism have been well documented2, the molecular signals that trigger cannibalistic attacks have remained poorly understood. Here we show that in Locusta migratoria, guaiacol, a volatile compound with augmented release after injury, attracts gregarious nymphs and induces cannibalistic behaviour. Guaiacol is detected by olfactory receptors LmOR36 and LmOR34, and disruption of either receptor abolishes attraction, thereby impairing induction of cannibalism. Guaiacol is synthesized by haemolymph symbiont Enterobacter hormaechei. Injury promotes bacterial congregation at the wound site, leading to elevated guaiacol production through a clustered set of vanillic acid decarboxylase genes; deletion of this gene cluster abolishes guaiacol production and its behavioural effects. Notably, guaiacol initially functions as a beneficial signal after injury. Guaiacol activates immune-related pathways in wounded locusts, enhancing pathogen resistance and increasing survival following minor injury. However, when guaiacol emission exceeds a threshold determined by injury severity, it functions as an external cue that attracts cannibals. Cannibalistic locusts exploit this immune-related odour to locate severely injured conspecifics, gaining both nutritional resources and immune system benefits. Together, our findings identify a microbial-chemical mechanism that links immune defence with cannibalistic behaviour and provide potential molecular targets for manipulation of cannibalism-dependent population dynamics.

items.title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Alterations in metabolism, stress response, sleep, circadian rhythms and neuroendocrine processes are key features of ageing and neurodegeneration1,2. These fundamental processes are regulated by the hypothalamus, yet how its functionally distinct subregions and cell types change during human ageing and Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains largely unexplored. Here we present HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, including high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals and single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei from young participants, patients with AD and age-matched non-dementia control participants. We show that hypothalamic subregions governing metabolism, stress and circadian rhythms are particularly vulnerable, showing notable changes in both volumes and gene expression during ageing and AD. At the molecular level, machine learning models identified the inflammatory response and regulators of circadian rhythms as key cellular predictors of AD. These signatures were reflected in specific cell types: microglia transitioned to a pro-inflammatory state, whereas inhibitory neurons within sleep-regulating and circadian-regulating hypothalamic subregions showed the most profound transcriptional alterations, including disruptions in ligand-receptor interactions and G-protein-coupled receptor signalling. HypoAD provides a high-resolution volumetric map and a transcriptomic atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and AD, relating lifestyle and behavioural changes to the relevant volumetric and molecular pathways. In addition, HypoAD provides a framework to investigate hypothalamic dysfunction and establishes a roadmap for targeted interventions aimed at mitigating physiological disruptions to potentially slow disease progression.

items.title: Physical activity coaching and text messaging for adults with mobility limitations (ComeBACK): hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial.

sections.objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of a physical activity coaching intervention compared with text messaging intervention and waitlist control in adults with mobility limitations.
sections.methods: Three arm, pragmatic, superiority, hybrid type 1 effectiveness implementation randomised controlled trial. 512 community dwelling adults (≥18 years) who self-reported mobility limitations (difficulty or inability to walk 800 m, with or without a walking aid) but were still able to leave home without physical assistance from another person. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 allocation ratio to: a six month, multicomponent intervention including fortnightly physiotherapist delivered telephone coaching (coaching group, n=172); a six month, multicomponent intervention including regular unidirectional text messages (texting group, n=171); and no intervention for six months, followed by the six month text messaging intervention (waitlist control group, n=169). Participants and physiotherapists were unmasked to group allocation.
sections.results: Participants' mean age was 69 years (standard deviation (SD) 10 years) and 76% (n=388/511) were women. More than half (n=263/508, 51%) of participants reported multiple long term conditions as the main reason for their mobility limitation. At six months, mean daily steps were 931 higher (95% confidence interval 409 to 1452 steps; P=0.001) in the coaching group (mean 7256 (SD 3736) steps) compared with waitlist group (6526 (3003) steps); and 571 steps higher (58 to 1084, P=0.03) compared with the texting group (6529 (3029) steps). Mean daily steps in the texting group were 359 higher (-91 to 810, P=0.12) compared with the waitlist group, but this was not statistically significant. The number of adverse events was similar between groups (11/172 (6%) in the coaching group, 7/171 (4%) in the texting group, and 13/169 (8%) in the waitlist group) and none were serious.
sections.conclusion: A person centred coaching intervention produced modest increases in physical activity and was more effective than a less intensive texting intervention or no intervention among adults with mobility limitations.
sections.other: Health services and general communities across five Australian states, 19 December 2018 to 7 March 2023. The primary outcome was device measured mean daily steps at six months, analysed according to treatment allocation using all available data. Outcome assessors and data analysts were masked to group allocation.

items.title: Effect of intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide and sodium bicarbonate on spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women after induction of labour (SAINT): multicentre randomised placebo controlled factorial trial.

sections.objective: To determine whether intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, and their combination increase the rate of spontaneous vaginal birth in nulliparous women undergoing induction of labour.
sections.methods: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled, 2×2 factorial phase 3 trial (SAINT). Nulliparous women aged 18-50 years with a singleton live fetus in cephalic presentation at term with an indication for induction of labour. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to oral sodium bicarbonate (4×1 g per dose) plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide (20 mg per dose), oral sodium bicarbonate plus intravenous placebo, oral placebo plus intravenous hyoscine butylbromide, or double placebo. The investigational medicinal product was administered at the onset of active labour and repeated every four hours to a maximum of three doses.
sections.results: Between 4 January 2023 and 29 January 2025, 3094 nulliparous women were randomised, and 2963 comprised the full analysis set. Spontaneous vaginal birth occurred in 57% (422/741) in the bicarbonate plus hyoscine butylbromide arm, 61% (445/734) in the bicarbonate arm, 61% (449/741) in the hyoscine butylbromide arm, and 56% (422/747) in the double placebo arm. Marginal risk differences for spontaneous vaginal birth compared with double placebo were -0.2 (95% confidence interval -5.1 to 4.7; P=0.93) percentage points for combined treatment, 3.1 (-1.7 to 8.0; P=0.21) percentage points for bicarbonate, and 4.0 (-0.8 to 8.9; P=0.10) percentage points for hyoscine butylbromide. Serious adverse events were similar between groups, and no treatment related serious morbidity or deaths were observed.
sections.conclusion: No clear evidence was found that intrapartum hyoscine butylbromide, sodium bicarbonate, or their combination increased spontaneous vaginal birth compared with placebo. Although small beneficial effects cannot be excluded, the findings do not support routine intrapartum use of either agent to facilitate spontaneous vaginal birth after induction of labour.
sections.other: 11 Norwegian hospitals providing comprehensive obstetric care. Spontaneous vaginal birth (no instrumental or caesarean delivery).

items.title: Proteome- and phenome-wide studies identify circulating protein drivers of kidney diseases.

sections.objective: Proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (PWMR) provides a genetic framework to identify circulating proteins causally implicated in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and prioritize them for drug discovery. However, the diverse etiologies of CKD and clinical presentations make it difficult to translate proteomic findings into actionable targets. Here, we studied protein associations with longitudinal kidney outcomes, CKD subtypes, and phenome-wide traits to identify proteins that are causally relevant and pharmacologically actionable.
sections.methods: We performed a PWMR study using cis-pQTLs as genetic instruments for 2807 circulating proteins from four proteogenomic cohorts (ARIC, Fenland, deCODE, and UK Biobank) and tested their effects across four kidney outcomes (eGFR, incident CKD, incident kidney failure, annualized eGFR slope) in up to 464,631 of Million Veteran Program participants. Proteins meeting proteome-wide significance underwent sensitivity testing, Bayesian colocalization, and external replication in CKDGen Consortium information. The same instruments were re-tested against nine diagnosis code-defined CKD subtypes using genome wide association studies meta-analysis across the Million Veteran Program participants, UK Biobank, and FinnGen, and against 1020 phecodes to distinguish kidney-restricted from systemic effects. Druggability was evaluated using ChEMBL annotations layered onto high-confidence STRING protein-protein interaction networks.
sections.results: We identified 93 proteins with proteome-wide significance, and twelve remained robust across sensitivity testing (ANGPTL3, FAM213A, GCKR, GSTA1, IDI2, INHBA, INHBC, MANBA, MICB, MST1, NRG4, UMOD). Forty-seven proteins mapped to at least one of nine kidney disease subtypes, with distinct patterns across diabetic, hypertensive, and glomerular kidney diseases. Phenome-wide testing separated seven proteins with kidney-restricted associations from those with broader systemic effects. Thirty-four proteins were pharmacologic targets, nominating candidates such as IL-1 pathway blockade for diabetic kidney disease and ANGPTL3 inhibition for podocyte protection.
sections.conclusion: Our integrative PWMR framework resolves circulating protein targets across CKD etiologies, separates kidney-restricted from systemic effects, and delivers actionable targets that may accelerate therapeutic innovation for CKD. About one-third of the 93 proteins could be targeted with existing or investigational medications.

items.title: Characterization of the Urine Proteome Using the Olink Explore 3072 Platform.

sections.objective: Urinary proteins are valuable biomarkers for physiological processes and early detection/monitoring of kidney diseases. However, comprehensive quantification and characterization of the urine proteome using a high-throughput platform remains limited.
sections.methods: Using the affinity-based Olink Explore 3072 proteomics assay, we quantified 2868 proteins in urine samples from 1268 participants of the German Chronic Kidney Disease (GCKD) study.
sections.results: Protein detectability in urine, defined as the percentage of samples with measurements above the limit of detection, showed a bimodal distribution: 659 (23%) proteins had high (over 80%) and 1336 proteins (47%) had low (under 20%) detectability, with stable detectability across strata of albuminuria and kidney function. More than 95% of highly detectable proteins had previously been identified in urine by mass spectrometry. Highly detectable proteins were enriched for extracellular, exosomal, and cell surface localization, and for expression in hepatocytes, immune cells and kidney proximal tubule cells. Comparison with plasma detectability from the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project identified proteins of likely kidney origin, including LRP2 (megalin) and NPHS2 (podocin). In a multivariable adjusted model of 13 clinical variables, albuminuria and an individual's sex showed significant associations with 779 and 670 proteins, respectively. Specific chronic kidney disease etiologies showed associations with 105 proteins, although etiology explained only a small proportion of protein variance. Correlation analysis revealed biologically meaningful protein clusters reflecting shared cellular compartments, tissue of origin, and molecular interactions.
sections.conclusion: Large-scale urine proteomic profiling using a high-multiplex affinity-based platform captures biologically meaningful molecular variation associated with clinical variables and chronic kidney disease, providing a valuable resource for biomarker discovery and future targeted studies.

items.title: Comparative Early Outcomes of Total Transfemoral vs. Upper Extremity Access for Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) Implantation.

sections.objective: Early experience with the Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) device relied on routine upper extremity access (UEA), but total transfemoral approaches have emerged to minimise aortic arch manipulations and the risk of neurological complications. The aim of this study was to evaluate outcomes following total transfemoral access (TFA) vs. UEA for TAMBE implantation.
sections.methods: A retrospective review of consecutive patients undergoing TAMBE implantation at a single centre between April 2020 and January 2026 was performed. Patients were stratified by access strategy into TFA and UEA. The primary outcomes were thirty day mortality and major adverse events (MAEs).
sections.results: One hundred patients underwent TAMBE implantation during the study period, of whom 32 underwent TFA and 68 UEA. The majority of aneurysms treated were thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (61%), and 45% of patients had a prior endovascular intervention with no significant difference between groups (all p > .050). Mean operative time (232.8 ± 92.4 minutes vs. 250.8 ± 77.3 minutes; p = .18) and fluoroscopy time (59.2 ± 28.4 minutes vs. 48.3 ± 21.6 minutes; p = .066) were not statistically different between groups. Technical success was 91% in the TFA group compared with 99% in the UEA group (p = .095). Thirty day mortality (3% vs. 3%; p = 1.0) and MAEs (16% vs. 13%; p = .76) were not statistically different between TFA and UEA groups. Spinal cord ischaemia rates were 16% for the TFA group and 7% for the UEA group (p = .16), with most cases mild and resolved by discharge (80%). No stroke events occurred in either group. At 6 months, overall branch patency was 92% (78 of 85 branches from 22 patients), including 83% (15 of 18 branches from five patients) in the TFA group and 94% (63 of 67 branches from 17 patients) in the UEA group (p = .16).
sections.conclusion: In this single centre experience, total transfemoral TAMBE implantation was performed in selected patients, and no statistically significant differences were detected in thirty day mortality, MAEs, and technical success between access strategies. Larger studies are needed to determine whether clinically meaningful differences exist.

items.title: Revascularisation Outcomes in Symptomatic Elderly Nonagenarians with Peripheral Arterial Disease: The ROSEPAD International Registry.

sections.objective: Data regarding the outcomes of revascularisation for symptomatic peripheral arterial disease (PAD) in nonagenarians are scarce, limited by short follow up periods and confounded by the competing risk of death. This multicentre, retrospective analysis of nonagenarians who underwent invasive treatment for symptomatic PAD (Rutherford category 3 - 6) between December 2017 and December 2023 aimed to analyse the safety and efficacy, as well as short term and medium term revascularisation outcomes in selected nonagenarians with lower limb PAD.
sections.methods: The primary endpoint was amputation free survival (AFS). Overall survival (OS), amputation free time, and freedom from any re-intervention of the index limb were additionally analysed. The cumulative incidence of major amputation and re-intervention were also estimated, accounting for the competing risk of death.
sections.results: A total of 566 patients were included. The majority underwent endovascular (81.6%), followed by open (10.6%), and hybrid revascularisation (7.8%). At 36 months, AFS was 21.4%, freedom from amputation was 85.7%, OS was 23.7%, and freedom from re-intervention was 73.7%. Men and history of coronary artery disease were associated with reduced AFS (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06 - 1.76; and hazard ratio 1.54, 95% CI 1.2 - 1.99, respectively). Accounting for the competing risk of death, the cumulative incidence of major amputation was 7.3% (95% CI 5 - 9.7), 7.6% (95% CI 5.2 - 10), and 9.2% (95% CI 6.4 - 12), while the cumulative incidence of re-intervention was 14.6% (95% CI 11.4 - 17.9), 16.2% (95% CI 12.8 - 19.6), and 17.3% (95% CI 13.7 - 20.9), after 12, 24, and 36 months of follow up, respectively.
sections.conclusion: Lower limb revascularisation in selected nonagenarians with PAD was associated with a low cumulative incidence of major amputation and re-intervention. However, a high overall mortality was observed after three years of follow up.

items.title: Trends and Variation in Uveal Melanoma Management in the National Cancer Database, 2004-2023.
items.abstract: We evaluated presentation and management of uveal melanoma in the National Cancer Database (NCDB) from 2004-2023 with multivariable logistic regression. Enucleations decreased and globe-sparing radiation increased. Significant socioeconomic and geographic variation in treatment persisted.

items.title: Retinopathy of prematurity: causes, treatment and prevention.
items.abstract: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is initiated at preterm birth. Vascular growth in the immature retina, conditioned to low intrauterine oxygen levels, is disrupted by rapid increases in oxygen which suppress oxygen-regulated growth factors. Maternally sourced essential lipids (ω-3 and ω-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids) and insulin-like growth factor-1 are also lost. Later, maturing (but avascular) retina becomes hypoxic and nutrient starved, driving a growth factor surge often causing destructive neovascularization. Current treatments address late-stage neovascular ROP by suppressing elevated vascular endothelial growth factor levels. Recent clinical studies address the initiating events, lack of specific maternally sourced lipids and growth factors, hyperoxia-induced metabolic changes, which induce suppression of normal retinal vascularization and retinal neural maturation. Early enteral supplementation with ω-3 and ω-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids reduces risk of neovascularization. Timed topical corticosteroids during early ROP which alter metabolism to promote normal vessel growth, show great promise in preventing severe disease. Risk algorithms with near 100% sensitivity and high specificity can reduce the number of screening examinations. AI-augmented photography and ultrawide field optical coherence tomography may further refine prediction, diagnosis and treatment. This review synthesizes recent clinical paradigm shifts toward early disease prevention, highlighting how novel metabolic, pharmacological, and digital health strategies can prevent ROP-related vision loss.

items.title: Heat-related mortality attributable to human-induced climate change: findings from the 100 Million Brazilian Cohort.

sections.objective: Over recent decades, the fact that global population health is directly and indirectly influenced by climate change has become increasingly clear, although few studies have directly attributed deaths to anthropogenic climate forcing. The impact of extreme heat is a key health risk in Brazil and is known to vary among population groups, including by age, socioeconomic condition, ethnicity, and other factors. In this Article, we aimed to quantify the impact of human-induced climate change on heat-related mortality in vulnerable populations in Brazil from 2000 to 2018.
sections.methods: We used the 100 Million (100M) Brazilian Cohort to quantify the attributable number of heat-related deaths to human-induced climate change. By 2018, the 100M Cohort assembled approximately 132 million low-income individuals in Brazil. We applied relative risk estimates generated with a distributed lag nonlinear model to modelled surface temperatures from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 Detection and Attribution Model Intercomparison Project climate model ensemble. The number of heat-related deaths is quantified in each immediate geographical region under factual and counterfactual (without anthropogenic forcing) scenarios. We also applied the same strategy used on the Cohort to the whole population of Brazil, using data from the Brazilian Mortality Information System, to give an independent estimate of heat-related deaths attributable to climate change in Brazil.
sections.results: We can attribute 0·89°C (90% CI 0·62-1·16) of heating in Brazil throughout 2000-18, relative to a 1961-90 baseline, to human-induced climate change. The nationwide percentage of heat-related deaths attributable to climate change in the 100M Cohort was estimated to be 51·1% (95% CI 34·8-74·9), meaning that around 75 800 heat-related deaths (95% CI 20 151-170 529) occurred in the 100M Cohort, equivalent to 2·2% (95% CI 0·6-4·9) of total non-accidental deaths. We found that extreme heat exposure causes a greater proportion of climate-attributable heat deaths than moderate heat exposure in most of Brazil's immediate geographical regions. Lastly, using the same parameters applied for the 100M Cohort, 43·7% (95% CI 27·6-71·1) of heat-related deaths in the whole Brazilian population are estimated to be attributable to climate change, broadly consistent with the Cohort-based estimate.
sections.conclusion: The results show that large numbers of heat-related deaths in Brazil would not have occurred without human influence on the climate system. The findings from the 100M Cohort were corroborated by results from a similar analysis conducted in the general population. This work highlights the urgent need to implement heat-adaptation policies to protect the Brazilian population, particularly the most vulnerable groups, and the need for ambitious global action on climate change mitigation.

items.title: Progress towards the elimination of transmission of Trypanosoma brucei gambiense in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a 25-year spatiotemporal analysis of national surveillance data.

sections.objective: Gambiense human African trypanosomiasis is a neglected tropical disease caused by the parasite Trypanosoma brucei gambiense. Multiple epidemics over more than two centuries have started in known risk areas termed human African trypanosomiasis foci, with DR Congo having historically carried the highest burden of disease. Since the latest resurgence of the disease in the 1990s, annual case notifications have decreased by 98%. In view of the WHO target to eliminate T b gambiense transmission globally by 2030, we aimed to outline areas of DR Congo that require intervention, aimed either at the elimination of ongoing transmission or at post-elimination surveillance.
sections.methods: We conducted a spatiotemporal analysis of national surveillance data on gambiense human African trypanosomiasis from across DR Congo. Screening and diagnosis data from TrypElim and the WHO Atlas of human African trypanosomiasis, geolocated at the village level and covering the period from Jan 1, 2000, to Dec 31, 2024, were combined with population data from LandScan. We then used WHO methods to outline areas at low or greater risk (≥1 case per 100 000 population) and at moderate or greater risk (≥1 case per 10 000 population) of gambiense human African trypanosomiasis for the periods 2000-04, 2005-09, 2010-14, 2015-19, and 2020-24. We assessed trends in surface area at risk over the whole study period, combining these results with infection rate data to define human African trypanosomiasis foci and estimate populations recommended to be kept under post-elimination surveillance.
sections.results: We included data on 137 690 cases of gambiense human African trypanosomiasis identified in 12 090 unique locations. Marked decreases in the areas at risk were observed over the time period studied: the area at low or greater risk decreased from 586 508 km2 (bootstrap SE 5028) at its peak in 2005-09 to 185 216 km2 (4550) in 2020-24, a 67% reduction, and the area at moderate or greater risk decreased from 340 730 km2 (2409) in 2002-06 to 8406 km2 (1385) in 2020-24, a 97% reduction. We identified 15 distinct human African trypanosomiasis foci, three of which accounted for more than 80% (99 625 of 124 467) of reported cases. At the national level, we observed a substantial decrease in infection rate among people screened in active screening campaigns, from more than 60 cases per 10 000 population in 2000 to less than one case per 10 000 population in 2024, divided into three distinct periods: a steep decline in infection rate between 2000 and 2004 (average of 29·9% per year [95% CI 25·3 to 34·3]), no significant change between 2005 and 2010 (+1·4% [-5·0 to 8·2]), and a further decrease between 2011 and 2024 (23·5% [18·9 to 27·9]), with considerable variation at a subnational level across the 15 foci.
sections.conclusion: The gambiense human African trypanosomiasis epidemic in DR Congo is now concentrated within a few foci, and elimination of transmission appears to be within reach. In foci with active transmission, sustained interventions remain imperative. New approaches, such as the presumptive treatment of individuals with suspected infection, could pave the way to the elimination of transmission, after which post-elimination surveillance across foci that have historically been affected will be crucial.

items.title: Thelazia callipaeda: an emerging zoonotic eyeworm from Asia to Europe and North America.
items.abstract: Thelazia callipaeda is an emerging zoonotic nematode transmitted by lachryphagous fruit flies to mammalian hosts, including dogs, cats, wild carnivores, and humans, with wildlife reservoirs having a major role in transmission. Once restricted to Asia, the parasite has expanded across many animal species in Europe and, in the past 10 years, in some locations in North America, raising veterinary and public health concerns. Ecological modelling, molecular epidemiology, and entomological findings support ongoing geographical expansion, driven primarily by animal movement and the presence of competent hosts and vectors across regions. Human infections (ie, thelaziasis) primarily present with unilateral conjunctivitis and ocular irritation but can progress to severe ocular disease if left untreated. Increasing reports in domestic and wild animals from newly affected regions, such as the eastern coast of the USA and the Baltic region, highlight the need for integrated surveillance, clinical awareness, molecular monitoring, and coordinated control strategies to mitigate further spread and zoonotic risk. This Review summarises knowledge of the biology, vector ecology, epidemiology, genetic diversity, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of thelaziasis.

items.title: Bias and equity in large language model-based applications for health care: a scoping review.
items.abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) into health care presents both opportunities for innovation and risks of perpetuating existing biases and health disparities. Although these concerns are widely discussed, a systematic understanding of the research landscape regarding bias and equity in LLM-based applications for health care remains limited, and few discussions have translated into actionable mitigation strategies. We conducted a Scoping Review to systematically map this landscape and identify key trends and gaps. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus for English-language articles published from Jan 1, 2018, to March 10, 2026. Our analysis of the 201 included studies revealed a strong focus on specific medical contexts and demographic factors and a predominant reliance on proprietary models that constrain transparency in bias evaluation. A disconnect exists between bias detection and mitigation, and the potential of LLMs to promote health equity remains underexplored. To realise a more coherent integration of bias mitigation and health equity objectives in health-care LLM development, the field needs large-scale, endpoint-driven studies grounded in real-world clinical workflows. Furthermore, we advocate for standardised multidimensional bias evaluation frameworks developed with support from professional societies and lifecycle bias governance across both proprietary and open-weight models to guide the safe and equitable integration of LLMs into health care globally.

items.title: Health-care professionals' experiences of caring for older adults across Europe and beyond: a multinational, multilingual qualitative analysis of a cross-sectional survey.

sections.objective: Population ageing is increasing the demand for care of older people; however, the workforce involved in geriatric care remains under-resourced. Evidence on professional attitudes of people caring for older adults relies largely on structured questionnaires, single-profession samples, and high-income settings and rarely captures how professionals themselves describe this work. We aimed to describe how health-care professionals across Europe and beyond experience caring for older adults and identify patterns to inform education and workforce policies.
sections.methods: This was a cross-sectional qualitative analysis of free-text responses to an optional open-ended item ("Please describe your thoughts and feelings on caring for older people") within a multinational, multilingual online survey fielded by the Cooperation in Science and Technology (COST) Action 21122 PROmoting GeRiAtric Medicine in countries where it is still eMergING (PROGRAMMING) network. The survey was developed in English, translated into 24 languages, and disseminated online between Oct 9, 2023, and June 5, 2024. The survey was open to anyone whose work involved the care of older people. Participation was voluntary and anonymous. Gender was self-reported as man, woman, or prefer not to say; race and ethnicity data were not collected. Responses with fewer than three words were considered non-interpretable and excluded. Native speaker members of the author team coded responses in their original languages using inductive reflexive thematic content analysis, followed by integrative cross-thematic synthesis in English. Reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research guidelines.
sections.results: 2196 (40·1%) of 5474 professionals from 60 countries or territories provided analysable responses in 25 languages for the free-text item. Most (1733 [78·9%] of 2196) respondents were from Europe. 436 (19·8%) respondents were from western Asia-predominantly Türkiye (378 [17·2%] of 2196)-and 27 (1·2%) of 2196 were from elsewhere. By qualitatively analysing these responses, we identified seven broad themes that reflected the shared patterns and tensions of the professionals involved in geriatric care. One theme was identified as the overarching pattern within which the remaining six themes were positioned. Three of the remaining themes (themes 2, 4, and 7) described the individual experiences of the work, whereas themes 3, 5, and 6 described the systemic context of the work.
